### Browser test-harness fake-media launch flags (2026-09-09, story task #20)

- [ ] **The Chromium fake-media launch flags are encoded three times across two packages, with nothing tying the config copies together** (surfaced by @dry-reviewer at Gate 2 of `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-09-web-app-in-meeting-loopback/`; owner `client` + `infrastructure`). The pair `--use-fake-ui-for-media-stream` / `--use-fake-device-for-media-stream` appears in `packages/web-app/playwright.config.ts` (`use.launchOptions.args`), `packages/web-app/vitest.config.ts:31` and `packages/sdk-svelte/vitest.config.ts:32`. All three must hold the SAME value — a browser tier that loses them gets no synthesized capture and no auto-granted permission, which presents as a media test failing for a reason unrelated to its subject. **Pre-existing; not introduced by task #20**, which added only a fourth *prose* encoding in `docs/runbooks/client-dev-local.md` §Secure Context and Media Setup and correctly tied that one down (the prose cites `playwright.config.ts` by path, and `scripts/dev-web.test.sh` asserts flag parity between the two with a positive control on the extracted flag count).

  **Why the obvious collapse fails, checked rather than assumed.** The natural shared home is `@darktower/test-utils`, and it does not work: that package's `exports` resolve to `./dist/*` and it has a build step, so importing it at vitest/playwright **config-load** time is a cold-`dist` build-order failure in three packages; `packages/sdk-svelte` does not depend on it at all. This is the INDEX reachability test — a proposed shared home that the consumer cannot reach is not a home, and forcing it would replace one honest triplicate with an unanchored fourth copy plus a build-order hazard. A `.json`/`.ts` file at the workspace root imported by all three configs would be reachable, but that is a new root-level artifact and a cross-package decision, which is why this is filed rather than fixed in a client task's diff.

  **SCOPE BOUND — the runbook prose is NOT a fourth member of this set and must not be folded into any fix here** (@operations, 2026-09-09). `docs/runbooks/client-dev-local.md` §Secure Context and Media Setup names both flags verbatim because it is prose a human pastes into a Chrome command line, and prose can never consume a TS constant; it is also *required* to name them, and `crates/dt-guard/src/no_insecure_browser_flags.rs`'s module docs anticipate exactly that text. It is already mechanically tied to `packages/web-app/playwright.config.ts` by `scripts/dev-web.test.sh`'s `flag-parity-matches-playwright-config-*` assertions, which carry a positive control on the extracted flag count so the parity check cannot pass vacuously when a reflow moves the launch line out of the extracted body. **That is the right control for the prose-to-config link and it already exists** — so a shared constant introduced for the three configs covers three sites, not four, and anyone extending it to the runbook has misread this entry.

  **Instrument, if picked up**: either a reachable shared const (workspace-root module, imported by all three configs) or a guard asserting the three config sites agree — following `scripts/dev-web.test.sh`'s flag-parity assertion, which already solves the prose-vs-config half of the same problem and is the natural place to extend. **Do NOT** solve it by adding an allowlist entry to `crates/dt-guard/src/no_insecure_browser_flags.rs`: these flags pass that guard on **vocabulary non-membership**, deliberately, and its own module docs record that an allowlist entry here would go on to mask a real cert-bypass setting added to the same file later. Low urgency — the three copies agree today and a divergence fails loudly in the affected tier rather than silently.

### From DRY Reviewer — story task #22 (2026-09-09)

Filed by @dry-reviewer at Gate 3 of `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-09-media-dashboards-and-catalogs/` as ADR-0019 extraction opportunities. Both are **pre-existing and were not introduced by task #22**; neither entered fix-or-defer.

- [ ] **The four Rust service jobs are encoded three times inside `crates/env-tests/`, in three different shapes** (owner `test` + `observability`). `crates/env-tests/src/fixtures/metric_hygiene.rs:SERVICE_JOBS` (a `&[&str]` slice), `crates/env-tests/tests/32_media_metric_hygiene.rs:JOBS` (a `|`-alternation string built for a PromQL `job=~` selector), and `crates/env-tests/tests/30_observability.rs:EXPECTED_SERVICES` (`&[(&str, &str)]` job→metric-prefix tuples). All three name the same four jobs and must agree: a service added to the fleet and missed in any one copy silently narrows whichever control reads it, and narrowing is invisible — the affected assertion keeps passing over a smaller set. Task #22 correctly derived its media-pair selector from `EXPECTED_SERVICES` rather than adding a fourth home.

  **The three are not one value in three encodings — they carry different payloads**, which is why this is a scoped collapse rather than a delete-two-of-three. `EXPECTED_SERVICES` pairs each job with its metric prefix (`ac_`, `gc_`, …), which the other two neither have nor need; `JOBS` is a regex alternation consumed inside a PromQL string, not a Rust collection. **Only the MEMBERSHIP question must agree.** A single `&[&str]` home with `SERVICE_JOBS.join("|")` at the selector site, prefixes kept beside their one consumer, collapses membership while leaving the payloads where they are used.

  **Reachability is satisfied, which is what makes this a genuine candidate** rather than a deliberate boundary: all three sites are inside `crates/env-tests/`, so the proposed home can be imported by every consumer (contrast the entries above where the collapse fails the INDEX reachability test). Filed rather than fixed because it edits a shared fixture with consumers in two test binaries, and task #22 touched only one of them.

  **SCOPE BOUND — the `key_custody` and `MediaDropReason` literals in `30_observability.rs` are NOT members of this set and must not be swept into any fix here.** They are deliberate restatements: an env-test's subject is the deployed artifact, and a test importing the emitter's constant agrees with the emitter no matter what the emitter becomes. Their rationale is recorded at the constants themselves and includes an explicit warning against "simplifying" them into imports. Anyone collapsing the job set who also collapses those has misread this entry.

- [ ] **`mh_grpc_requests_total`'s retired `method` values are restated in prose on `mh-overview.json` panel 28** (owner `media-handler`). The description states that `register_meeting` is the only RPC on `MediaHandlerService` and that `register`, `route_media` and `stream_telemetry` "were retired … and can never appear". **Accurate today, and deliberately written** — it tells an operator why those series will never appear. It is filed only because it is a second home for a fact whose first home is `docs/observability/metrics/mh-service.md`, and no guard compares them: `dt-guard application-metrics` and `dashboard-panels` match metric **names**, never label keys or values. If `MediaHandlerService` ever gains a second RPC, this sentence becomes false with nothing to catch it. **Low severity, listed as a locatable instance** of the class filed under §Observability Debt → *"Restated label rosters and restated counts have no guard, and no sweep enforcement"*; close it with that class, not on its own.

## Port Constant Scattering (Kind / K8s / Env-Tests)

- [ ] **MC/MH port constants duplicated across 6+ files with no single source of truth**: Host ports (4433, 4434, 4435, 4436), NodePorts (30433, 30434, 30435, 30436), and observability ports (9090/30090, 3000/30030, 3100/30080) are hardcoded independently in `infra/kind/kind-config.yaml`, `infra/services/{mc,mh}-service/service.yaml` (NodePort values), `infra/services/{mc,mh}-service/{mc,mh}-{0,1}-configmap.yaml` (advertise addresses), `infra/services/{mc,mh}-service/configmap.yaml` (bind addresses), `infra/docker/{mc,mh}-service/Dockerfile` (EXPOSE + bind defaults), `infra/kind/scripts/setup.sh` (print output), and `crates/env-tests/src/cluster.rs` (ClusterPorts::default). Changing a port in one file without updating all others causes silent breakage. Consider extracting port assignments to a shared config (e.g., `ports.env` sourced by setup.sh, referenced by Kustomize configMapGenerator). The new `kind-config.yaml.tmpl` (ADR-0030) correctly uses envsubst placeholders for its hostPorts, avoiding this issue for devloop clusters. **Update (2026-09-02, story task #9 / devloop `2026-09-02-mh-transport-parameter-manifests`, @dry-reviewer's condition on an accepted deferral)**: the closing "low priority — manual workflow only" in the original text is now FALSE and has been struck. Three of the scattered MH values are bind addresses a running service reads, and `crates/mh-service/src/config.rs:22,25,28` holds byte-identical duplicate strings (`DEFAULT_GRPC_BIND_ADDRESS`, `DEFAULT_HEALTH_BIND_ADDRESS`, `DEFAULT_WEBTRANSPORT_BIND_ADDRESS`) of all three ConfigMap values. **Fresh MH inventory**: `4434` at 9 sites, `8083` at 10, `50053` at 9 — ~28 across `configmap.yaml`, `mh-0-configmap.yaml`, both deployments (containerPort, both probes, and `MH_GRPC_ADVERTISE_ADDRESS`'s embedded `"grpc://$(POD_IP):50053"`), `service.yaml` and `network-policy.yaml`; `service.yaml:32,56` and `network-policy.yaml:30` also restate ports in **prose comments**, which a derivation would leave stale. **No port guard exists** (`dt-guard` has no `containerPort` logic). **Why kustomize `replacements:` alone cannot close this** (established while landing the `MH_TERMINATION_GRACE_SECONDS` derivation): (a) `infra/kind/scripts/setup.sh:1211-1217` **rewrites** `mh-{0,1}-config`'s `MH_WEBTRANSPORT_ADVERTISE_ADDRESS` with `kubectl patch` *after* `apply -k`, so no build-time replacement can ever guard it; (b) deriving `containerPort` from a ConfigMap needs `options.delimiter`, which yields a **string**, and `containerPort` is int32 — so the chain must run source=containerPort → target=ConfigMap, the opposite of the intuitive direction; (c) the shared `mh-service-config` has no single instance to source from, unlike the grace-period case whose source and target sit inside one object. A partial derivation covering only the kustomize-reachable subset would manufacture false assurance. **Named follow-up, owner infrastructure**: *Port SSoT for per-instance services* — **step 1 is a compare-only `dt-guard` drift check** across the five MH manifest files plus `config.rs` (cheap, zero deploy blast radius, and the only half that can reach the `setup.sh` patch); step 2 designates each deployment's `containerPort` as canonical and derives ConfigMap bind addresses, Service `port`/`targetPort`, NetworkPolicy ports and both probe ports, chaining mh-0→mh-1 for the shared-ConfigMap source question; then MC, then GC/AC. Revisit the single-file `replacements:` idiom at ~6 entries. **Update (R-37, task #4)**: the AC/GC host-side E2E ports are now also scattered — static host ports 8443 (AC) / 8444 (GC) and NodePort containerPorts 30082 (AC) / 30180 (GC) are hardcoded in `infra/kind/kind-config.yaml` (new AC/GC `extraPortMappings`), `infra/kind/kind-config.yaml.tmpl` (30082/30180 under `${HOST_PORT_*}`), `infra/kubernetes/overlays/kind/services/{ac,gc}-service/nodeport.yaml`, `infra/kind/scripts/setup.sh` (`print_access_info`), and the committed client config (`packages/web-app/vite.config.ts` proxy targets `127.0.0.1:8443/8444`). Same single-source-of-truth opportunity as MC/MH above.

- [ ] **AC and GC encode `DATABASE_URL` in two independently-authored places with nothing asserting they agree (2026-08-14)**: Surfaced during review of devloop `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-08-14-gc-meeting-refusal-causes/main.md` (owner @database; **pre-existing, not introduced by that diff**). GC's connection string is a literal in `infra/services/gc-service/secret.yaml:14` (`postgresql://…postgres.dark-tower.svc.cluster.local:5432/dark_tower`); AC's arrives via `secretKeyRef` → `ac-service-secrets` (`infra/services/ac-service/statefulset.yaml:42-46`), a Secret not tracked in this repo. Both services read the **same** `organizations` table, defined once in `migrations/20250118000001_initial_schema.sql:5` — so this is one logical database with two authored values and no guard on their agreement (CLAUDE.md: "when two places encode the same value, they will drift").

  **Why it matters concretely**: if the two ever diverge, AC mints a validly-signed token naming an org row GC cannot see, and GC returns `500 ORGANIZATION_NOT_PROVISIONED` — the referential-integrity branch added by R-6. That branch is otherwise reachable only by out-of-band mutation, so a config divergence would present as data corruption. The failure is silent until a meeting-create request happens to exercise it.

  **Already operator-visible, which is why this is worth closing rather than just knowing**: `docs/runbooks/gc-deployment.md` now instructs a deploy-time operator to check whether GC and AC point at the same database *before* reaching for a rollback. That turns an unguarded config invariant into a manual triage step performed under time pressure — the runbook is the compensating control, not the fix.

  **Shape of the fix**: derive both from one source (a shared Secret, or a Kustomize `configMapGenerator`/`secretGenerator` consumed by both services) rather than authoring them separately; failing that, a validation-pipeline check asserting the two resolve equal. Same defect class as the port scattering above. Owner: infrastructure + database. Defer trigger: next infra touch to either service's Secret wiring, or any report of `org_not_provisioned` in a non-test environment.

- [ ] **Auto rollout-restart on cert-secret recreate in `setup.sh`**: `scripts/generate-dev-certs.sh` uses 14-day WebTransport leaf validity (Chrome's `serverCertificateHashes` cap), so expiry is a routine dev event. On an already-running cluster, `setup.sh` regenerating an expiring leaf + recreating the `mc/mh-service-tls` Secret does NOT restart the pods serving the old leaf (`kubectl apply` is a no-op on unchanged Deployment specs). **The remaining work is the automation only**: add the rollout-restart to `setup.sh`'s secret-recreate path. Deliberately deferred out of R-36 — it's a behavior change firing on ALL runs including fresh setup, so it carries regression surface and needs its own test cycle. The operator-facing manual sequence is **documented** in `docs/runbooks/client-dev-local.md` §5 F7 and printed by `generate-dev-certs.sh`'s expiry hint; do not restate it here. Owner: operations / infrastructure. Low priority — dev-loop only. (Was mis-owned to "R-49 dev runbook (task #20)"; task #20 produced prose and discharged the documentation half only — a runbook cannot deliver a `setup.sh` behavior change. Re-owned 2026-07-29 by task #20.)

- [ ] **A dead STREAM and a dead CONNECTION are indistinguishable in `wtransport`'s error values — task 16's forward path needs that distinction and can only get it from local state (owner: media-handler, story task 16; discovered 2026-09-02 at `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-02-mh-transport-config-and-drain/`, @test concurring)**: `crates/mh-service/src/transport/mod.rs` states as a **contract** that `write_all` after a successful `finish` returns `TransportError::StreamClosed`, justified by quinn returning the stream-scoped `WriteError::ClosedStream`. quinn does — but **`wtransport` folds it away**: `wtransport-0.7.2/src/driver/streams/mod.rs:564-568` maps `quinn::WriteError::ClosedStream` and `ConnectionLost(_)` **both** to `StreamWriteError::NotConnected`, whose own docstring reads "Connection has been dropped". By the time an error reaches MH the two cases are one value, and **no mapping choice recovers information that has already been discarded**. (`wtransport` defines a `Closed` variant meaning "already finished or reset locally", but its `From<quinn::WriteError>` never produces it on this path.)
  **This was found by test, not by reading**, on the first run of `crates/mh-service/tests/transport_real_impl.rs` — which exists because, before it, nothing in the tree opened a unidirectional stream or sent a datagram over the real transport, so every `finish` assertion in the workspace ran against the deterministic double. Task 16's forward-path tests will trust that double at exactly this point.
  **The fix task #12 landed is a pattern, not a general solution**: `WtSendStream` carries a `finished: bool`, latched only when `finish()` returns `Ok`, checked *before* touching the transport. It works because **MH is the party that caused the transition** and therefore holds what the vendor dropped. Mapping `NotConnected -> StreamClosed` instead was rejected as inverting the damage — a genuinely lost connection would report as a dead stream and the forward path would hold it open indefinitely, which is strictly worse since the stream case is recoverable and the connection case is not.
  **The constraint on task 16**: a dead stream is a **per-subscriber** problem and a dead connection is a **per-participant** one, with different remediations — so the distinction is load-bearing for the forward path, not cosmetic. Any transition MH does **not** cause is unrecoverable: a peer-initiated stream reset arriving as `NotConnected` is indistinguishable from connection loss, and task 16 must either generalise the local-state pattern to every case it can, or design explicitly for the cases where it cannot. Do not read the `finished` flag as having closed this.

- [ ] **`NOMINAL_AUDIO_BITRATE_BPS` must be re-confirmed against the SDK encoder config when story task 19 lands — and the likely reader will be holding the word "ceiling" (owner: media-handler + client, story task 19; filed 2026-09-02 at `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-02-mh-transport-config-and-drain/`)**: `crates/mh-service/src/config.rs::NOMINAL_AUDIO_BITRATE_BPS` is 32 kbps — the **floor** of the 32-48 kbps VBR range story task 19 specifies. There is no SDK encoder config in the tree yet, so the cross-reference the task text asks for cannot be performed; when task 19 lands, check that the shipped encoder's configured **floor** is still at or above 32 kbps.  **AMENDED 2026-09-08 (story task 19) — THE CROSS-REFERENCE WAS PERFORMED AND IT DOES NOT HOLD. Owner now media-handler + client + operations; NOT closed.** The SDK encoder now exists: `packages/sdk-core/src/config/clientConfig.ts` sets `media.audio.defaultBitrateBps = 32000` with `bitrateMode: 'variable'`, and MC's directed `EncodingParameters.max_bitrate_bps` overrides it when present. **The reader holding the word 'ceiling' was right to worry, and the finding is the reverse of the one this entry anticipated.** Under VBR, 32 kbps is a TARGET/CEILING and **not a floor**: there is no configurable Opus minimum, so quiet input produces frames below MH's nominal size. `mh-service` sizes `NOMINAL_AUDIO_FRAME_BYTES` at `SUPPORTED_AUDIO_BITRATE_FLOOR_BPS = 32000` — the smallest frame it expects — so its operator-facing 'N frames = M ms' datagram-buffer budget is an AVERAGE-CASE sizing, not the worst case its doc comment claims ('holds at most what it says at every bitrate in the range'). **SIZED, so this is a bounded finding rather than an alarming one (@operations).** Per-frame overhead floors real frame size: publisher region + 50-byte wrapped-key block + 64-byte signature is ~156 B irreducible, against a ~236 B nominal. So the buffer holds at most ~48 frames ≈ **970 ms** against a documented 640 ms — a real ~1.5x UNDERSTATEMENT of the operator-facing latency ceiling, bounded, not unbounded. The 64-byte signature ADR-0036 §3 calls expensive is what caps the error. **THE HAZARD IS ONE-DIRECTIONAL**: frames LARGER than nominal make the budget conservative (fewer held, less latency) and are safe. Only the small-frame side breaks the ceiling. **MH's compile-time pin is the 'accidentally correct' case**: it encodes the right PRINCIPLE (size at the smallest frame) while guarding a constant that is not the smallest REAL frame under VBR, so it will keep passing. A green pin here is not evidence the relation is checked. **NOT fixed client-side**: switching to CBR would make the constant true and contradicts the task text (which requires variable bitrate with a configured ceiling), and it would be fixing the wrong end. Handed to @media-handler.
  **The specific way this will be got wrong, recorded because it was got wrong twice inside one review gate** — by the implementer, the DRY reviewer, and the Lead independently, each having read the governing ADR row. `datagram_send_buffer_size` is a **latency ceiling, not a capacity guarantee**: ADR-0036 §1's complaint about quinn's 1 MiB default is that it holds *too much* ("~93 seconds of queued audio ... a realtime path must prefer loss to unbounded latency"). Frames held equals `buffer_bytes / actual_frame_bytes`, so the worst case is the **smallest** frame, i.e. the **lowest** bitrate. Sizing at the range ceiling (48 kbps) makes a 32-frame budget hold **37** frames (~740 ms) at 32 kbps traffic — over the intended bound — while sizing at the floor holds at most 32 at every bitrate in the range. Whoever lands the encoder config arrives holding the word "ceiling" and is the single most likely person to adjust this constant upward; that is the mistake to prevent.
  A compile-time pin (`NOMINAL_AUDIO_BITRATE_BPS <= SUPPORTED_AUDIO_BITRATE_FLOOR_BPS`) and a held-frames unit test both fail if it is re-sized at the ceiling, so the edit breaks the build rather than shipping. **Deliberately NOT an `ANCHOR (DRY):`** — MH and the SDK do not hold one value, they stand in an inequality, so an anchor would claim a lock that cannot be checked. Note an anchor asserting a shared `32` would currently look *accidentally correct* while encoding the wrong relation, which is the most durable way for a false single-source-of-truth to survive review.

- [ ] **`infra/services/mh-service/configmap.yaml:174` states a per-connection ceiling that two arithmetic defects make wrong; the Rust docstring now supersedes it (owner: @infrastructure; filed 2026-09-02 at `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-02-mh-transport-config-and-drain/` by @team-lead ruling)**: that comment predicts task #12's declared receive side drops MH's per-connection adversarial receive ceiling to "~263 KB". Two independent defects, **pointing in opposite directions** — recorded separately rather than netted, or the next reader inherits a number that is right by coincidence: (i) `stream_receive_window` is **double-counted**, when it is bounded *by* the connection receive window rather than additive to it; (ii) quinn's `crypto_buffer_size` (16 KiB, undeclared, left inherited) is **omitted**. With the constants task #12 landed the ceiling is **~264 KB**, or **~281 KB** counting the crypto buffer.
  **Deliberately not fixed in task #12's diff**, by @team-lead ruling with @security and @operations concurring: the comment's *conclusion* — that `500 x per-connection` is roughly 13% of the pod's 1 Gi limit — survives both figures (~132 MB / ~140 MB), the figure is tilde-qualified, and forcing an @infrastructure co-sign onto that commit to move a number by 7% is not a good trade. The authoritative arithmetic lives in `crates/mh-service/src/config.rs::CONNECTION_RECEIVE_WINDOW_BYTES`, whose docstring says explicitly that it **supersedes** the ConfigMap comment — stated rather than left implicit, because two numbers differing with no declared precedence invite a future reader to reconcile them by editing the Rust *down* to the stale prose. Fix here is one comment edit whenever @infrastructure next opens that file.

- [ ] **`MH_MAX_CONNECTIONS` is a chosen bound but not a memory-derived one — MH's connection-level QUIC receive flow control is undeclared (2026-09-02, story task #9)**: task #9 set `MH_MAX_CONNECTIONS: "500"` in `infra/services/mh-service/configmap.yaml`, a 20x reduction from the unchosen `DEFAULT_MAX_CONNECTIONS = 10_000` (`crates/mh-service/src/config.rs`, the `DEFAULT_MAX_CONNECTIONS` const) that no manifest supplied. It is sized against expected peak, **not** against the pod's memory limit, and the arithmetic does not close: quinn-proto 0.11.17 leaves `receive_window = VarInt::MAX` (unbounded — the dominant term), `stream_receive_window = 1.25 MB` and `datagram_receive_buffer_size = 1.25 MB`, giving a per-connection adversarial receive ceiling of **~206 MB against a 1 Gi limit** — roughly five hostile connections, not 500. Two amplifiers: ADR-0036's Context records that MH has **no `accept_uni` loop** today, so incoming stream data is never read and the windows fill and stay filled (the worst case is the *ordinary* case, not a tail); and **OOMKill is SIGKILL**, which bypasses `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` entirely, so the drain window task #9 derived is **void under exactly the adversarial condition where it would matter most**. **Lowering the number is not the fix** — at 100 connections it is still ~20 GB of worst-case credit; no usable value closes while `receive_window` is unbounded, so a reduction would be a false mitigation that looks more careful while fixing nothing. **Not fixable at the manifest surface**: a hand-typed receive-window ConfigMap key would be a second encoding of a budget whose real source is `resources.limits.memory` in the same file — the exact R-21 defect task #9 existed to remove — and it would be structurally invisible to `dt-guard env-config`, whose check 1 keys off `ConfigError::MissingEnvVar` and whose check 3 resolves `configMapKeyRef` from the deployment manifests, never from Rust. **Fix**: task #12 declares the receive side as named Rust constants (`receive_window`, `stream_receive_window`, and `datagram_receive_buffer_size` — the last its OWN constant, deliberately NOT derived from `MH_DATAGRAM_BUFFER_AUDIO_FRAMES`, since that quinn field also feeds the advertised `max_datagram_frame_size` and the two directions have opposing sizing pressures). That drops the per-connection ceiling to ~263 KB and makes 500 genuinely memory-derived (~132 MB, ~13% of 1 Gi). Owner: **media-handler (task #12)**; @operations directed this entry and @security set it as a Gate-1 condition; filed by infrastructure so one pen owns it — amend in place rather than opening a second entry. Defer trigger: task #12, or any change to `resources.limits.memory` in `mh-{0,1}-deployment.yaml`. **RUST-CONSTANT HALF DISCHARGED 2026-09-02 by task #12** (`docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-02-mh-transport-config-and-drain/`). Landed in `crates/mh-service/src/config.rs` and applied in `webtransport/server.rs::build_transport_config`: `CONNECTION_RECEIVE_WINDOW_BYTES = 256 KiB`, `STREAM_RECEIVE_WINDOW_BYTES = 64 KiB`, `DATAGRAM_RECEIVE_BUFFER_BYTES = 2 KiB` (its own constant, not derived from the send-side frame budget, and pinned by a compile-time floor assertion so it cannot be shrunk below the largest legitimate audio datagram). **TWO CORRECTIONS to the arithmetic above, which is why the landed figure is not the ~263 KB this entry predicted** — they point in opposite directions and are stated separately rather than netted, so that whoever revisits memory headroom does not inherit a number that is right by coincidence: (i) `stream_receive_window` was **double-counted** — it is bounded *by* the connection receive window, not additive to it, so the connection window is the only stream-side term; (ii) quinn's `crypto_buffer_size` (16 KiB, undeclared and left inherited) was **omitted** from the ceiling. Corrected per-connection ceiling: **~264 KB**, or **~281 KB** counting the crypto buffer — so `500 x per-connection` is ~132 MB (~13%) or ~140 MB (~13.7%) of the 1 Gi limit. **The conclusion this entry drew is unchanged**, which is why `infra/services/mh-service/configmap.yaml:174`'s tilde-qualified "~263 KB" was deliberately left unedited (@team-lead ruling: not worth an @infrastructure co-sign). The authoritative arithmetic now lives in the `CONNECTION_RECEIVE_WINDOW_BYTES` docstring, which states that it **supersedes** that ConfigMap comment. Sibling entry filed below for @infrastructure to sync the comment if they wish. **STILL OPEN, AND NOT DISCHARGED BY TASK #12: the observability addendum below** — the downward-API `resourceFieldRef: limits.memory` startup validation. @security explicitly did **not** require it at task #12's Gate 1, calling it task-sized (a sixth required var) and its own devloop. It remains unowned work and this entry must not be closed until it lands. **Observability addendum (@observability, task #9 Gate 3; placed by @operations to avoid a second entry):** once #12 lands, `500 x ~263 KB ~= 132 MB` against 1 Gi is a **statically-computed premise, not a derived one**. Nothing connects it to `resources.limits.memory`, so lowering that limit silently invalidates the arithmetic with no signal — the failure is a return to OOMKill-as-only-indicator, and it would arrive through an unrelated resource-tuning change that no reviewer would connect to connection admission. Drift-free shape: downward-API `resourceFieldRef: {resource: limits.memory}` feeding a #12 startup validation, so the premise is checked against the actual limit at boot rather than assumed. Task-sized (a sixth required var); flagged rather than folded in. **@operations condition on that shape**: it converts a silent OOMKill into a startup refusal, which is the right trade (loud and at deploy time, not at 3am under load) *only if* the refusal names both numbers and the remedy — the computed requirement, the observed limit, and which of the two to change. A bare `ConfigError` here reproduces the sentinel's failure mode: correct, fail-closed, and undiagnosable at the moment of use.

## Env-Test Resilience & Runbook Validation

- [ ] **`test_all_services_have_logs_in_loki` (`30_observability.rs:116`) hard-asserts Loki readiness with NO retry** (surfaced 2026-06-26 by task #56's first live Layer-7 run). The test does `assert!(cluster.is_loki_available().await, …)` (a single HTTP `GET /ready`) at test start; if Loki isn't warm yet — which it often isn't in the seconds right after a cluster bring-up — the test fails cold even though Loki comes up moments later (verified: a re-run with Loki warm passes). The crate already HAS `src/eventual.rs::assert_eventually` + `ConsistencyCategory::LogAggregation` (45s budget) — the body of this test uses it, but the upfront availability gate doesn't. Fix (either, @observability to decide at pickup): **(a) RETRY** — wrap the `is_loki_available()` gate in `assert_eventually(ConsistencyCategory::LogAggregation, …)` so it tolerates warmup (makes a cold-but-coming Loki GREEN); **(b) CONDITIONAL-SKIP** — skip `test_all_services_have_logs_in_loki` when `is_loki_available()` is false/None, honoring the crate's declared optional-Loki auto-skip intent (makes a genuinely-ABSENT Loki a clean SKIP, not a FAIL). (a) and (b) are complementary: (a) fixes the cold-start flake, (b) covers genuine absence; both together make absent-Loki non-failing. This is the ONLY thing that makes absent-Loki not a loud Phase-2 FAIL — neither task #56's Phase-1e soft-poll nor any classifier can (a classifier would reopen reverse-masking; ruling #3). Owner: env-tests / observability (@observability co-owns per task #56 Gate-1). Out of task #56's scope (that task fills the pipeline wiring, not the env-tests crate); task #56's Layer 7 correctly surfaced this as a loud `STATUS=FAIL`, no masking. Defer trigger: the next env-tests / observability touch, or a recurring cold-start flake in Layer 7. (Compensating control: task #56 may add an observability-endpoint readiness poll to layer7.sh Phase-1e — see that devloop's §Accepted Deferrals — which would convert this from a Phase-2 test flake into a Phase-1 wait.)
- [x] **Counter-delta baseline capture not robust to stale-series inflation across a pod rollout** (surfaced 2026-08-05, task #19 Gate-2 L7 attempt-2: `26_mh_quic.rs::test_mc_media_connection_update_increments_participant_mh_status_metric` flaked with "did not increase above baseline 5 within 60s (last observed: 1)" — full diagnosis in `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-08-04-e2e-negative-specs-pipeline/main.md` §Issues Encountered). Mechanism: the `sum(...)` instant-vector baseline is captured while old-pod series are still inside Prometheus's staleness window (Layer-7 Phase-1c `rebuild-all` still draining), those series expire mid-assertion, and the fresh pods' counters can never exceed the inflated baseline → false-negative 60s timeout (loud, never a false pass). Affects BOTH counter-delta helper families: the Rust ones in `crates/env-tests/tests/26_mh_quic.rs` (`assert_participant_mh_status_increases_past`, `mh_notification` twins) and the deliberate TS mirrors in `packages/web-app/e2e/mcMetrics.ts` (`pollUntilSumAbove` consumers; header there carries the matching caveat). The concrete browser-suite exposure is the Layer-7 RETRY path (@test, task #19 review): attempt N's spec increments the counter on the then-current MC pod; attempt N+1's Phase-1c rebuild rolls the pods; the retry's baseline read can include the old pod's soon-to-expire series — a guaranteed 60s timeout on exactly the attempt that burns the final budget. Fix shapes to evaluate at pickup: settle-wait until the target set matches current pods, or a per-current-pod query (`sum by` over live instances), applied consistently to both languages. Owner: env-tests / observability (+ test for the mcMetrics.ts mirror). Defer trigger: next env-tests crate touch or a recurring L7 counter-delta flake. **Occurrence 2 — 2026-08-28, defer trigger MET** (`docs/devloop-outputs/2026-08-28-env-config-guard-per-instance-workloads/`, Gate-2 `layer-all.sh` attempt 1): same test, same helper, signature `"did not increase above baseline 7 within 60s (last observed: 1)"` — identical to occurrence 1 but for the baseline integer (5→7). Did NOT reproduce on attempt 2 (`26_mh_quic` 7 passed/0 failed in 71.53s), so it was ruled operator-lane, not diff-caused; the changeset contained no service runtime code and no mc-service file at all, yet mc-0/mc-1 had rolled. This is the entry's stated forcing condition — a recurring L7 counter-delta flake — now met, 23 days after occurrence 1, on the same test. **Two occurrences is also the evidence that the 'loud, never a false pass' property is holding**: both instances cost a pipeline attempt and neither could have greened over a real defect. **RESOLVED 2026-08-29** (`docs/devloop-outputs/2026-08-29-l7-counter-delta-per-instance/`): both counter-delta helper families now capture the baseline as a PER-INSTANCE map via `sum by (instance)(...)` (grouping label `instance` = pod IP:port, confirmed by @observability against the scrape config) and pass when ANY currently-present instance beats its OWN baseline (a fresh post-rollover pod, absent from the baseline, passes once its value > 0). A stale old-pod series that expires mid-assertion is simply absent from the current map and can no longer inflate anything, because the comparison never sums across pods — the retry-path exposure is gone with it. The pure decision (`any_instance_exceeds_baseline` in `crates/env-tests/src/fixtures/metrics.rs`; `anyInstanceExceedsBaseline` in `packages/web-app/e2e/instanceCounters.ts`) is the single source of truth per language, each covered by a deterministic no-cluster unit test; the Rust↔TS parity is held by convention + those mirrored tests (NOT structurally — a NaN/Inf parse divergence was caught at Gate 3 and pinned as a parity case). **This closes 2 of the 3 sites of the stale-series defect class** — the two `26_mh_quic.rs` families and their `mcMetrics.ts` mirror. The third, `31_gc_telemetry.rs::pii_dropped_sum`/`assert_drop_counter_increased`, is the same cluster-wide-`sum` shape and is tracked as a separate same-owner follow-up below (it needs a magnitude predicate, not this boolean one — genuinely task-sized). **Qualifying the entry's "loud, never a false pass" property (@security, Gate 3):** that property held for the OLD cluster-wide form, whose churn failure was one-directional (false-negative only). The per-instance form trades it for rollover-robustness and carries a NARROW residual false-pass window: an instance absent from the baseline is compared against zero, so a *pre-existing* pod that was merely missing from the baseline read (unscraped beyond `query.lookback-delta`, or a transient empty result) and then reappears passes on its accumulated value rather than on a test-driven increment. It is documented on both decision functions rather than designed out (no cheap new-pod-vs-returning-pod discriminator without pod start time); the window it opens is narrower than the flake it removes.
- [x] **`26_mh_quic.rs::mc_participant_mh_status_counter` masks Prometheus query failure as a 0.0 reading** (`Err(_) => return 0.0`; same surfacing context as the entry above, flagged 2026-08-05 by task #19/@operations as a fail-loudly/never-mask violation). A Prometheus outage mid-poll reads as "counter is 0" — indistinguishable from a real zero, misdirecting triage toward the service under test. The TS mirror (`packages/web-app/e2e/mcMetrics.ts::promInstantSum`) deliberately THROWS on transport/query failure (global-setup already proved Prometheus healthy, so a failure there is a real problem) — the Rust helper should match that contract; audit sibling helpers in the crate for the same `unwrap_or(0.0)`-on-error shape while there. Owner: env-tests / observability. Defer trigger: next env-tests crate touch or a recurring L7 counter-delta flake. **RESOLVED 2026-08-29** (same devloop as the entry above): the per-instance readers now route through `PrometheusClient::instance_counter_map` → `instance_map_from_query`, which PANICS on a transport/HTTP-status/deserialization error (naming the PromQL + `PrometheusError` so triage lands on Prometheus, not the service under test) and maps ONLY an empty instant vector (a successful query for a not-yet-observed series) to an empty/zero map — the two are kept strictly distinct and the split is unit-tested. Sibling audit: `31_gc_telemetry.rs:324` was ALREADY fail-loud (`pii_dropped_sum` does `.expect(...)` on the query; its `unwrap_or(0.0)` is only the absent-series fallback) — left unchanged; `30_observability.rs`'s `Err(_) => return false` sites are inside `assert_eventually` retry closures (a readiness/warmup contract whose terminal failure panics loudly) — left unchanged, by design.
- [ ] **`31_gc_telemetry.rs::pii_dropped_sum`/`assert_drop_counter_increased` is the third (still cluster-wide-`sum`) site of the stale-series-inflation defect class** (surfaced 2026-08-29 by @test-reviewer + @dry-reviewer at Gate 3 of `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-08-29-l7-counter-delta-per-instance/`, which fixed the other two sites — the `26_mh_quic.rs` families + their `mcMetrics.ts` mirror, see the resolved entry above). `pii_dropped_sum` (`crates/env-tests/tests/31_gc_telemetry.rs:312`) captures a cluster-wide `sum(gc_telemetry_pii_attributes_dropped_total{kind=…})` scalar as `before`, then `assert_drop_counter_increased` (line 331) waits for `pii_dropped_sum >= before + expected`. On the Layer-7 retry path a `rebuild-all` rolls the 2-replica GC Deployment; an old GC pod that recorded drops in attempt N is still inside Prometheus's staleness window when attempt N+1 captures `before`, inflating it; the old series then expires mid-assertion and the fresh pods' sum can never reach `before + expected` (unless the rolled pod's contribution was 0 — which a prior drop-planting run makes false) → the same guaranteed-timeout-on-the-final-attempt exposure as `26_mh_quic.rs`. **Why a follow-up, not folded into the 2026-08-29 fix (Lead ruling, Gate 3):** this uses a MAGNITUDE predicate (`>= before + expected`), not the boolean `> baseline` the per-instance helpers provide, and its current correctness depends on the cluster-wide sum being pod-agnostic ("correct regardless of which pod served the POST" — the `C2′` comment at line 305). Per-instance-izing it needs a real design decision (identify the serving GC pod and assert the delta on that instance, or a different stale-robust shape) plus a `by ≥ expected` predicate variant of `any_instance_exceeds_baseline` — materially more than the boolean conversion. The now-shared `crates/env-tests/src/fixtures/metrics.rs` (`instance_counter_map` + the pure decision helpers) is the extraction point. **BLOCKING QUESTION, must be answered by @global-controller BEFORE any port — do not pick a default** (merged in from @dry-reviewer's entry so it lives with the authoritative record): does the assertion require that ONE pod saw the whole `expected` delta, or that the deltas SUMMED across pods reach it? These are different assertions, and the one-pod reading is strictly WEAKER for `expected > 1` — a 2-pod split of a 2-attribute drop satisfies the summed form and fails the one-pod form, or, if the predicate is written as "any pod moved by >= expected", silently passes on a partial. The `C2′` comment's R7 one-writer-per-`{kind}` argument SUGGESTS one-pod, but that is a claim about GC telemetry routing (does a single POST's attributes always land on one pod's counter?), not a property of the metric, and it is unverified. Record the answer here when obtained, because both fix shapes encode it. **Fix shapes, once the above is answered**: (a) a per-instance magnitude predicate beside the boolean sibling in `crates/env-tests/src/fixtures/metrics.rs` — `any_instance_exceeds_baseline_by(baseline, current, delta)` for the one-pod reading, or `total_increase_across_instances(baseline, current) >= delta` for the summed reading. **The summed variant is the safer default if the routing answer is uncertain**: it is per-instance for the STALE-SERIES purpose (only instances present in `current` contribute, so an expired old-pod series cannot inflate) while still summing the deltas, so it kills the flake WITHOUT weakening the assertion either way. Pin whichever is chosen with a unit test that names the rejected alternative. Or (b) leave the sum and add a pods-settled pre-read, accepting the retry-path exposure. Owner: env-tests / observability (@test co-owns the mcMetrics mirror class; @global-controller owns the routing answer above). Defer trigger: next `31_gc_telemetry.rs` touch, or a recurring L7 GC-telemetry counter-delta flake. (This is the single authoritative entry for the GC site; @dry-reviewer's §Cross-Service Duplication line is a one-line pointer here.)

Both the drift and the missed sibling are direct consequences of there being no automated check. When built, the guard's scope must be the **three-way** set: runbook §3 ladder + `_common.sh::__status_rank`/`status_to_exit_code` + the `run-guards.sh` exit-block ANCHOR (DRY) mirror.
- [x] **`validate-subdomain-regex-sync.sh`'s sweep scans generated files, not tracked source** (surfaced 2026-08-21 by dry-reviewer at Gate 3 of the fast-fail-guards devloop). **RESOLVED 2026-09-01** (`2026-09-01-subdomain-guard-tracked-only`): the step-(3) sweep is now `git -C "$REPO_ROOT" grep -I -n -F -e "$CANONICAL" -- :(exclude)…` (guarded by a REPO_ROOT-is-git-top-level precondition; no `:/` anchor — @security S1/S2) — git-tracked files only, so gitignored build output (`coverage/**`, `.nx/cache/**`) is excluded BY CONSTRUCTION, closing the false positive AND the exact-equality false negative (an untracked artifact can no longer offset a deleted tracked pin) in one move. SINGLE-PATH, per the constraint below: there is no scan branch — the guard runs the same `git grep` against the real root and the seam, and the self-test makes the seam viable by `git init`+`git add -A`ing its synthetic fixture (shape (a)) rather than the guard branching for a non-git tree. The audit-trail carve-out (`docs/devloop-outputs/**`, `docs/user-stories/**`) survives as `:(exclude)` pathspecs — those dirs ARE tracked and DO quote the pattern; the guard file self-excludes the same way. Pinned 10 re-verified over tracked source with `coverage/`+`.nx/` artifacts present (green); all 22 self-test assertions green. The stale grep-option-ordering / `--`-terminator header comment was replaced to describe the git-tracked mechanism. Original entry follows. The guard `grep -rn`'s the tree with a `--exclude-dir` denylist (`node_modules/target/dist/…`) and pins an EXACT-EQUALITY total (`total -ne EXPECTED_TOTAL_OCCURRENCES`, 10 = 7 enumerated SITES + 3 unenumerated test pins). A denylist is unsound in **both** directions: (false POSITIVE) a gitignored generated dir it doesn't list — `coverage/` (vitest HTML) and `.nx/` (nx cache) mirror the sdk-core `SUBDOMAIN_REGEX` into copies — inflates the count and reds a LOCAL guard re-run after a TS coverage build (observed this devloop: 10→13); (false NEGATIVE) because the pin is exact-equality, deleting an unenumerated test pin (10→9) while a stray artifact adds +1 (→10) passes SILENTLY, losing a real pin — the drift-masking the guard exists to prevent. Adding `--exclude-dir=coverage --exclude-dir=.nx` (the interim fix considered + REVERTED this devloop) is whack-a-mole on the positive and does nothing for the negative. **Proper fix (task-sized):** rewrite the sweep to scan **tracked files only** — `git ls-files -z | grep -F -z` (or per-file) — which closes the false-positive (generated files are untracked, never scanned), the false-negative (an untracked artifact can never offset a deleted tracked pin), and the build-state nondeterminism, by construction. **Why task-sized, not a trivial edit (deferral burden of proof, verified by dry-reviewer):** the guard resolves `REPO_ROOT="${SUBDOMAIN_GUARD_ROOT:-$__real_root}"` and the self-test drives it against a synthetic tree with **no `git init`**, so `git ls-files` there returns nothing → `total` hits 0 → the guard's own vacuity branch fires → every self-test case reds. The seam must be reworked in the same change. **Do NOT repair it by branching the scan** (`git ls-files` for the real root, `find`/`grep -r` under the seam): that makes the guard's tested path structurally different from its production path — the "a green test proves *a* path ran, not that *the* path ran" defect class recorded elsewhere in this file, and especially poor to build into a DRIFT guard. Single-path shape: keep ONE `git -C "$REPO_ROOT" ls-files -z` sweep and have the self-test `git init` + `git add -A` its fixture (a few lines in the test, no branch in the guard). Also re-verify the pinned 10 against tracked source once artifacts are excluded. Owner: operations (validation-pipeline guards). CI is unaffected today (Layer 3 precedes the coverage-generating Layer 4 on a fresh checkout); the bite is local re-runs + the latent false-negative. Deliberately NOT folded into the fast-fail-guards diff — an unrelated guard edit inside a validation-pipeline change is the shape that should not be convenient (Lead reversed an initial fold-in ruling on exactly this ground).

- [ ] **Env-test probe class: "observed nothing" must be distinguishable from "observed a passing value" — one invariant, three sites, no shared helper** (class named 2026-09-02 by @test-reviewer + @dry-reviewer at task #9 Gate 2; filed as a class rather than a fourth one-off so the next instance is greppable). The invariant: *an assertion whose purpose is to detect a non-empty bad thing must first prove its input set is non-empty; absence of evidence is not evidence of absence.* Three known instances, three different mechanisms, one violated invariant: (1) `26_mh_quic.rs::mc_participant_mh_status_counter` — error-swallow (`Err(_) => 0.0`), a Prometheus outage read as "counter is 0"; **RESOLVED 2026-08-29** (see the resolved entry above). (2) `31_gc_telemetry.rs::pii_dropped_sum`/`assert_drop_counter_increased` — stale-series/cluster-wide-`sum` baseline; **OPEN**, tracked in full above (magnitude-predicate variant needed; @global-controller owes the routing answer). (3) `00_cluster_health.rs:61,108` credential-leak probes — empty-selector (`-n default` matched zero pods, `!"".contains(...)` passed unconditionally); **FIXED in task #9** by namespace correction + an `assert_pods_exist()` panic guard that re-fires on the next namespace/label drift (Lead Ruling 2 — fixed, not deferred, because a bare namespace swap would re-arm the trap). **The generalizable fix is one shared helper, not three rewrites**: an env-test primitive that every probe calls to assert its result set is non-empty (pods matched / series present / rows returned) before asserting anything about contents — the shape `01_mh_deployment_config.rs::fetch_pod` already embodies (panics on empty `items`, on all-terminating, on absent field; never a vacuous green). Scopable as a single follow-up covering the still-open site (2) plus the extraction of the shared primitive; the next instance will be a fourth probe type (not `kubectl` or PromQL), and this named class is what lets a `git grep` for the invariant find the precedent instead of re-deriving it. Owner: **test / env-tests** (@observability co-owns the PromQL sites; @global-controller owns site (2)'s routing answer). Defer trigger: next env-tests crate touch that adds or edits a probe, or the next recurrence of a vacuous-green env-test.


- [ ] **`dt-guard env-config`'s per-service hard-fail does not catch a workload dropped from a service that still has one — the detector is a number a human has to notice (owner: infrastructure, as `dt-guard` machinery per CLAUDE.md; surfaced 2026-09-02 by @operations at Gate 3 of `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-02-mh-transport-config-and-drain/`, verified at source by @media-handler)**: the guard hard-fails when a service has **zero** discoverable workloads (`crates/dt-guard/src/env_config.rs`, the `discovered.workloads.is_empty()` branch and its `NO_WORKLOAD_MANIFEST` rule, pinned by the `missing_workload_is_hard_fail` test). That is an all-or-nothing check **per service**, and it is not the failure that matters for per-instance services.
  **The uncaught case**: if `mh-1-deployment.yaml` stops being discovered — renamed, moved, `kind:` changed, or made unparseable — `discovered.workloads` is `[mh-0]`, which is **not empty**. So no hit is raised, `checked_workloads` increments by 1 instead of 2, the REASON token silently reads `...-5-workloads`, and **`STATUS=OK`**. `mh-1` is then entirely unchecked for required-env-var coverage while the guard reports clean — which is precisely the crash-loop-a-single-pod case the per-workload design exists to prevent, and the same "a signal silent about its own coverage reads as clean" shape recorded elsewhere in that devloop.
  **The count is the intended detector, and that is the gap.** `Report::checked_workloads`'s own docstring says it "makes a silently-dropped instance manifest visible in the status line rather than only in a diff" — so the mechanism is deliberate and correct as far as it goes. But **visibility is not enforcement**: it requires a human to read the token and remember that the right number is 6. Nothing anywhere asserts the real-tree count. The one place `6` appears (`clean_outcome_reports_both_counts_when_services_were_checked`) constructs a `Report` by hand to test **token formatting**; it never touches the tree. Verified: no `min_workloads`, `expected_workloads` or equivalent floor check exists in `crates/dt-guard/` or `scripts/`.
  **Shape of the fix**: assert the discovered workload count against the manifest tree rather than against an operator's memory — e.g. count workload-kind documents under `infra/services/*/` and fail when the number the guard *checked* is lower than the number that *exists*. Deriving it from the tree rather than enumerating an expected total is what keeps it from becoming a second thing to drift (same constraint as the runbook-workload guard entry below). Defer trigger: the next `dt-guard env-config` touch, or any service moving to or from per-instance workloads — the latter being exactly how the sibling runbook defect arose.

- [ ] **163 runbook commands target Kubernetes workloads that do not exist — 79 remaining after the MC sweep of 2026-09-03** (surfaced 2026-09-02 by @operations at Gate 1 of `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-02-mh-transport-config-and-drain/`, while fixing the two instances inside that devloop's own diff). Three distinct defects share one shape — a runbook naming a workload after its *Service* rather than its actual workload object:
  - `deployment/mh-service` (**33 refs remaining**: `mh-incident-response.md` 32, `mc-incident-response.md` 1) — no such Deployment. MH's workloads are `mh-0`/`mh-1` (`infra/services/mh-service/mh-{0,1}-deployment.yaml:4`). Owner: @media-handler.
  - `deployment/mc-service` — **CLOSED 2026-09-03** at Gate 3 of `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-03-mc-client-media-signaling/`. All 80 command sites were rewritten to `mc-0` / `mc-1`, both MC runbooks gained an §MC Topology preamble, and the 29 sites that were also on the wrong health port now forward `8080:8081`. **Re-opened and re-closed 2026-09-05** for the Service-DNS form — see the second paragraph below; do not read the original "CLOSED" as covering it. The 7 surviving textual occurrences are deliberate *negative examples* ("there is no `deployment/mc-service`") in `mc-deployment.md` (2), `mc-incident-response.md` (2), `mh-incident-response.md` (2) and `gc-incident-response.md` (1) — **do not "fix" them**, and note that a naive `grep -c` therefore over-reports this line as open.
    **The first close attempt was premature, and the reason generalises to the two remaining sweeps.** The sweep matched `deployment/mc-service` — the **slash** form — and therefore missed six live commands in the **space-separated** form, `kubectl get deployment mc-service` / `kubectl describe deployment mc-service` (`mc-deployment.md` 185/239/252, `mc-incident-response.md` 468/807/1931). Two of them sat *inside the very hunk* whose sibling line the sweep had just corrected. Each returns `deployments.apps "mc-service" not found`, and they directly contradicted the §MC Topology preamble the same commit added. Fixed at the operations review of the same devloop. **`kubectl` accepts `<kind>/<name>`, `<kind> <name>` and `<kind>s <name>` interchangeably — any sweep or guard for this class must match all three**, which is also a requirement on the Layer-3 guard candidate two entries below. Budget the MH and AC sweeps accordingly.

    **A SECOND close attempt was also premature, and it found a THIRD form the "all three" rule does not cover — the Service-DNS form (@operations, 2026-09-05, at the Gate-3 operations review of the same devloop).** Six live commands read `curl http://mc-service.dark-tower.svc.cluster.local:8080/{health,ready}` — `mc-incident-response.md` 2, `gc-incident-response.md` 2, `mh-incident-response.md` 2 — and survived both earlier passes because they name no workload kind at all, so neither the slash sweep, the space sweep nor the `8080:8080` port-forward sweep could see them. **They are broken twice over, and the second break is the dangerous one.** (a) The `mc-service` ClusterIP exposes health on **8081**, not 8080 (`infra/services/mc-service/service.yaml`), so nothing listens. (b) More seriously, MC's NetworkPolicy admits TCP 8081 from **Prometheus only** — GC and MH are admitted on gRPC 50052 and nothing else — so correcting the port alone would have produced a command that is *silently dropped* and **times out** instead of failing fast. A timeout during an incident reads as "MC is wedged", which is the single conclusion a dependency-health check exists to rule out. **The trap is the asymmetry with the sibling lines in the same command block**: AC admits 8082 from gc/mc/mh and GC admits 8080 from everywhere, so in a block of three dependency curls the AC and GC lines genuinely work and only the MC line cannot — an operator has every reason to read the odd one out as the broken dependency. Fixed at that review: all six replaced with `kubectl get endpoints` plus the per-instance port-forward form, and the reason stated once as a new bullet in the byte-identical §MC Topology preamble carried by both MC runbooks. **The generalised rule, which supersedes "match all three" as too narrow: sweep for the RESOURCE, not for the syntax that names it.** A workload can be referenced as `<kind>/<name>`, `<kind> <name>`, `<kind>s <name>`, by label selector, or — as here — by Service DNS with no kind token anywhere in the line. Any guard for this class must also check that a cited port is actually exposed by the Service and actually admitted by the NetworkPolicy, because a syntactically-correct command against a netpol-denied port fails *silently and slowly*, which is worse than the `NotFound` this entry was originally about. Budget the MH and AC sweeps for this too: MH has the identical netpol shape (8083, Prometheus only). Sweeping the sites also surfaced three adjacent defects fixed in the same pass: 8 `kubectl scale` commands that *succeed* and then break ADR-0023 session binding (replaced with the arithmetic, and the surrounding prose that still prescribed scaling was rewritten with it — a half-corrected command block is worse than an uncorrected one), an inverted `Required` column plus six phantom variables in `mc-deployment.md`'s env table, and a wrong TLS Secret block.
  - `deployment/ac-service` (**46 refs remaining**: `ac-service-incident-response.md` 37, `gc-incident-response.md` 4, `mc-incident-response.md` 2, `mh-incident-response.md` 2, `gc-deployment.md` 1) — wrong **kind**, not wrong name: `ac-service` exists but is a **StatefulSet** (`infra/services/ac-service/statefulset.yaml:2`). Correct form is `statefulset/ac-service`. Owner: @auth-controller.

  **What the MC sweep demonstrated, and why the remaining 79 should not be batched as a `sed`**: the workload-name substitution was the *cheapest* part. Each of the 8 `scale` sites needed the surrounding remediation prose rewritten too, because replacing a command while leaving "Option 1: Scale horizontally to distribute load" above it produces a labelled remedy, an expected recovery time, and no action — a runbook that reads as complete and is not. Budget the MH and AC sweeps for per-site reads on the same basis.

  Every one returns `NotFound`. The operational cost is concentrated: these are `rollout undo`, `rollout restart`, `rollout history`, `scale`, `patch` and `exec` commands, so they fail **at the moment of use during an incident or a rollback** — loud, but loud in the worst possible window, and the operator must then derive the correct name under time pressure. "It fails safely" describes the failure mode, not the cost.

  **A blind `sed` is NOT the fix and would cause a regression.** `deployment/gc-service` is **correct** — GC genuinely is a single Deployment of that name (`infra/services/gc-service/deployment.yaml:4`) — and there are **115 such refs** (`gc-incident-response.md` 73, `gc-deployment.md` 25, `mc-incident-response.md` 9, `mc-deployment.md` 5, `mh-incident-response.md` 3). A pattern-wide rewrite would corrupt all of them. The per-service answer differs three ways (per-instance pair / per-instance pair / kind change), so each of the 161 needs the right substitution, and the per-instance cases additionally need a judgement call per site: some commands are correct against **both** pods (`rollout restart deployment/mh-0 deployment/mh-1`, the form already used correctly at `mh-incident-response.md:401`), while `exec`-shaped ones target **one** pod and the runbook must say which, or say "either".

  **Why deferred rather than fixed at the surfacing devloop**: 7 files across 4 owning specialists (@media-handler, @meeting-controller, @global-controller, @auth-controller), 161 sites, each needing a per-site read. That is task-sized by any reading and none of those owners were on the transport-config panel. **Original counts are as of the pre-fix tree (`7c740e71`)**: 163 broken across 7 files, of which the surfacing devloop fixed the 2 sitting in its own diff (both in `mh-deployment.md`), leaving 161 across 6 files; the 2026-09-03 MC sweep then closed 82 more (80 `mc-service` plus the 2 in `mh-incident-response.md`), leaving **79 across 5 files**. Re-verify the per-service counts before acting rather than trusting these numbers — that is the point of the paragraph below. `deployment/gc-service` is 115 in both snapshots. Stated explicitly because a reader re-deriving the total today gets 161, not 163 — the first filing of this entry quoted 162, a figure that mixed a post-fix `mh-service` count with a pre-fix `mc-service` one while the corpus was being edited underneath the measurement. The two instances that sat inside that devloop's own diff (both in `mh-deployment.md`: `deployment/mh-service` in the rollback command, `deployment/mc-service` in the MH rollback block) **were fixed there**, not deferred — each was one line in an already-open operations-owned file and a manifest lookup, not a domain judgement.

  **The durable fix is a guard, not 161 edits** (CLAUDE.md: "add a guard that fails validation on drift"; ADR-0036: a control's coverage must be demonstrated, not asserted). Shape: parse `kubectl <verb> <kind>/<name>` occurrences out of `docs/runbooks/**` and assert each `(kind, name)` pair resolves to a real workload in `infra/services/**`, failing on any that does not. This is the same class as the existing alert-rule check that every runbook *reference* resolves to a file — extended from "the doc exists" to "the object the doc tells you to operate on exists". **A resolvability guard is necessary but NOT sufficient, and must not be mistaken for the whole fix**: it would green a command that resolves and still does the wrong thing. `rollout restart` is correct against *both* pods of a per-instance pair, while `exec`-shaped commands target *one* and the runbook must say which — a per-site judgement no guard can make. Fix the sites by hand; use the guard to stop the class regenerating. Without it, the class recurs the next time a service moves to per-instance workloads, which is exactly how they arose (MC and MH both migrated to per-instance Deployments; the runbooks were never swept). A `dt-guard` subcommand (ADR-0034) or a `scripts/guards/simple/` script; note it must read the workload inventory from the manifests rather than an enumerated list, or it becomes a second thing to drift.

  Owner: operations (validation-pipeline guards), with the four service specialists confirming their own workload names and the one-pod-vs-both-pods reading at each `exec` site. Defer trigger: next guard-pipeline touch, the next runbook edit touching a `kubectl` command, or the next incident where a documented command returns `NotFound`.

## Env-Test Self-Sufficiency

- [ ] **AC org provisioning endpoint**: Add an admin/internal API to AC for creating organizations. Env-tests should create their own test org via this endpoint instead of depending on pre-seeded data in `infra/docker/postgres/init.sql`.
- [ ] **Remove init.sql seed data**: Once the AC provisioning endpoint exists, remove the `devtest` org/user seed logic from `infra/docker/postgres/init.sql` and update env-tests (20, 21, 23) to self-provision via the API.
- [-] **Env-test portability — remove localhost/port hardcoding**: Partially resolved. `ClusterPorts::from_env()` (ADR-0030) now reads `ENV_TEST_AC_URL`, `ENV_TEST_GC_URL`, `ENV_TEST_PROMETHEUS_URL`, `ENV_TEST_GRAFANA_URL`, `ENV_TEST_LOKI_URL` with localhost defaults. Remaining: (1) remove `mc_webtransport_url` from `ClusterConnection` — MC/MH endpoints should come from GC join responses, (2) tag the invalid-token negative test as local-only or discover MC endpoint dynamically.

## Bootstrap Data Provisioning (SQL seeding → admin APIs)

*One pattern, several instances: bootstrap state the product should own is written by raw SQL from `setup.sh`, so test suites reach around the services to arrange state, exercise paths no real client can take, and duplicate rules (subdomain shape, cap semantics, credential scopes) that a service should enforce once. Sequencing constraint across all of them: calling an admin API needs an admin credential, and credentials are themselves SQL-seeded, so none escapes seeding until the credential API lands first.*

- [ ] **AC org provisioning API**: `setup.sh:705` has carried `TODO: Replace with AC org provisioning API` at the `seed_demo_org` INSERT for some time; `provision_run_org()` (added 2026-08-15 for per-run layer-7 org isolation) is a second instance and is marked as a stopgap in place. Both write `organizations` rows via `kubectl exec … psql`, which additionally requires the dev container to hold a cluster-admin kubeconfig for what should be an API call. Would also give org **deprovisioning** a home — see the Organization Lifecycle entry, which is blocked on a separate FK problem. Note for planners: during the 2026-08-11 story-runner planning a specialist proposed exactly this and the lead scoped it out as unnecessary, on the incorrect reasoning that existing SQL seeding made an API a non-dependency. It is not a dependency of *provisioning working*; it is the difference between a test fixture and a product capability.
- [ ] **AC admin API for service credentials**: Add `POST /api/v1/admin/service-credentials` to AC for registering/updating service credentials (client_id, scopes, service_type). Idempotent upsert. Currently service credentials are seeded via raw SQL in `infra/kind/scripts/setup.sh:seed_test_data()`, which has caused bugs (missing `internal:meeting-token` scope for GC) because credential config is decoupled from the code that requires it.
- [ ] **Per-service credential registration Jobs**: Each service (GC, MC, MH) should own its credential registration via a K8s Job in its Kustomize base. The Job calls the AC admin API to register the service's client_id and required scopes. Deploy pipeline ensures AC is ready before downstream services deploy. This way, adding a new scope (e.g., `internal:meeting-token`) is part of the same PR that adds the endpoint requiring it.
- [ ] **Remove setup.sh SQL seeding**: Once the admin APIs and registration Jobs exist, remove the raw SQL seeding from `infra/kind/scripts/setup.sh` and `infra/docker/postgres/init.sql` — credentials (`seed_test_data`) **and** organizations (`seed_demo_org`, `provision_run_org`, and the `dt_psql` helper they share). Removing the org path also removes layer 7's need for a cluster-admin kubeconfig to provision.

## Organization Lifecycle

- [ ] **Org deprovisioning is unsupported — deleting an organization fails on a FK violation**: `organizations`' children cascade (`ON DELETE CASCADE`), but the cascade reaches `users` and stops: `auth_events.user_id REFERENCES users(user_id)` has no `ON DELETE` clause (`migrations/20250122000001_auth_controller_tables.sql:59`) and `auth_events` carries no `org_id`, so the delete aborts. Two consequences worth knowing before this is picked up: (1) a retention decision is needed first — audit rows probably should outlive the user, so `ON DELETE SET NULL` rather than cascade; (2) GC maps a missing org to **500** (`MeetingRefusal::OrganizationNotProvisioned`) on the reasoning that `org_id` comes from a signed JWT claim, so an org that does not exist is a provisioning bug rather than a lifecycle state — if deprovisioning ships, revisit that mapping, since a valid token for a deleted org becomes normal and 401/403 fits better. Surfaced 2026-08-15.

## Client Architecture

- [ ] **Evaluate HTTP/3 for AC**: AC currently serves HTTP/1.1 (TCP-based). For consistency with GC, evaluate adding HTTP/3 support. Low priority — client is protocol-agnostic via `fetch()`. Follow-up to ADR-0003.

- [ ] **Roster shows a departed participant for 30–60s on tab-close (leave-latency fix #64 incomplete)**: Manual test 2026-08-08 — closing a browser tab leaves the participant's name in other participants' rosters for 30–60s before it clears. Task #64 added `MC_QUIC_MAX_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default 10s, `crates/mc-service/src/config.rs:54`) as the crash/network-loss fallback, but the observed 30–60s ≠ the configured 10s — which means the config value is almost certainly **not wired into the actual QUIC endpoint** (the underlying wtransport/quinn library default ≈30s is firing instead): a plumbed-but-not-wired gap in the same shape as #63 (config field + validation + parse tests exist, but the last wire to the transport is missing). **Verify**: grep where `quic_max_idle_timeout_seconds` is *consumed* by the endpoint builder. Deeper gap: a tab-close should trigger **prompt** departure via a WebTransport close event (~1s), not any idle timeout — the fix is (1) client sends an explicit leave on `pagehide`/`beforeunload` (reliable — do not depend on the browser's implicit connection-teardown timing), (2) MC handles the transport-close event immediately (broadcast ParticipantLeft), (3) idle timeout as last-resort fallback, actually wired this time. **Test-vs-reality gap**: #60's teardown E2E uses Playwright `context.close()` (likely a cleaner teardown than a user tab-close) and asserts *eventual* departure (60s poll), not promptness — so it passed while the real path is slow; the fix's test must assert **bounded** latency via a mechanism that matches a real tab-close. Owner: meeting-controller + client (+ test). Surfaced 2026-08-08 manual test.

- [ ] **`SignalingClient.#terminate` teardown-robustness — emit before `#teardown`** (slug: `signaling-client-terminate-emit-before-teardown`, **Owner: client**). In `packages/sdk-core/src/signaling/SignalingClient.ts`, `#terminate` calls `this.emit('error', …)` on the join-settled branch BEFORE `this.#teardown()`, so a throwing consumer `error` listener skips teardown and strands the transport/reader (`#terminated` already latched → no recovery). Same shape as the `MeetingSession.disconnect` issue fixed in task #14 (symmetric ~2-line fix: run the settle/emit in `try`, `#teardown()` in `finally`). **Pre-existing** — task #14's diff only renamed `#emit`→`emit`, not the ordering — so scoped out of that devloop. Surfaced 2026-06-29 by browser-client-join task #14 (operations reviewer, Gate 3).

## Observability Debt

### Six single-event `increase(...)>0` alerts have no automated exerciser — and after the counter-visibility fix they change from silently-never-firing to firing (2026-09-10, counter-zero-init devloop; owner: `test` for the harness, `operations` for the rollout)

The counter-visibility fix (present-at-zero of discrete-event `*_total` counters) un-breaks six alerts that could NOT fire before (a lazily-created counter has no `0→1` edge, so `increase(...)>0` read 0 forever): `MCActorPanic` (`mc-alerts.yaml:35`), `MCMediaPolicyDivergence` (`:162`), `MCSenderIdSpaceExhausted` (`:314`), the GC org meeting-creation alert (`gc-alerts.yaml:325`), `MHCallerTypeRejected` (`mh-alerts.yaml:173`), and the MH sender-binding out-of-range/conflict alerts (`mh-alerts.yaml:229,251`). Correctness of "does each now fire" is **derived by inspection**: the repo has NO `promtool test rules` harness (`gc-alerts.yaml:321` says so in-tree) and two of the six cannot be provoked in a Kind devloop, so "verify each fires" is unverifiable here and was NOT claimed (OPS-17, resolution a). TRIGGER: build a `promtool test rules` harness (task-sized, its own devloop) and add fixtures for these six; until then, the first deploy after the fix may surface a genuine backlog on these alerts — triage each against its runbook scenario, do NOT silence (silencing restores the exact defect the fix removed).

### `dt-guard` subcommand count is past ADR-0034's re-debate heuristic (2026-09-10, counter-zero-init devloop; owner: `infrastructure`)

`dt-guard` now exposes ~37 subcommands (the counter-zero-init guard is the newest); ADR-0034 §When-to-Revisit trips its "consider splitting into 2-3 focused binaries" heuristic at ≥10. This is pre-existing machinery debt, not introduced by any one guard. TRIGGER: run the split re-debate (a `/debate`), NOT a mechanical fix.

### `dt_client_*` metrics have ZERO static guard coverage in alerts and dashboards (2026-09-09, story task #22)

**Owner**: policy content `observability`; **guard machinery `infrastructure`** (per
CLAUDE.md's guard ownership split — matcher implementations and the shape of the
constructs policy is expressed in are machinery).

`dt-guard application-metrics` extracts metric references from alert rules and dashboards
with `SERVICE_METRIC_PREFIX_RE`, which is built at `Lazy::new` time from
`CANONICAL_SERVICES` (`crates/dt-guard/src/common/services.rs`: the const at `:45`, the
regex at `:65`), giving `\b((?:ac|gc|mc|mh)_[a-z][a-z0-9_]*)`. **Underscore is a word
character**, so `dt_client_media_frames_dropped_total` matches nothing, is never
extracted, and is never checked — in either direction.

**Demonstrated, not asserted** (task #22): corrupting `mh_media_forward_latency_seconds_bucket`
in `infra/grafana/dashboards/mh-media.json` fires
`VIOLATION: mh-media.json (dashboard_metric_missing)`; corrupting
`dt_client_media_frames_dropped_total` in `infra/grafana/dashboards/client-media.json`
leaves the guard reporting `STATUS=OK REASON=application-metrics-clean`.

**Consequence**: a typo in `MCMediaMissingKeyMaterial`'s expression
(`infra/docker/prometheus/rules/mc-alerts.yaml`) passes CI silently while the alert never
fires. That rule's sole coverage is operations' "does it apply" step — the counter
arriving in Prometheus from a real browser through the SDK sink and the GC telemetry
proxy. That is why the step is load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces.

**THE WRONG FIX, NAMED**: adding `dt_client` to the alternation. This is the same
word-boundary property ADR-0036 §11 describes for the deny-guard vocabulary, but §11's
segment-splitting remedy **does not transfer**. Two failures, in the order they occur:

1. The alternation is derived from `CANONICAL_SERVICES`, which is a **guarded
   release-premise mirror, not a free-to-edit metrics list** — its own doc comment says
   so, and `release_build_profile`'s `canonical_services_roster_drift` rule derives from
   it. `dt_client` is not a `crates/*-service` workspace member, so **roster-drift fires
   first**.
2. Even past that, extracting the name would immediately fail `alert_metric_missing`,
   because no Rust `metrics.rs` defines it and none ever will.

**The real fix** is a TypeScript-aware metric source for the guard (parsing
`packages/sdk-core/src/**` emission sites the way the Rust side parses `metrics.rs`).
Task-sized; explicitly out of scope for task #22.

### Restated label rosters and restated counts have no guard, and no sweep enforcement (2026-09-09, story task #22)

**Owner**: policy content `observability` (with `security` for label-value policy);
**guard machinery `infrastructure`**.

Two surfaces, one mechanism: **nothing in the tree compares prose to the thing it
describes.**

- **Label rosters.** `application-metrics` and `dashboard-panels` validate metric
  **names** against code, catalogs, dashboards and alerts, and `alert_rules.rs` pins an
  alert `expr` byte-for-byte against its `alerts.md` entry. **No guard reads a label key
  or a label value.** So a label roster restated in a panel description, a runbook table
  or a doc comment decays invisibly to CI. The remedy adopted in task #22 is procedural —
  the per-service catalogs are the single home and new panel descriptions *cite* rather
  than restate — which is a convention, not a control.
- **Counts.** `MediaDropReason::ALL: [Self; 13]` is compile-checked; every prose copy of
  that number is unchecked.

**The sweep is the thing that needs the guard, not the individual sentence.** Story task
26 added two `MediaDropReason` tokens, and *that same commit* wrote `ALL`'s warning against
naming ordinals **and** deleted `mh-service.md`'s restated cardinality integer — then left
`crates/mh-service/src/observability/metrics.rs`'s "11 MH-local series rather than 22"
behind, stale, in the very file defining the compile-checked length. This is not "nobody
knew the rule": it is a **correctly-diagnosed class with an incomplete sweep**, which is
why better prose is not the instrument. (Fixed in task #22 by deletion, not by updating
the integer — updating it re-arms the trap at token 14.)

**Candidate remedy** (machinery, `infrastructure`): a guard flagging prose integers
adjacent to a compile-checked `ALL: [Self; N]`, and/or label-value extraction so a roster
in a description can be compared to the emitting site. Task-sized; explicitly out of scope
for task #22.
