- [ ] **Two remaining matcher anchors are narrower than Rust's grammar in two independent ways (owner: infrastructure for the construct shape, observability for the metric-label policy half; surfaced 2026-09-08 in `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-08-media-telemetry-deny-policy/`)**: **this is a DIFFERENT failure from the entry above and must not be folded into it.** That one is *a guard reporting clean over an absent scope*; this one is *a live guard missing a live spelling inside a scope it is walking correctly*. Different failure, different remedy.
  **The two classes, per anchor.** (1) **Whitespace before `!`** — Rust tokenises `path ! delim`, so `counter !("m")` compiles; and consumers run over `blank_non_code` output, which turns an interposed comment into spaces. (2) **Paren-only delimiter** — the anchors end `!\s*\(`, but `counter!{…}` and `counter![…]` are legal invocations, so this is a one-CHARACTER evasion where the first is a one-space evasion.
  **Outstanding — exactly TWO anchors, both in one file**: `crates/dt-guard/src/metric_macros.rs:152` (`MACRO_INVOCATION_RE`) and `:180` (`MACRO_INVOCATION_WITH_FIRST_ARG_RE`), both classes, consumed by `application_metrics`, `dashboard_panels`, `metric_coverage` and `histogram_buckets`. **`metric_labels.rs` is NOT outstanding — both its halves landed on 2026-09-08** (see the line below); if you find it listed as outstanding anywhere else, that text is stale.
  **ALREADY FIXED on 2026-09-08, so this entry is TWO outstanding items and not five**: `telemetry_macros.rs:252` (`LOG_MACRO_RE`) and `:275` (`TRACING_NAMED_RE`, which had *three* sub-gaps — no whitespace around `::`, none before `!`, paren-only); both anchors in `media_telemetry_deny.rs`; and **`metric_labels.rs`'s `MACRO_OPENER_RE` in BOTH halves** — the whitespace half first, then the delimiter half after the deferral below was re-priced and withdrawn in review.
  **THE SEAM — line gates versus body scanners — is real, but it does NOT size the work, and a first draft of this entry used it to justify a deferral that did not survive contact with the code.** A *line gate* is an `is_match` call and widens for free. A *body scanner* parses from the delimiter: `metric_labels.rs`'s `find_macro_invocations` locates the opener as `whole.end() - 1` and depth-matches, so it must know the matching closer. That distinction is worth keeping — it tells you where to look — but it was then used to price the body-scanner half as "task-sized", and **that was wrong by roughly an order of magnitude**: the remedy is to read one opener byte, derive its closer, and compare the depth loop against those two variables instead of two literals. Six lines. The sizing was done without opening the loop. **Both halves of `metric_labels` landed in the surfacing loop as a result.**
  **The two anchors that DO remain are the cheapest shape in the class, not the most expensive — do not inherit the paragraph above as their price.** `MACRO_INVOCATION_WITH_FIRST_ARG_RE`'s four consumers (`application_metrics.rs:56`, `dashboard_panels.rs:113`, `metric_coverage.rs:39`, `histogram_buckets.rs:41`) are all `captures_iter` reads of capture group 3; **none depth-matches anything**, and `MACRO_INVOCATION_RE` has no consumer outside `metric_macros.rs` at all. So there is no body scanner behind either, and the *code* change is regex-only. The real cost is elsewhere and should be priced there: a full-tree false-positive sweep plus pin updates across four consumer guards, two of which (`application_metrics`, `metric_coverage`) are themselves the subject of the vacuity entry above. (Consumer audit by @infrastructure, 2026-09-08.)
  **Severity is not "a missed match", and this is the sentence that sets the priority.** `metric_labels.rs`'s opener is the **discovery loop** feeding the label PII checks, and it is used a second time as a **file-discovery** gate — so an invocation that evades it is never label-checked, and a file whose metric macros are all brace-form never enters the scan set at all. `counter!{"m", "email" => user_email}` would ship an unbounded, PII-bearing metric label with nothing firing (ADR-0029). The now-fixed `telemetry_macros` pair had the same shape in `rust_pii.rs:133` and `rust_log_secrets.rs:186`, where a miss skipped the **entire** PII and secrets vocabulary scan for that line.
  **Why the class is self-perpetuating and nobody noticed**: the pinned equality tests on these patterns exist to make a *narrowing* red. These patterns were never wide enough, so **no pin redded and nothing noticed** — it took a widening in an unrelated guard (`media_telemetry_deny`, ADR-0036 §11) to surface the class at all. And unlike `media-telemetry-deny`, which fails loudly on its own scope, none of these guards has a scope self-check, so a narrowed anchor is indistinguishable from a clean tree indefinitely. Read those pins as coverage of **preservation**, never of adequacy.
  **Not a promotion regression**: @security's `c0538b56` trailer certified that the promotion **preserved** these detection sets, which it did faithfully. It never certified they were adequate. Both holes are inherited verbatim from the pre-promotion literals.
  **THE CLASS IS "GATES ON MACRO-INVOCATION SPELLING", NOT "`Lazy<Regex>` ANCHORS" — and scoping it to regexes is why the item below was missed (@security S3).** A raw `contains` doing the same job belongs in this entry: `crates/dt-guard/src/rust_log_secrets.rs:218` gates Check 4 (secret in a named tracing field) on `line.contains("tracing::") || line.contains("#[instrument")`. **INHERITED HOLE, INTRODUCED DIVERGENCE — the split sets the priority and must not be collapsed (@infrastructure).** This diff did NOT open a hole in a secrets guard: Check 4's gate is byte-identical to its 2026-09-07 form, so `tracing :: info!(…)` evaded it before this diff and evades it after, and its coverage is exactly unchanged. What this diff changed is that two gates which previously AGREED now disagree — `TRACING_NAMED_RE` tolerates `tracing\s*::\s*` and the raw `contains` does not. Read as "we opened a hole in a secrets guard" this pages someone; read correctly it is the SSoT cleanup it actually is. The concrete divergence: after 2026-09-08, `tracing :: info!("x", user = %ctx.token)` is caught by `rust_pii` Check 2 and by nothing in `rust_log_secrets` — Check 2 there does not cover it either, because `SECRET_IN_LOG_SHAPE_RE` wants the vocabulary word immediately after `%`/`?`, inside `{}`, or as `, word ,)`, and `%ctx.token` is none of those. Unspaced, Check 4 catches it; spaced, nothing does. That is a secret-in-log false negative. **THE OBVIOUS FIX IS A TRAP, and this sentence is why the item is deferred rather than done inline (@infrastructure).** `TRACING_NAMED_RE.is_match(line)` is NOT a behaviour-preserving swap for the `contains`. The two differ in **two** dimensions, in opposite directions: the regex is wider on WHITESPACE, but the `contains` is wider on SPELLING — it fires on any `tracing::` occurrence at all, including non-macro ones like `tracing::Span::current()` or `tracing::field::display(...)`, which the regex cannot match because it requires a level name, a `!` and an open delimiter. Swapping it in as a DRY cleanup would silently NARROW a secrets guard on every non-macro `tracing::` spelling. (Contrast G6, where the re-point was safe because the derived alternation was byte-identical and pinned; the difference is invisible unless you read both.) So closing the divergence means either widening the `contains` to tolerate whitespace — a broadening, needs a sweep — or introducing a third pattern deliberately wider than `TRACING_NAMED_RE`, which needs @security sign-off on what Check 4's gate is *supposed* to be. Both are judgement calls, and that is the real reason this is deferred. Deferred with the same sweep discipline as the anchors above, and named here rather than left implicit because an Outstanding list that reads complete and is not is the defect this whole entry is about. (For completeness so the next author does not re-sweep: `rust_pii.rs:90`'s `contains("#[instrument") && contains("skip")` is a **suppressor**, so its spelling-sensitivity fails CLOSED — more findings, not fewer — and is not a false negative.)
  **Conditions that travel with the fix**: pin against hand-written literals in the test body, never against anything derived from `MacroKind::ALL` (a self-comparison passes unchanged when a variant is deleted); keep `MacroKind::ALL`'s declared order, which its own doc calls load-bearing, rather than sorting as the `Level` pins do; and run a full-tree false-positive sweep **for the names actually being widened** — the 2026-09-08 sweep covered the brace/bracket form for the LEVEL names only, and the metric-name half had to be run separately by @infrastructure (zero pre-existing invocations tree-wide, `metric-labels-clean-5-files` unchanged, which is the count that moves if the file-discovery gate pulls new files in). Citing a neighbouring set's measurement as coverage of yours is the same error one level down. Since a delimiter widening is a broadening. Target slug: to be scheduled; pair with security.

- [ ] **`MH_MAX_TOTAL_EGRESS_EDGES` has a terminal signal but no saturation signal (owner: observability, with operations; trigger: story task 21's MH media alerting; raised by @operations as OPS-1 at Gate 3 of `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-02-mh-register-meeting-policy-apply/`, accepted by @observability)**: today the only visibility into the aggregate egress-edge bound is `mh_media_policy_applies_total{outcome="apply_failed"}`, which fires when new meetings are *already* dark. `RoutingSnapshot::total_edges()` and `meeting_count()` are already exposed as accessors in `crates/mh-service/src/routing/mod.rs`, so the instrument is cheap: a pod-level gauge of edges in use, and the ratio against the configured bound, turn a signal that only exists after the fact into one that can be acted on before it. **Deliberately not landed at task 11**: a new metric carries a catalog entry, a dashboard panel and both the `metric_no_catalog` and `metric_no_dashboard` obligations — task-sized, not a Gate-3 fix.
  **What ratchets is a floor, not the total** — this is the corrected mechanism and the alert design follows from it. `projected_total_edges` subtracts the meeting's own installed edges before adding its new ones, so a live meeting that shrinks releases headroom. What nothing releases is the edges held by meetings that have **ended** — MH gets no teardown signal, `MediaHandlerService` has no such RPC, and `NotifyMeetingEnded` is MC→GC. That floor rises at the meeting-completion rate while the headroom above it shrinks asymptotically, so `apply_failed` from this cause is **intermittent before it is permanent**: it clears when some unrelated meeting happens to shrink and returns when none does, uncorrelated with anything the affected meeting did, worsening over uptime. **Alert on the floor's trend as a fraction of the configured bound, never on instantaneous headroom and never on a crossing condition.** Instantaneous headroom oscillates with ordinary meeting churn, and there is no single crossing to alert on: the first failures are isolated and self-clearing, so a crossing alert either fires on a transient and gets tuned out, or is debounced hard enough that it only fires once the floor is permanently high — which is past the point where anything but a restart helps.
  **The pod does not look degraded while this happens**, which is why a gauge is the only thing that catches it. Existing meetings re-asserting at an unchanged generation take the `==` arm and never reach the cap check, so they keep reporting `outcome="applied"` at the full re-assert cadence. And the affected population is not only new meetings: an existing healthy meeting cannot admit a new **participant** either, because that needs an extra egress edge, therefore a higher generation with more edges, therefore the cap arm. Everyone already talking keeps talking; every new arrival gets silence in a meeting that is otherwise working, blames their own network, and drops — so the failure suppresses its own evidence and will not arrive as a user report. That is ADR-0036 §8's black-hole-reporting-healthy failure arriving through a resource bound rather than through a generation echo.
  **Wrong-fix trap, named because the gauge invites it.** A bare pod-level count is the whole fix. The reach that follows — "add a `meeting_id` (or `sender_id`, or `by(meeting)`) dimension so we can see *which* meeting is consuming the edges" — is barred by `docs/observability/label-taxonomy.md` §R1 (no meeting identifier on any metric, raw **or hashed**) and §R2, and it arrives disguised as triage rather than as a policy change, typically a release after the gauge lands and from someone who never read this entry. The correct triage surface for per-meeting attribution is the `mh.session.policy` WARN line, which already carries `installed_total_edges` and `installed_meeting_count` and is not a metric. **Record the gauge as deliberately dimensionless.** A pod-level aggregate raises nothing under §R2 — it has no per-stream or per-meeting decomposition and `pod` is R2's stated aggregation floor — and that judgment is recorded here so task 21 does not relitigate it.
  **Paired with the missing reclamation path** filed under §Media Path Obligations: that entry is the missing reclamation, this one is the missing early-warning, and they are two halves of one cliff.

- [ ] **D1 — MH/MC/GC scrape cadences are configured in a file the cluster does not read; deployed cadence is 15 s, not 5 s/10 s (surfaced 2026-09-02, story task 7)**: `infra/docker/prometheus/prometheus.yml` sets `mh-service` to `scrape_interval: 5s` ("More frequent for real-time media metrics", `:44`) and `mc`/`gc` to 10 s (`:37`, `:30`). That file is **live but local-only** — mounted by `docker-compose.yml:87-98`. The **deployed** path is Kind: `infra/kind/scripts/setup.sh:587` applies `infra/kubernetes/overlays/kind/observability/`, a labels-only passthrough over `infra/kubernetes/observability/prometheus-config.yaml`, which declares **no per-job `scrape_interval` at all** — every job inherits `global.scrape_interval: 15s` (`:27`, its only occurrence). So MH is scraped at **15 s wherever anyone actually triages**, 3× coarser than intended. **Why it matters, not cosmetic**: a decomposed forwarding-latency histogram is close to useless for triage at 15 s — a media-quality incident is typically shorter than a few scrape intervals, so a responder sees two or three points across the whole event, not enough to distinguish a spike from a ramp or to tell which of the three latency phases moved. The 5 s cadence was chosen precisely to make that readable. **Fix**: add the three per-job `scrape_interval` overrides to the authoritative k8s config (~6 lines), and close the mechanism as well as the instance — reciprocal `ANCHOR (DRY):` comments in both files plus a sync guard, following the tree's existing precedents (`packages/sdk-core/src/validation/limits.ts:94`; `scripts/guards/simple/validate-subdomain-regex-sync.sh`, `validate-slug-class-sync.sh`). Without the guard the two files rediverge silently. **Also update `docs/observability/dashboard-conventions.md` §Periodicity as part of this fix** — that subsection currently documents the 15 s deployed cadence as a gap, and every statement in it (the Deployed column, "the deployed cadence is 15 s", the Intended/Deployed split, the triage-resolution argument) **inverts and becomes false** the moment the overrides are applied. Nothing else will prompt it, and the doc that describes the drift truthfully today would become the tree's most confident wrong statement about cadence. **Note the deploy step**: the ConfigMap edit changes nothing until `kubectl apply -k infra/kubernetes/overlays/kind/observability/` runs and Prometheus reloads — an in-tree edit alone re-creates the same doc-says-X/reality-says-Y gap pointing the other way. Rollback is one line (revert the keys, re-apply; no migration, no restart ordering, existing series unaffected). **Cost is explicitly NOT an objection** — scrape interval changes samples-per-series, not cardinality, and does not multiply series count. **Why not fixed in task 7**: Domain-judgment on a deployed config owned by infrastructure, who was not on that panel; ADR-0024 §6.3 routes that to owner-implements, and the required `kubectl apply` is a host operation the devloop container cannot perform. Documented truthfully in `docs/observability/dashboard-conventions.md` §Periodicity in the meantime. Owner: **infrastructure** (+ operations for the cadence decision). **Corroboration — three independent arrivals, 2026-09-02 story task #9 (@observability, Gate 3)**: two further specialists reached this gap from directions unrelated to the original latency-triage argument. @media-handler-consult arrived via *buffer dynamics* (asking what scrape cadence a datagram-queue gauge needs to be meaningful); @operations arrived via *config precedence*, and stated it in the most legible form yet — "a media service scraped at 15 s in the environment that matters, while the config that says media deserves 5 s is the one nobody deploys." Recorded because the entry previously read as one observer's finding: three arrivals from three directions is materially better prioritisation evidence, and the third route is the one that shows the drift is reachable without any media-specific context at all. **A live instance of the cost, same day**: `infra/services/mh-service/configmap.yaml` briefly carried the literal "MH is scraped at 15 s" in a comment; @code-reviewer read the nearest Prometheus config (the local-only compose file), concluded 5 s, and filed the comment as a factual error. A careful reviewer was actively misled by the two-config split during review — not hypothetically. The comment was rewritten to state the *relationship* (scrape interval ≫ buffer fill/drain time) and cite no figure at all, which is the cheapest form of re-derivability: do not restate a value the tree already encodes twice. That fix does not close this entry — it removes one consumer of the ambiguity, not the ambiguity.

- [ ] **MH's transport-ceiling saturation signal exists only while task #16 stays on quinn's non-dropping send path — one boolean silently converts a live alert into a dead one (surfaced 2026-09-02 by @observability at Gate 3 of story task #9)**: quinn offers two datagram send paths and only one of them is observable. `Datagrams::send(data, drop=true)` pops the oldest queued datagram and emits `trace!(len, "dropping outgoing datagram")` and nothing else (`quinn-proto-0.11.17/src/connection/datagrams.rs:44-49`) — an untraceable, uncountable discard. `send(data, drop=false)` instead sets `send_blocked` and returns `SendDatagramError::Blocked(data)` (`:52-55`, with `Event::DatagramsUnblocked` at `connection/mod.rs:3327`) — a **returned value**, therefore countable, therefore the thing an alert can rest on. @media-handler-consult has committed task #16 to the non-dropping path via `send_datagram_wait`, which is what makes MH's transport saturation observable at all, and additionally makes the application queue trip first **mechanically** rather than merely numerically (a shallower app bound alone guarantees nothing if the code pushes into quinn unconditionally). **The exposure**: flipping that one boolean — a plausible edit for someone optimising away an `await`, in a hot path where awaiting looks like the expensive choice — silently removes the only countable saturation signal. **Why this is worse than losing a metric**: once an alert rests on the `Blocked` counter, the flip leaves the alert *defined, enabled, and rendering as active on the dashboard*, while it can never fire again. **A dead alert is worse than no alert** (@operations), because it manufactures assurance at exactly the wrong moment: a responder triaging audio loss who checks the media-saturation alert, sees green, and moves on has been *actively misled*, whereas an absent alert routes them to the next signal. This is ADR-0036 §11's "a control that applies but never fires" with the operational consequence spelled out, and it is the **third instance of one pattern in this story** — the struck `MH | Audio jitter` objective (`docs/observability/slos.md` §Struck), the gauge-only-alert prohibition on `MH_DATAGRAM_BUFFER_AUDIO_FRAMES`, and this. All three read as coverage, cannot fire, and stop anyone asking the question. **Why guard-able rather than merely documentable, which is unusual for this class**: the failure has a single mechanical signature — a `drop=true` argument, or a `send_datagram(` call where `send_datagram_wait(` is required — inside `crates/mh-service/`. That is a grep, not a semantic judgement, so unlike most "someone might later change X" residuals this one can be enforced rather than hoped for. **Fix shapes**: (a) a `dt-guard` simple check rejecting the dropping-send call form in mh-service, with the rationale naming the alert-invalidation consequence rather than merely asserting the rule — a guard whose justification names the failure it prevents survives review, one that asserts a preference does not; (b) at minimum, a comment at the call site recording that `drop=false` is load-bearing for **observability**, not only for back-pressure (@media-handler-consult has committed to this half regardless). Prefer (a); (b) alone leaves the property resting on a comment nobody re-reads. **Not actionable until task #16 lands** — the call site does not exist yet, so there is nothing to guard today. Owner: **media-handler** (task #16 for the call site and the comment; the guard is infrastructure's mechanism per task #17), **@observability reviews** — the property being protected is metric survivability, which is why this sits in Observability Debt rather than the alerting section: it is about whether a signal can be emitted at all, upstream of any expression-or-threshold question. Defer trigger: task #16 review.

  **CORRECTED AND LARGELY VOIDED 2026-09-05 (story task 16, at its own review). The premise above is FALSE, and this entry is the pre-correction claim it warns about, standing in the file the corrected `configmap.yaml` now cites as authoritative.** Recorded as an amendment rather than a rewrite, because a reader who checked one clause, found it false and discarded the whole entry would lose the part that survives.
  **What is false**: `send(data, drop=false)` does not deliver a countable `Blocked` **to MH**. The public API MH can reach is `quinn::Connection::send_datagram`, which hardcodes `drop=true` and treats the blocked arm as `unreachable!()`; the congestion-aware `send_datagram_wait` does reach that arm but **retains the payload and yields `Poll::Pending`** (`quinn-0.11.11/src/connection.rs`). Back-pressure is expressed by **awaiting**, never by returning a value. So there is **no countable saturation signal on either path**, "@media-handler-consult has committed task #16 to the non-dropping path" never happened and could not have — MH's seam method is synchronous by design because `wtransport::Connection::send_datagram` is a plain `fn` — and no alert can ever have rested on a `Blocked` counter.
  **What survives, and it is the useful half**: a dead alert is worse than no alert, and this class of failure — a control that applies but can never fire — is real. It simply lands somewhere else. MH's **own bounded egress queue** is the only observable shed, which is why the `EgressQueueDoesNotBindFirst` startup validation exists, and the residual blindness beneath it is tracked at the entry titled *"MH's egress-drop counter is structurally blind to quinn's own silent drop-oldest one layer below it"* in §Media Path Obligations, which carries the full citations against `Cargo.lock`-pinned versions and is the **single home** for this fact.
  **The proposed guard is voided with it.** There is no `drop=true`-versus-`drop=false` call form in `crates/mh-service/` to grep for: MH calls the seam, the seam calls `wtransport`, and neither exposes the boolean. A guard rejecting `send_datagram(` in favour of `send_datagram_wait(` would forbid the only call MH can make. **Do not build it.** Owner: observability (this entry's author) to close or re-scope; media-handler concurs. Left open rather than deleted only so the correction is read by whoever comes looking for the original claim.


- [ ] **D3 — seven ratio alerts do not carry the non-zero-denominator guard (surfaced 2026-09-02, story task 7)**: `GCHighErrorRate`, `GCErrorBudgetBurnRateCritical`, `GCErrorBudgetBurnRateWarning`, `GCMCAssignmentFailures`, `GCTokenRefreshFailures`, `GCDatabaseDown`, `MCGCHeartbeatWarning`. The convention (`and sum(rate(<denominator>)) > 0`) is now documented at `docs/observability/alert-conventions.md` §Non-Zero-Denominator Guard and seeded into `_template-service-alerts.yaml`, but these predate it. **None is currently misfiring** — all seven have pre-existing totals as denominators, and PromQL yields NaN for 0/0 which does not fire, so this is consistency rather than an active defect. **Read the convention before "fixing" these**, because the obvious rationale is wrong: the guard is not divide-by-zero protection, it is load-bearing only when the denominator is *attempts* (`forwarded + dropped`), where guarding one addend instead of the sum makes the alert **silent in the everything-dropped case**. Also do **not** normalise the three deliberate look-alike idioms into conformance: `mc-alerts.yaml:69` is a rate floor (`> 0.1`), and `gc-alerts.yaml:123,140` are offset baselines for silence detection — removing the `offset` inverts their meaning. Four of the seven are `severity: page`. Durable fix is a `dt-guard` check flagging unguarded ratio expressions, which must distinguish those three idioms or it will push someone to break the seasonal-baseline alerts. Owner: **observability** (mechanism) with the GC/MC service specialists (per-rule judgment, ADR-0031).

- [ ] **D4 — the media-path identity prohibition has no enforcement covering its stated scope (surfaced 2026-09-02, story task 7)**: `docs/observability/label-taxonomy.md` §Media-path identity states the meeting-identifier ban as applying to "any metric **anywhere in this design**", per ADR-0036 §11. The durable enforcement is §11's **directory-scoped macro deny**, which covers only the media hot-path directory — strictly narrower than the rule's stated scope. **Nothing enforces the difference**, and the vocabulary guard cannot close it: `meeting_id` is in no guard vocabulary (`crates/dt-guard/src/common/pii_vocabulary.rs` has no `meeting` token), and `meeting_id_hash` is **actively exempted by construction** — `HASHED_SUFFIXES` (`pii_vocabulary.rs:286`) contains `_hash` and `_id_hash`, consumed by `metric_labels.rs:529 is_hashed_label()`. So a raw or hashed meeting-id label on any non-media metric passes every guard in the tree today. **Wrong-fix trap**: adding `meeting_id` to the Category B denylist is *inert against the realistic spelling* and would read as coverage while shipping the violation — ADR-0036 §11's "vocabulary additions cannot be cited as the protection" as a concrete instance. A real fix needs segment-splitting matching plus a decision about the ADR-0028 grandfathered join-flow set, which legitimately carries `meeting_id_hash`. Task-sized. Owner: **observability + security**. **AMENDED 2026-09-02 (story task 8, security review).** Three facts D4 did not have. **(a) There is no server-side backstop — the proxy actively permits the label.** `crates/gc-service/src/services/telemetry_filter.rs:25` `ALLOWLIST` carries `meeting_id_hash` at index 3, applied by `filter_attrs` to datapoint attributes **and** exemplar `filtered_attributes` on Gauge/Sum/Histogram/ExponentialHistogram. So D4's "the client-side guard is missing" understates it: the guard is missing **and** the one control that would otherwise catch a client regression is configured to allow it. Three independent blessing points — `HASHED_SUFFIXES` exemption, `media-transport.test.ts:270` asserting it, and this ALLOWLIST — each individually defensible, composing to zero defence in depth. **(b) Exemplars are an uncovered surface.** R2 names four surfaces; the directory-scoped macro deny reaches log fields and span attributes, the (proposed) label allow-list reaches metric labels, and **nothing reaches exemplars**. ADR-0036 §11 rejects exemplars by name on this path, so the correct rule is a presence **deny**, not an allow-list extension — extending the allow-list would legalise them with a blessed label set. Note `packages/sdk-core/src/telemetry/telemetryConfig.ts` configures no exemplar behaviour at all, so OTel JS defaults govern: a config-shaped surface with no macro and no call site to match. **(c) Mechanism: count-don't-drop.** `filter_metrics` binds `metric` at the loop head (`:155`), so `metric.name` is available at every `filter_attrs` call site — name-aware handling is parameter threading, **not** the redesign it was first sized as. Enforcement stays client-side per R3; the server contributes the missing **detection**: increment a bounded counter when an allowlisted-but-media-inappropriate key appears on a media-prefixed metric. No behaviour change, no risk to the ADR-0028 grandfathered join metrics. **Both new labels must be projected onto a closed set before becoming dimensions** — the offending key bucketed by ALLOWLIST membership, the metric name matched against the known media set with an `other` bucket. Not `assert!`: this is production request-path code over untrusted OTLP, so a panic is client-triggerable and ADR-0002 prohibits it outright; `debug_assert!` is worse, compiling out exactly where the untrusted input arrives. Owner for the proxy half: **global-controller** (not on the task-8 roster). **AMENDED 2026-09-02 (story task 13, observability review) — the vocabulary half is now PARTLY closed, and D4's "wrong-fix trap" must be read with one correction.** D4 says adding `meeting_id` to the denylist is inert and would read as coverage. That holds for **Category B**, which is where D4 assumed it would go — and it is exactly why the change that landed put `meeting_id` in **`PII_PREFIX_DENYLIST`** instead: `pii_token_hit` scans prefixes before `is_hashed_label()`, so `meeting_id_hash` is caught rather than exempted. **D4 stays open, for three reasons plus one:** (a) the Prefix arm is gated on `pii_safe.is_none()`, so the bar is **bypassable** by a one-line comment — only Category A is not, while ADR-0036 §11 states R1 absolutely; (b) the match is `starts_with`, so a trailing compound (`x_meeting_id`) still passes — the segment-splitting matcher D4 asks for remains the real fix; (c) the scanner reads `crates/`, so the TS client SDK half, including the ADR-0028 grandfathered join set and amendment (a)'s GC telemetry-proxy `ALLOWLIST`, is untouched. **Plus**: the guard's Prefix finding message hardcodes `raw_` semantics ("the `raw_` prefix signals an unsanitized identifier; rename or add `# pii-safe`"), which is wrong advice for this term and advertises the bypass as the remedy. Owner unchanged: **observability + security** for the vocabulary content; the bypassability and per-entry-message halves are guard **machinery** (**infrastructure**) per CLAUDE.md §Guard-crate ownership, since both change a construct's shape rather than a list's membership. **The finding-message string correction that landed with story task 13 does NOT discharge this**: it stops the message asserting `raw_` semantics over a non-`raw_` term, but the per-entry fix — `PII_PREFIX_DENYLIST` carrying its own guidance per term, so `raw_`'s "unsanitized identifier, surfaced for review" and `meeting_id`'s "absolute bar" read differently to an author — still requires the construct change and is still open.

- [ ] **D5 — client media-path metrics inherit `meeting_id_hash` by inertia; exemption not yet applied (surfaced 2026-09-02, story task 7)**: `docs/observability/label-taxonomy.md` §Media-path identity R3 requires client media-path metrics to carry **only** `client_version` and `org_id`. That is a **required end state, not current behaviour**: `packages/sdk-core/src/session/MeetingSession.ts:308` builds the implicit join label set (`client_version`, `meeting_id_hash`, `org_id`) and threads it into every emission site including the media module (`packages/sdk-core/src/media/events.ts:44`), and `packages/sdk-core/src/media/__tests__/media-transport.test.ts:270` **asserts** `meeting_id_hash` in that label set. So a passing test currently pins the behaviour the rule prohibits. The risk is inertia: the label set arrives by default and **doing nothing ships the violation**. A hashed meeting id is barred on both of §11's grounds — identical cardinality to a raw one, and per-meeting aggregation in a two-person meeting is nearly per-stream. **Fix**: apply the media-path exemption and update the test when the SDK media pipeline lands (story task 19). Owner: **client** (with observability review). **AMENDED 2026-09-02 (story task 8, security review).** The inertia is dangerous, not merely untidy: `reason` × `meeting_id_hash` is a **decryption oracle**. The reject-reason vocabulary is a faithful mirror of where in the crypto stack a frame died; aggregated it is operationally necessary and harmless, but joined to a meeting dimension it becomes a per-target distinguisher — an attacker who can inject crafted frames reads which crypto layer rejected each probe. `unwrap_failed` is the sharpest: it confirms the KEK unwrap **succeeded**, i.e. the prober's KEK generation matches the receiver's, which is a positive fact about receiver key state. The discriminator is **not** codec-versus-crypto but **byte-determined versus receiver-state-dependent**: a reason fully determined by the frame bytes and the public format spec tells the frame's author nothing they did not have (so all eight codec structural rejects are safe to emit per-token), while one depending on receiver-held state is an oracle (`no_kek_for_generation`, `no_roster_entry`, `no_transmit_key` — codec-layer but receiver-state-dependent — `signature_invalid`, `decrypt_failed`, `unwrap_failed`). **This is orthogonal to granularity**: all reason values are emitted individually per R-25/R-31; the restriction is solely about never joining them with a participant, meeting or stream dimension. The rule changes nothing operationally today — R2 already bars identity dimensions from all media-path labels — it exists to pre-answer *"the codec tokens are harmless, can we slice just those by meeting?"*: no, because R2's trace argument still reaches them even though the oracle argument does not.  **AMENDED 2026-09-08 (story task 19) — HALF LANDED, ENTRY STAYS OPEN AS A STANDING OBLIGATION.** **What landed**: every media-path emission now goes through `mediaMetricLabels` in `packages/sdk-core/src/media/setup/mediaMetrics.ts`, an ALLOW-LIST projection whose constructor takes two named strings rather than a `MetricLabels` bag — so `meeting_id_hash` is not merely absent from media metrics, it is UNREPRESENTABLE at that boundary, and there is no spread to inherit a future join label from. `media/__tests__/hotPathLayout.test.ts` asserts positively that `setup/mediaMetrics.ts` is the ONLY file under `media/**` naming a `dt_client_` metric, which closes the sibling-directory hole (`lifecycle/`, `setup/`, `teardown/` sit outside ADR-0036 §11's deny by design and hold the KEK, roster keys and transmit keys). A negative test asserts no `dt_client_media_*` series carries `meeting_id_hash`. **What did NOT change, by written ruling (@observability, 2026-09-08)**: `dt_client_mh_connection_total` KEEPS `meeting_id_hash`, and `media/__tests__/media-transport.test.ts` keeps the assertion that pins it — annotated at both sites so the two opposite-direction assertions read as a pair rather than a contradiction. Grounds: it is an ADR-0028 join-flow metric that carried the join set from birth, §11 grandfathers those AS A SET, and neither §11 argument reaches it (the trace argument is about the time-ordered sequence of sizes for ONE stream; the oracle argument is about `reason` mirroring which crypto layer rejected a frame, and `status`/`mh_index_bucket` are not crypto-layer discriminators). The grandfathered set is now FROZEN with a named member list in `docs/observability/metrics/client.md`, because a closed exception with no roster opens by analogy. **WHY THIS ENTRY STAYS OPEN**: the ruling creates a STANDING OBLIGATION with no mechanical enforcement — keep the roster frozen, and classify every future client metric against the line **the test is what a metric OBSERVES, not which directory it lives in** (connect-lifecycle is grandfathered; media-carrying is under the bar). A directory-shaped rule fails in both directions, and the failure that will actually happen is permitting a media counter placed outside the media tree. The enforcement gap is D4, which stays open.

- [ ] **D6 — `docs/observability/dashboards.md` catalogs almost none of the dashboards that exist (surfaced 2026-09-02, story task 7)**: 14 dashboard JSONs are on disk (`ac`/`gc`/`mc`/`mh` × `overview`/`slos`/`logs`, plus `errors-overview.json` and `_template-service-overview.json`), while the catalog documents a handful and marked two existing ones — `ac-overview.json` (75,849 B) and `mh-overview.json` (53,638 B) — as "🚧 To be created". Those two were corrected in task 7 because they sat in blocks already being edited. **The rest of the index was not audited.** This is the doc an oncall consults to learn what exists; for any service it under-reports, that means hand-rolling PromQL against a deployed dashboard nobody knew was there. Note `platform-overview.json` and `database-performance.json` are **correctly** marked as not existing. Owner: **observability**.
- [ ] **D7 — `ac-slos.json` plots token issuance at p95 while the AC SLO is p99 (surfaced 2026-09-02 by @operations during story task 7)**: `infra/grafana/dashboards/ac-slos.json` uses `histogram_quantile(0.95, …)` — its only quantile — while `docs/observability/slos.md` and ADR-0011 both define AC token issuance and validation as **p99** (< 350 ms / < 50 ms). **The dashboard an operator opens to check SLO compliance is tracking a quantile the SLO is not written against**, so it under-reports exactly the tail the objective exists to bound. On a bcrypt-dominated path p95 and p99 are materially different bars, so this is not a rounding difference. Surfaced only now because task 7 created the authoritative register that makes the comparison possible — which is the register's purpose working as intended, on its first day. **Not fixed in task 7**: changing an SLO dashboard's quantile alters what a shipped compliance signal reports and makes its history non-comparable, the same reason the GC availability-numerator entry is scoped separately; and `ac-slos.json` is AC's artifact per ADR-0031, with AC not on that panel. Check the AC alert rules for the same mismatch while fixing. Owner: **auth-controller** (dashboard), with **observability + operations** as reviewers (ADR-0031).
- [ ] **D8 — `slos.md` declares itself the authoritative SLO register while omitting ~11 targets the rest of `docs/observability/` already asserts (surfaced 2026-09-02 by @dry-reviewer at Gate 2 review of story task 7)**: task 7 created `docs/observability/slos.md` and gave it stated precedence ("This file is authoritative for SLO targets... Where the two differ, this file wins"). Its Live register holds **5** targets (AC issuance/validation, GC request + availability, MC session join) plus the two MH rows. The tree asserts **~16** SLO targets outside it, most absent from the register: `docs/observability/metrics/ac-service.md:30` (p99 <350ms), `:220` (p95 <200ms); `metrics/gc-service.md:49` (p95 <200ms), `:106` (p95 <20ms), `:139` (p99 <50ms), `:607` (p99 <200ms); `metrics/mc-service.md:82` (p99 <100ms), `:96` (p99 <10ms); `metrics/mh-service.md:51` (p95 <100ms); `dashboards.md:28` (200ms), `:32` (20ms), `:35` (50ms), `:167` (500ms); `alerts.md:714` (p99 <500ms); `alert-conventions.md:47` (500ms). (`dashboard-conventions.md`'s "a 200ms SLO sets the red threshold at 0.200" is a threshold-config *example*, not a target claim — leave it.) **Why this is newly load-bearing rather than pre-existing noise**: before task 7 these were scattered peers with no stated winner. Task 7 declared a winner. An authoritative-but-incomplete register is worse than no register, and `slos.md` names the exact failure itself — "an absent row is indistinguishable from a decision not to have an SLO, which is precisely how a paging gap survives behind a green dashboard" — then omits eleven rows. Concretely: a reader consulting the authoritative register for the MC assignment-latency SLO concludes there is none, while `dashboards.md:32` specifies a 20ms SLO line for it (and `GCMCAssignmentSlow` pages on it). **Two live inconsistencies already visible**: `dashboards.md:32` specifies a "20ms SLO line" for MC Assignment Latency, an SLO the authoritative register does not contain at all; and `dashboards.md:167` specifies a 500ms line for MC *message processing* while the register's only 500ms entry is MC *session join* — a different operation. **Fix**: reconcile each of the ~16 into one of three dispositions — (a) genuine ratified SLO, promote into the register; (b) a dashboard threshold convention, not an SLO, reword to drop the "SLO" claim; (c) stale, delete. Then make the satellites point rather than restate, as `dashboards.md`'s AC and MH blocks now do. **Not doable inside task 7**: per-target this is a ratification judgment, and `slos.md` itself states a target lands only when observability and operations have both signed off; eleven of those decisions is task-sized, not an inline edit. **Wrong-fix trap**: do not bulk-copy the 16 literals into the register to make it "complete" — that promotes unratified dashboard thresholds to fleet SLOs by clerical action, which is how `MHHighAudioLatency`'s unratified `>30ms` became load-bearing in the first place. Owner: **observability + operations** (joint, per ADR-0011:40). **WIDENED 2026-09-02 with @operations' independent Gate-3 finding (F6), which reached the same defect from live artifacts rather than from doc restatements — folded here rather than opening a parallel entry, since two entries for one gap is the failure mode this file already suffers from.** The omitted targets are backed by SHIPPED artifacts, not aspiration, and one of them **pages today**: **GC MC-assignment p95 < 20 ms** is enforced by `GCMCAssignmentSlow` (`infra/docker/prometheus/rules/gc-alerts.yaml`, `histogram_quantile(0.95, …) > 0.020`) and dashboarded at `gc-slos.json` "MC Assignment SLO – Compliance %" / "– Current p95"; **AC availability and error-rate** ship as dedicated panels in `ac-slos.json` ("Availability SLO – Error Budget Remaining", "– Uptime", "Error Rate SLO – Current") against a register carrying only AC's two latency rows; **MC heartbeat and token-refresh** ship in `mc-slos.json` ("GC Heartbeat SLO – Success Rate", "Token Refresh SLO – Success Rate", "– Current p99") against a register carrying only session join. These are `*-slos.json` **compliance** dashboards, not exploratory panels. **The paging case is the sharpest consequence and the one to write any fix against**: an operator paged by `GCMCAssignmentSlow` consults the authoritative register for the objective, its error budget and its burn posture — the register's stated purpose — finds no row, and under the precedence rule concludes the 20 ms threshold is an unratified guess when it is a shipped, alerting objective. That **inverts the triage**, which is worse than the ambiguity the precedence rule was added to remove. Note `ac-slos.json`'s "Token Issuance Latency SLO – Current **p95**" independently corroborates D7 (register says p99). Ratifiers therefore include **auth-controller, global-controller and meeting-controller** alongside the joint observability + operations owners. **Strongest single piece of evidence that the register was worth writing** (@dry-reviewer's observation at Gate 3): the AC token-issuance quantile drift shows up **twice, independently, in two different artifact kinds** — `dashboards.md:140-141` asserted p95 in *prose*, and `ac-slos.json` ships a "Token Issuance Latency SLO – Current **p95**" panel in *dashboard JSON* — against a register and an ADR that both say **p99**. Two encodings of one objective, drifted the same way, in two media, neither detectable before a register existed to contradict them. That is the argument for the backfill: each unreconciled target is not one stale line but an unknown number of mutually-consistent-looking copies. The prose half was fixed in task 7; the JSON half is D7.
- [ ] **D9 — no commit-boundary assertion that planned files are tracked or staged; eleven green guards validated an artifact that would not have been committed (surfaced 2026-09-02 by @operations at Gate 3 of story task 7)**: at the end of task 7, `docs/observability/slos.md` — the central artifact of the task — was **untracked**, along with the devloop output directory. A `git commit -am` stages only modified *tracked* files, so it would have committed the eleven modified files and **silently dropped `slos.md`**. Closed for that commit with `git add -A`; nothing structural prevents a recurrence. **THE MECHANISM IS THE OPPOSITE OF A BLIND SPOT, AND THIS IS THE PART TO READ BEFORE PROPOSING A FIX.** The guards do not fail to see untracked files — they **deliberately include** them: `crates/dt-guard/src/common/git_changes.rs:132` documents the changed set as *"Union of [`get_modified_files`] + [`get_untracked_files`], deduplicated"*, implemented at `:139-140` (`modified.extend(untracked)`) over `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` at `:117-119`; `scripts/guards/common.sh:62` does the same on the bash side. So all eleven guards **saw `slos.md`, read it, validated its content and reported green** about a file that would have vanished at commit. `validate-cross-boundary-scope` stayed green *correctly*: the path was in the plan **and** in the guard's changed set, so planned-untouched drift rightly did not fire. **The green was the source of the false assurance, not absent from it** — the same false-green shape as the `dt-guard` path-roots entry in this section, where an empty result reads as success. **WRONG-FIX TRAP**: do **not** "make the guards check for untracked files". They already do, the inclusion is deliberate and correct for pre-commit linting, and removing it would break every guard's ability to validate new work. **Fix**: a separate assertion at the **commit boundary** — at Gate 2 or in `scripts/workflow/devloop-stop-hook.sh` — that every path named in the devloop plan's Cross-Boundary Classification table is **tracked or staged** (`git ls-files --error-unmatch`, or absent from `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`). Different control at a different lifecycle point; the guards themselves need no change. **Why it is worth a guard rather than a checklist line**: it generalises to *every* devloop that creates a file, and the failure is invisible to content review by construction — task 7 verified every citation, count and line number across seven review rounds while the central artifact sat untracked in plain sight in `git status` output. **Concrete counterfactual, which is the reason to prioritise it**: the outcome would not have been "a missing file". It would have been **eleven confident pointers asserting authority over a nonexistent path** — ADR-0011's amendment, `alerts.md`, both `dashboards.md` blocks, `gc-incident-response.md`, `mh-alerts.yaml` ×2, `API_CONTRACTS.md`, and the D7/D8 entries — which is **strictly worse than the `(to be created)` hedges that same commit retired**, because a hedge tells a reader the file is missing and a confident pointer does not. Owner: **infrastructure** or **test** (story-runner / commit-gate machinery, not metrics-guard infrastructure under ADR-0031) — deliberately routed away from observability, who found it but does not own the pipeline.

- [ ] **D10 — `failure_reason` carries a different bounded value set on MH than on GC/MC, so `sum by(failure_reason)` silently does not line up across services (surfaced 2026-09-02 by @observability during story task 8)**: the same label key on the same JWT-validation concept enumerates `none, signature_invalid, expired, missing_token, scope_mismatch, malformed` in `docs/observability/metrics/gc-service.md:408` and `docs/observability/metrics/mc-service.md:141`/`:581`, but `none, signature_invalid, expired, scope_mismatch, malformed, validation_failed` in `docs/observability/metrics/mh-service.md:135`. Both six-valued; they differ by one member (`missing_token` vs `validation_failed`). **This is a real service divergence, not doc drift** — verified against code rather than catalogs alone: `crates/mh-service/src/observability/metrics.rs:230-231` documents MH's set and `:361` emits `validation_failed`, so the catalogs are accurate and the services genuinely differ. **Consequence**: a cross-service panel or alert aggregating `sum by(failure_reason)` produces two disjoint series for what a reader takes to be one taxonomy, and the divergence is invisible on any single-service dashboard. `signature_invalid` — the token the whole fleet does agree on — masks the problem, because the value an operator most often looks at lines up. **Not a finding against story task 8**: pre-existing, discovered while checking the vectors' crypto reject-reason spellings against fleet spellings (criterion 12), and it never entered fix-or-defer. **Deliberately NOT folded into D4/D5**: those carry the media-path identity/oracle mechanism; this is label-value drift on a control-plane metric, a different mechanism, and merging them would muddy D4/D5's argument. **Action**: decide whether the two sets should converge (and if so which spelling wins — note `validation_failed` and `missing_token` are not synonyms, so this is a semantics question before it is a naming one) or whether the divergence is intentional and should be documented as such in all four catalog locations. Ties into the existing "Label-value drift is unguarded on every surface" entry below, which is the mechanism that would have caught this. Owner: observability, with auth-controller/global-controller/meeting-controller/media-handler as per-service ratifiers.

- [ ] **Guard path roots are unasserted inputs, and where every consumer reads "empty" as success the guard goes silently green (found 2026-09-01 by @observability at Gate 1 of `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-01-internal-contract-reshape/`, self-audit prompted by @security's dead-GSA-glob finding; owner: observability per ADR-0031 "Guard infrastructure for metrics/dashboards/alerts")**: every path root in the observability-owned guards is a hardcoded constant that is never asserted to exist; each extractor early-returns an empty set on a missing directory. Whether that is safe depends entirely on **consumer polarity** — whether some consumer treats an empty result as a *failure*. Two sites have no such consumer and are the load-bearing instances: (a) `crates/dt-guard/src/application_metrics.rs:176` (`ALERTS_SUBDIR` = `infra/docker/prometheus/rules`) feeds only check 4 ("alert-rule metrics exist in source code"), so an empty set means "nothing to validate" and alert-rule validation stops happening, green; (b) `crates/dt-guard/src/kustomize.rs:145` returns zero hits when `infra/grafana/dashboards` is not a dir **or** `infra/grafana/kustomization.yaml` is not a file — OR-gated on two inputs, one of them a single file (likelier to be renamed than a directory), silencing a *bidirectional* coverage check in both directions at once, with both paths as inline literals rather than named constants. Three further roots are polarity-safe today and should get the assertion anyway for uniformity: `application_metrics.rs:116` (`DASHBOARDS_SUBDIR`, saved by check 5 reading empty as "every metric undashboarded"), `application_metrics.rs:66` (`CATALOG_SUBDIR`, saved by check 6 reading empty as "every metric undocumented"), and `metric_coverage.rs:69` (`tests_dir`). **Fix — one predicate, and it is joint with @security's half**: a guard's path roots are *inputs* and must be asserted present; "directory absent" is a hard error, never an empty result set. Twelve call sites across the guard crate; fourteen more in the GSA canon (see the `.proto`-scanner and dead-glob entries under §"From ADR-0024 §6 Amendment" — same mechanism, and that half is **live** where this half is **latent**, so schedule theirs first). **Two in-tree precedents to copy rather than a principle to argue from**: `crates/dt-guard/src/metric_coverage.rs:66-67` documents *why* its empty case is safe ("caller treats this as a per-service uncovered signal"), and `crates/dt-guard/src/alert_rules.rs:260-262` returns an **error** when the runbooks dir cannot be resolved. The right answer has been in the same crate the whole time; it simply never generalised. **Enumeration is PARTIAL and the bound is stated so a later reader does not treat it as exhaustive**: these five were found by grepping one idiom, `if !x.is_dir() { return ... }`. Sites using `exists()`, `try_exists()`, a `match` on the read result, or `let Ok(..) else` are invisible to that grep and were not assessed. Same class as the "control checks the wrong target set" family already recorded in this section. Task-sized: shared gate tooling with its own `.test.sh` and fixtures, not foldable into a feature devloop. Defer trigger: the next dt-guard metric-guard devloop, or @security's `.proto`-scanner work, whichever lands first.

- [ ] **Top-line `TOTAL_RESULT=N/A` on a fully-green run is not self-describing** (surfaced 2026-08-20 during the validation-run-all devloop review; **pre-existing aggregator behavior, NOT introduced by that diff** — but that diff promotes it from intermittent to the common case). `layer-all.sh`'s top-line `TOTAL_RESULT` is the worst-child over per-layer results, and `N/A` ranks **above** `OK` in the `__status_rank` ladder (rank 4 > rank 3) — deliberately, so a real documented-gap N/A is never masked by an OK sibling. Consequence at the top line: a clean run where Layer 4 aggregates `N/A` (proto's `test.sh` placeholder emits `not-applicable-to-this-lang`) and Layer 6 aggregates `N/A` (rust/ts audit `SKIPPED-NO-DIFF no-dep-changes` + proto `N/A`) produces `TOTAL_RESULT=N/A` even though everything that ran passed. **Why this change matters here**: with the skip-if-untouched short-circuit retired (2026-08-20), every layer runs every language on every task, so a no-dep-change task now *reliably* shows L4=N/A + L6=N/A → `TOTAL_RESULT=N/A` on essentially every green run, where before it was intermittent. The **exit code is still 0** (`N/A`→exit 0 via `status_to_exit_code`), so gating is correct — this is purely a top-line-label legibility defect: an operator glancing at `TOTAL_RESULT=N/A` cannot distinguish "clean pass" from "nothing ran / real gap." **Proposed fix**: collapse the *top line only* to `OK` when every contributing child is ∈{`OK`,`N/A`,`SKIPPED-*`} with at least one `OK` (i.e. the aggregate is a success-exit class with real work done), leaving the per-layer `LAYER=n RESULT=…` lines and `__status_rank` worst-wins semantics untouched (those must keep N/A>OK to avoid masking mid-pipeline). **Blast radius**: touches the top-line emit in `layer-all.sh` + must be reconciled with `status_to_exit_code` and every consumer that greps `TOTAL_RESULT=` (CI summary jobs, run-story gate telemetry); needs its own design cycle + hermetic cases in `layer-all.test.sh`. Deliberately out of scope for the validation-run-all devloop (own design decision, own test cycle). Owner: observability.

  **AMENDED 2026-09-09** (@infrastructure + @operations, at Gate 3 of `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-09-web-app-in-meeting-loopback/`). The entry above is accurate, but its **proposed fix is superseded** and would not fix the defect as now understood.

  **Observed, not predicted.** On that devloop's Gate-2 run, Layer 6 went `FAIL` -> **`N/A`** once the `fast-uri` advisory cleared: proto's `audit.sh` intentional-gap placeholder permanently N/As Layer 6 exactly as proto's `test.sh` does Layer 4, and the `FAIL` had merely been outranking it. Layer 4 reported `RESULT=N/A` on a run with 392 rust tests / 0 failed and every TS suite green. The Lead confirmed the tests genuinely passed only by reading the children's own `STATUS=` lines -- the manual step the contract exists to remove.

  **The hazard was recognised in ADR-0033 twice, and dodged twice.** `adr-0033:172` routes dep-gated audits to `SKIPPED-NO-DIFF` and says so in terms: "**not** N/A, which ranks above OK in `aggregate_worst_status` and would mask a passing layer". `adr-0033:273` routes the CI no-cluster lane to `SKIPPED-NO-CLUSTER`, "and NOT `N/A` (which ranks ABOVE `OK` and would wrongly dominate CI's total)". Both escapes worked because those cases are genuinely *skips*, with a below-`OK` enum available. **An intentional-gap placeholder is a true "does not apply" and has nowhere to go**, so the hazard the ADR twice steered around has landed in the one place it could not. `adr-0033:149` records the placeholder as intended design without noting that it permanently N/As the layer.

  **Scope, stated so this is not over-claimed**: this is a **legibility and detection-erosion** defect, **not** masked failure in the gating sense. `N/A` -> exit 0, and `FAIL` (rank 5) still outranks `N/A` (rank 4), so **no red is hidden today**. The harm is prospective: a verdict channel that always reads the same carries no information, so a future aggregation regression is indistinguishable from the steady state.

  **The harm is prescriptive, not incidental.** `.claude/skills/devloop/SKILL.md:387` instructs every Lead to "Read the `TOTAL_RESULT=` line in the `LAYER_SUMMARY` block for the verdict, not any single layer, and not a wrapper's exit status." The one line designated authoritative is the line that cannot express success while a placeholder exists. And the desensitisation is written into the operations-owned contract as expected behaviour: in `docs/runbooks/devloop-validation.md`, the Layer-4 and Layer-6 placeholder rows state it as **Expected** in the `Cause / Fix` remediation column (the table header is `REASON token | Wrapper | Cause / Fix` -- there is no column headed "Expected"), a worked example and its commentary reproduce the same aggregate as normal, and the exit-class table places `N/A` in the success-exit class. The Layer-4 row states the defect in the tree's own words: *"N/A ranks above OK, so a clean Layer 4 with proto touched aggregates to `N/A` (still exit 0)."* A responder who reads the runbook correctly and concludes "nothing is wrong" has done everything right.

  **Superseded fix.** The top-line-only collapse proposed above explicitly preserves the per-layer lines and `__status_rank`, so `LAYER=4 RESULT=N/A` survives on every green run. A reader who implements it sees `TOTAL_RESULT=OK`, believes this entry closed, and leaves the per-layer defect live.

  **Replacement fix -- split the enum, do not re-rank it.** Re-ranking `N/A` to neutral would reintroduce the masking the rank exists to prevent for an *unexpected* N/A (a wrapper that should not be N/A, hidden by a sibling's `OK`) -- the residual `FAIL-MISSING-VERB` was created to close (`adr-0033:257`). The pipeline's established move when one enum carries two meanings is to split it: task #52 split `FAIL-MISSING-VERB` out of `SKIPPED-NO-VERB`; task #56 added `SKIPPED-NO-CLUSTER` + `PRECONDITION_FAILURE`. Same medicine: a distinct enum for documented intentional-gap placeholders, ranked **at the bottom of the band, below `SKIPPED-NO-VERB`**, with bare `N/A` keeping its above-`OK` rank for the unexpected case. Renumber the band up by one rather than inserting a fractional rank.

  **The sub-rank is NOT the load-bearing part** (@operations, and this is recorded so it is not relitigated): every enum below `OK` is exit 0 and `OK` dominates the whole band, so the sub-rank changes output only in a layer where *every* child is in the band. "Below `OK`" is the entire load-bearing decision and is settled by the masking argument above -- **that must not move.** Bottom placement follows from the rule the band already encodes, how informative the state is about *this run*: a per-run skip varies and tells you something new, whereas an intentional-gap placeholder is a permanent structural property of the repository, identical on every run, carrying zero bits about the run in front of you. Surfacing the invariant over the variable would be a small-scale replay of this very defect.

  **Blast radius -- cross-owner, not infrastructure-alone.** Machinery + ADR (**infrastructure**): `scripts/lang/_common.sh` `__status_rank` and its precedence comment, the ADR-0033 exit-code table and STATUS enum list, hermetic cases in `layer-all.test.sh`. Runbook surface (**operations**): in `docs/runbooks/devloop-validation.md`, the exit-class table, the enum/REASON table, the printed rank ladder, the intuition paragraph, and the four placeholder/worked-example rows. **Two mirrors must be fixed, and they are not the same risk.** The intuition paragraph announces itself as a copy of the `_common.sh` comment, so a careful editor knows to check it. The printed rank ladder carries the integers inline (`... OK (3) < N/A (4) < FAIL (5) ...`) and presents as a diagram: a renumber leaves its shape correct and only its numbers wrong, so it still reads as authoritative while contradicting the code. Name it separately -- if only the intuition paragraph is updated, the ladder becomes a printed reference that disagrees with the ranks it claims to document. Prefer collapsing both to a citation of the code (the direction `docs/runbooks/client-dev-local.md` Step 0 already uses for `dev-web.sh`'s check list) over updating them in place.

  **Owners**: filer **observability** (unchanged); **infrastructure** for the machinery and the ADR amendment; **operations** for the runbook surface. The `TOTAL_RESULT`-as-verdict observation is the Lead's, from that devloop's unattended `layer-all.sh` run.

Add a cross-service overview: a curated RED-method top line (rate / errors / duration per service) + key business SLIs (meetings active, join success rate, participants active) + optionally the most important client metrics (see the client-governance entry below). Two design constraints: (a) **ownership is cross-cutting → observability-owned**, NOT any single service — ADR-0031 makes per-service dashboards service-owned, but a system overview crosses boundaries; (b) **curate, don't dump**, and avoid drift from the per-service panels (share the query source or treat it as an explicit curated derived view). - [ ] **Client metrics have plumbing but no governance — dashboards, alarms, AND a coverage guard all missing (ADR-0032 analog for the client); needs a `/debate`**: the GC telemetry proxy (R-2: `POST /api/v1/telemetry/v1/{metrics,traces}`) and its proxy-side ingest metrics (#16: `gc_telemetry_ingest_total` etc.) exist, but the client metrics that flow *through* it have **no Grafana dashboards, no alerts, and — critically — no coverage guard**. Service metrics are governed by ADR-0032 (every metric must have a test + dashboard + catalog entry, enforced by `validate-application-metrics` / metric-coverage guards); the client has none of that machinery. When the deferred client-metrics catalog is built out (browser-client-join stubbed it), without a guard client metrics will drift into the exact silent-failure state ADR-0032 fixed for services — a browser-emitted metric with no dashboard/alert/test, invisible until an incident. **Not a copy of the Rust guard**: client metrics travel a different path (browser → GC proxy → OTel collector → Prometheus, not a service scrape) and live in TS, so the guard must be telemetry-path-aware and `ts`-lang-aware (ties into the ADR-0033 polyglot pipeline — the `ts` lang wants its own metric-coverage guard). Needs a `/debate` (cross-cutting: observability + client + infrastructure + polyglot-guard) to set the client-metric governance pattern, mirroring ADR-0032. Owner: observability + client + infrastructure. Surfaced 2026-08-08.

- [ ] **MC emits no log event on the `MediaConnectionUpdate` success path — `statuses_count` is unreachable from logs at any `RUST_LOG` (browser-client-join Task #20 → MC observability)**: `handle_media_connection_update` (`crates/mc-service/src/webtransport/connection.rs:663-724`) carries `#[instrument(name = "mc.media_connection_update", fields(connection_id, statuses_count = update.statuses.len()))]`, but emits **no event on the success path** — its only log is a `debug!` on the actor-gone error branch (`:715-721`), which is itself invisible under the deployed `RUST_LOG=info,mc_service=debug` because the target `mc.webtransport.connection` does not prefix-match `mc_service`. Since `tracing_subscriber::fmt::layer().json()` (`crates/mc-service/src/main.rs:120`) writes one line per **event** and no `.with_span_events(...)` is configured, the span exists only as context on events that never occur. **Consequence**: `statuses_count` — the per-join media fan-out width, and the single richest completeness datum MC has — cannot be read from logs at any log level. The `mc_participant_mh_status_total{state}` counter (`crates/mc-service/src/actors/participant.rs:478`) is the only available substitute, and it is strictly weaker: it increments *inside* the per-entry loop, so an **empty** fan-out produces no increment at all and is indistinguishable from "the client never sent an update" — precisely the case (GC returns empty `media_servers`, client still reaches `joined`, MC still logs `Join succeeded`) that most needs an observable. **Action**: add an `info!` on the success path of `handle_media_connection_update` carrying `statuses_count` (and `connection_id`), target `mc.webtransport.connection` so it is visible at the deployed `info` global. ~3 LoC; the span field already computes the value. Then update `docs/runbooks/client-dev-local.md` §4.2, which currently documents the counter-delta workaround and explicitly warns readers **not** to reach for the span field — that warning can be removed once the event exists. Owner: observability (with meeting-controller — the edit is in MC's WebTransport connection handler). Surfaced 2026-07-29 during task #20 by @observability: the runbook draft cited a `jq` filter on the span name as "the completeness signal", which returns empty output on a healthy join — a phantom signal in a document that trains readers to treat absence as evidence. Caught at review; the runbook now uses the counter delta.

- [ ] **TS metric emission policy — Case A vs Case B (ADR-0033 follow-up)**: ADR-0033 (Polyglot Validation Pipeline) is silent on whether the TypeScript client emits its own application metrics (Case B — browser RUM / OpenTelemetry web SDK to a collector) or is purely a metrics consumer that reports server-side via API (Case A — server emits, no TS-side metric guards needed). The decision drives whether `validate-metric-coverage.sh` and `validate-application-metrics.sh` need to extend to TS file globs and whether ADR-0032's presence-guard pattern generalizes to TS. (The former sub-question "whether `lang/ts/changed.sh` should treat metric-emission sites specially" is moot as of 2026-08-20 — `changed.sh` was retired, ADR-0033 §2/§3.) **Action**: needs its own ADR or design discussion before client telemetry tasks (R-19, R-24, R-25, R-26, R-27 in browser-client-join story) land. Surfaced 2026-05-06 by observability in ADR-0033 Round 1.

- [ ] **MH Kind-overlay `OTEL_ENABLED=true` patch + MH→otel-collector egress NetworkPolicy rule deferred (browser-client-join Task #27 → MH R-55 dev enablement)**: Task #27 wired MH's `init_otel` + the four ConfigMap keys (mirroring AC task #25's shape — see `infra/services/ac-service/configmap.yaml` + `infra/kubernetes/overlays/kind/services/ac-service/configmap-otel-patch.yaml`), but deliberately did NOT add MH's counterpart of the two pieces AC also shipped: (a) a Kind-overlay strategic-merge patch flipping `OTEL_ENABLED` to `"true"` for dev (`infra/kubernetes/overlays/kind/services/mh-service/` has no `configmap-otel-patch.yaml` today), and (b) an MH-egress → otel-collector:4317 rule in `infra/services/mh-service/network-policy.yaml` (today's egress list covers GC/MC/AC/DNS only). Task #27's own instructions scoped only the base ConfigMap; the overlay+netpol pair was called out as likely-in-scope-for-AC-only during planning and confirmed out of scope at Gate 1. **Hazard if skipped when someone else flips `OTEL_ENABLED=true`**: `init_otel`'s eager collector probe (fail-hard at init, `crates/common/src/observability/otel.rs`) would CrashLoop the MH pod on every restart until the egress rule is added — default-deny NetworkPolicy blocks the OTLP-gRPC connect. **Action**: add both pieces together (never `OTEL_ENABLED=true` without the egress rule already merged) once MC's R-57/R-55 (task #6) and GC's R-55 (task #26) reach the same state, so dev-cluster OTel enablement lands once, consistently, across all four services rather than piecemeal per-service Kind drift. Owner: media-handler + operations. Surfaced 2026-07-03 (task #27) per Gate-1 directive 5 (operations + observability). **Update 2026-07-05 (task #6)**: MC's counterpart pair LANDED — `infra/kubernetes/overlays/kind/services/mc-service/configmap-otel-patch.yaml` (flips `OTEL_ENABLED=true` for dev, wired into that overlay's `kustomization.yaml`) + the MC→otel-collector `:4317` egress rule in `infra/services/mc-service/network-policy.yaml`. So AC (#25) and MC (#6) now both ship the full base+overlay+netpol trio; MH (#27) remains the only service missing the overlay patch + egress rule (this entry's original gap stands for MH). **Update 2026-08-28 (env-config guard devloop) — MH's four base ConfigMap keys were REMOVED, so this entry is now the sole home of the MH OTel re-add recipe.** Why removed rather than kept: they were referenced by neither MH deployment (per-key `configMapKeyRef`, no `envFrom`), so they were never delivered to a pod — misleading rather than merely dead. Behaviourally a no-op: `crates/mh-service/src/config.rs` reads all four as optional-with-defaults identical to the removed values, pinned by `test_otel_defaults` (OTel off by default). Surfaced by the `dt-guard env-config` coverage fix, which had never checked mh-service at all.
  **The four keys, verbatim, for `infra/services/mh-service/configmap.yaml` `data:`** — `OTEL_ENABLED: "false"`, `OTLP_ENDPOINT: "http://otel-collector.dark-tower:4317"`, `OTEL_SAMPLE_RATE: "1.0"`, `DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT: "development"`.
  **Semantics that would otherwise be lost with the deleted comment block**: (a) enablement is an EXPLICIT BOOLEAN `OTEL_ENABLED`, NOT presence of `OTLP_ENDPOINT` — a populated endpoint with `OTEL_ENABLED` unset/false stays OFF (`init_otel` is never called, no layer composed); (b) the `http://` scheme is REQUIRED on `OTLP_ENDPOINT` (parsed via tonic `Endpoint::from_shared`; a bare `host:port` fails at init); (c) `OTEL_SAMPLE_RATE` is a head-sampling ratio in `[0.0, 1.0]` whose range has a SINGLE owner, `init_otel` — MH's config side is PARSE-ONLY and must not regrow a range check; (d) `DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT` is the ADR-0011 `deployment.environment` resource attribute, and the prod-mistag caveat in the AC+GC entry above re-attaches to MH on re-add.
  **Action — three ORDERED steps. Do not reorder; each step's hazard is created by the one before it.** **(1)** Re-add the four keys to the base ConfigMap **AND** add the four matching `configMapKeyRef` env entries to BOTH `mh-0-deployment.yaml` and `mh-1-deployment.yaml` (mirror `infra/services/ac-service/statefulset.yaml`'s OTel block). Re-adding the ConfigMap keys ALONE is inert and recreates exactly the orphan state this update removed — that omission IS the original bug. **(2)** Add the MH→otel-collector `:4317` egress rule to `infra/services/mh-service/network-policy.yaml` (today's egress allowlist covers GC/MC/AC/DNS only). **(3)** ONLY THEN create `infra/kubernetes/overlays/kind/services/mh-service/configmap-otel-patch.yaml` flipping `OTEL_ENABLED: "true"` **and** add the `patches:` stanza to that overlay's `kustomization.yaml` — it has NO `patches:` stanza at all today, unlike ac/gc/mc, so creating the patch file alone is a silent no-op. **Two distinct CrashLoops guard this order.** Doing (3) before (1): a Kustomize strategic merge on a ConfigMap is ADDITIVE, so patching `OTEL_ENABLED: "true"` against a base that lacks the key does NOT error — it CREATES it, MH starts with `OTEL_ENABLED=true` and an empty `OTLP_ENDPOINT`, and trips the cross-field validation in `crates/mh-service/src/config.rs` (`InvalidOtelConfig`: "OTEL_ENABLED=true requires a non-empty OTLP_ENDPOINT"). Doing (3) before (2): `init_otel` probes the collector eagerly and FAILS HARD at startup, and default-deny NetworkPolicy blocks the OTLP-gRPC connect, so the pod CrashLoops on every restart. AC (#25) and MC (#6) are the two worked examples of the completed trio.

- [ ] **R-26 bounded client join LOGS — emission deferred from Task #14 (browser-client-join, PATH B)**: Task #14 wired the five `dt_client_*` join METRICS (R-24/R-25) at their `MeetingSession.join` / `MediaTransport.connectAll` emission sites, but the R-26 bounded join LOGS (`logJoinEvent`/`JoinEvent`/`JoinLogRecord`, scaffolded in `packages/sdk-core/src/telemetry/logger.ts`) are NOT emitted yet. **Root cause (@observability §3, corrected framing)**: the 7 R-26 events span the WHOLE join lifecycle — `join.started`/`signup_complete`/`gc_token_received` all fire inside `MeetingSession.join` BEFORE `SignalingClient` even exists — but the only `dt_client.join` span is created INSIDE `SignalingClient.join`, so it covers only the signaling sub-portion. There is therefore NO single consistent `trace_id` across all 7 events. A read-only getter on SignalingClient does NOT fix this (the early MeetingSession events still have no span, and correlating some events but not others is worse than a clean defer). The only correct fix is the DESIGN DECISION to relocate the `dt_client.join` ROOT span to `MeetingSession.join` (signaling span becomes a child), which touches task #13 span semantics and warrants its own planning. The metric labels' `meeting_id_hash` (SHA-256 via `crypto.subtle.digest`) computed in THIS task is reusable for the log record, so the follow-up is span/trace_id wiring only. **Action**: (a) relocate the `dt_client.join` root span to `MeetingSession.join` so one trace_id roots the whole join; (b) make SignalingClient's signaling span a child; (c) emit `logJoinEvent` across all 7 `JoinEvent` states from `MeetingSession.join`. Owner: client (with observability). Surfaced 2026-06-29 (task #14); deferral accepted by @observability, scope split locked by @team-lead at Gate-1 (PATH B).
