## Input Validation

- [ ] **AC: Validate displayName at registration**: `users.display_name` is `NOT NULL` but nothing rejects empty or degenerate values at the registration boundary, so `""` (or `" "`, or a single character) flows legally through AC's fail-closed meeting-token minting (`resolve_meeting_display_name` — which correctly refuses only *missing* users, not empty names) into MC's roster broadcast and renders blank in every participant's UI. Non-empty alone is likely insufficient: at implementation time, determine a reasonable minimum length (post-trim; consider what the roster UX and abuse surface actually need — e.g. ≥2 visible characters), enforce it in the registration handler with a clear 400, mirror the constraint client-side in the SignUp form for immediate feedback, and add the negative registration test. Surfaced 2026-08-06 while tracing display-name plumbing for story task #65 (MC drops the claim; the empty-string edge is AC's half of the invariant). Owner: auth-controller.

- [ ] **Only ONE gRPC ingress in the tree states its decode bound; the other three inherit tonic's implicit default, so a dependency-default change is caught in one service and silent in three (surfaced 2026-09-02 by @dry-reviewer at Gate 3 of `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-02-mh-register-meeting-policy-apply/`, confirmed and scoped by @security; owner: security + infrastructure)**: that devloop added `MediaHandlerServiceServer::new(...).max_decoding_message_size(MAX_GRPC_DECODING_BYTES)` at `crates/mh-service/src/main.rs`, with the correct reason — `RegisterMeetingRequest` grew two unbounded repeated fields, the decoder is the OUTERMOST allocation bound on that path (`PolicyLimits` only applies once a message is already decoded into memory), and tonic's default merely *happens* to be 4 MiB, so stating it stops a tonic bump silently widening the surface. `grep -rn max_decoding_message_size crates/` returns exactly that one hit: MC's, GC's and AC's servers are all still implicit. **The reasoning MH's comment gives applies verbatim to every other ingress, and after this diff only one of them is protected by it.** Confirmed sibling exposure: `proto/dark_tower/internal/v1/internal.proto::AssignMeetingWithMhRequest.mh_assignments` is a repeated field on a GC->MC inbound message served by `MeetingControllerService`. It is **pre-existing and ADR-0010-era, NOT introduced by the 2026-09-01 reshape** — which makes it worse rather than better, since it has sat unexamined rather than arriving with a change someone reviewed. (The reshape's own repeated fields are both MC->MH, i.e. the path already hardened.)
  **THE FIX IS PER-SERVICE EXPLICIT VALUES PLUS A GUARD — NOT a shared `common::MAX_GRPC_DECODING_BYTES`, and this is stated first because the natural reading of "only one service has it" is "hoist it".** 4 MiB is not a tuned figure; it is tonic's default restated so a bump cannot move it silently, and that is the whole content of MH's line. A shared constant would assert something stronger and false — that four services with different inbound message shapes should share one allocation budget (MH's control plane carries forwarding policy bounded at 512x16; MC's carries MH assignments; AC's carries token requests). The first person with a legitimate reason to tune one would fork the constant, recreating the drift the hoist was meant to prevent, or move all four for a reason that applies to one. That is a false SSoT: two things that look like one value but are not one decision. What genuinely has a single home is **the requirement that every gRPC ingress state its bound explicitly**, and that is machinery, not a constant — a `dt-guard` check that a `Server::builder()` chain adding a service also sets `max_decoding_message_size`. A guard holds the property under a tonic bump, under a new service, and under someone tuning one value; a shared const holds it under none of those. Per CLAUDE.md's guard-crate split, the check's implementation is **infrastructure**'s and the policy content — which ingresses are in scope, what the floor is — is **security**'s.
  **Why not fixed in the originating devloop**: three other service crates, each needing its own value decision, plus guard machinery owned by a different specialist. Cross-service coordination well past any single media-path task. It is also **not a finding against that diff on the merits** — that diff is the one service that got it right, and penalising the first hardening for being the only one is backwards. **Defer trigger**: the next devloop touching any of `crates/{mc,gc,ac}-service/src/main.rs`'s server construction, or a tonic major bump.

## Media Path Obligations (ADR-0036 frame v2)

- [ ] **The MC→MH control channel that now carries a ROUTING AUTHORITY is plaintext HTTP/2 with no authentication of the MC peer; MH also transmits its own OAuth service token over it (filed 2026-09-08 by @security as S6 at Gate 3 of `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-05-sender-id-binding-contract/`; owners: infrastructure + operations + security)**: story task 24 made `NotifyParticipantConnectedResponse.sender_id` load-bearing — MH binds a media route on the strength of a value in that response body (`crates/mh-service/src/webtransport/connection.rs::resolve_sender_binding`). **The direction that matters is MH→MC and back, and only one half of it is authenticated.** MC authenticates MH: `McAuthLayer` validates a JWKS-signed service token and enforces scope `service.write.mc` (`crates/mc-service/src/grpc/auth_interceptor.rs`). **MH does not authenticate MC at all.** MH dials whatever string arrived as `RegisterMeetingRequest.mc_grpc_endpoint`, and that string is `http://$(POD_IP):50052` — cleartext, no TLS, therefore no server certificate and no peer identity (`infra/services/mc-service/mc-0-deployment.yaml`, `MC_GRPC_ADVERTISE_ADDRESS`; dialled at `crates/mh-service/src/grpc/mc_client.rs::try_send` via `Endpoint::from_shared`). **Two consequences, and the second is the one usually missed.** (1) Anything that can occupy that address—port answers MH's binding question, and MH binds the ordinal it is given — an on-path cross-participant media-crossing primitive. (2) `add_auth` attaches MH's live OAuth **service token in cleartext** on every one of those calls, so the same position that can forge a binding also harvests a `service.write.mc` credential. **The control that exists today is network topology only** — `infra/services/{mc,mh}-service/network-policy.yaml` restricts MC↔MH gRPC to 50052/50053 between those pods. That is a real control and it is why this is filed rather than escalated, but it is **network isolation plus an MC-attested endpoint, NOT a cryptographically authenticated peer**, and the difference is exactly what an ADR-0003 §5.7 reader would assume the other way. **Where the tree is already honest about this, and must stay so**: `proto/dark_tower/internal/v1/internal.proto` at `rpc NotifyParticipantConnected` ("NOTHING IN THIS EXCHANGE ESTABLISHES THAT"), and `MHMediaSenderBindingOutOfRange`'s annotation in `infra/docker/prometheus/rules/mh-alerts.yaml` ("the MC->MH gRPC channel has no cryptographic peer authentication, so this counter is the only signal separating those two causes"). **THERE IS NO WORKING DETECTOR FOR THIS TODAY, AND THE SENTENCE ABOVE IS NOT ONE.** Two independent reasons, and the first was found by @operations at Gate 3 of this same devloop, after this entry was first written: (1) **CORRECTED 2026-09-09 (story task 21): alert rules ARE now evaluated, by the authoritative cluster Prometheus — `infra/kubernetes/observability/prometheus.yml` (the server config, extracted to a real file and generated with a content hash) mounted by the Deployment in `prometheus-config.yaml`.** The superseded original text read: *"no Prometheus in this tree evaluates any alert rule at all — `rule_files:` is commented out at `infra/docker/prometheus/prometheus.yml`, and the commented glob points at a directory and extension the rules do not use, so `MHMediaSenderBindingOutOfRange` is inert rather than quiet."* **Every clause of that is now false**: `rule_files:` is active in both configs with the glob `rules/[a-z]*-alerts.yaml`. It is QUOTED rather than left inline because an earlier attempt at this correction left the remnant running on unquoted and in the PRESENT TENSE, where "`rule_files:` is commented out ... **so** ... QUIET, NOT INERT" drew the opposite conclusion from its own premise — a commented-out `rule_files` is exactly what makes a rule inert. So, currently: `MHMediaSenderBindingOutOfRange` is **QUIET, NOT INERT** — the rule is loaded and evaluating, and reads zero because nothing has tripped it. **This changes nothing about the ceiling below.** (see the alerting-chain entry in §Observability Debt, which must not be closed in isolation from this one). (2) Even once it evaluates, it fires **only on an out-of-range answer**: a forged binding inside `1..=65535` is indistinguishable from a real one at MH, so the counter is the *ceiling* of the detection story rather than coverage of impersonation. Do not read the alert's existence, or its annotation's confident wording, as a compensating control. **Fix when acted on**: mTLS on the MC↔MH gRPC channel (MH verifies MC's certificate; MC keeps its existing token check), which requires the advertise address to become `https://`, a cert/SAN scheme for pod-IP-addressed peers, and a rollout ordering of its own — task-sized infrastructure work with an operations rollout half, not an inline edit. Second-choice interim if mTLS is deferred: pin the dialled endpoint against the MC identity `RegisterMeeting` was authenticated as, so a substituted address is refused rather than dialled. **Defer trigger**: the next devloop touching MC↔MH transport configuration or `MC_GRPC_ADVERTISE_ADDRESS`, ADR-0003 §5.7 revision, or any change that would make a forged binding survive MH's range check undetected. **Explicitly NOT this devloop's to fix** — task 24 owed only the honest trust statement at the proto field and the reject arms, and that statement landed.

- [ ] **`dt_client_media_frames_received_total`'s counting point must move from the TRANSPORT boundary to the PARSE boundary when video lands, and the accounting identity must be re-established there (owner: client; TRIGGER: story 3, video; filed 2026-09-08 at story task 19)**: today one datagram is one frame, so counting at the wire — the first statement of the datagram loop, before any parse — makes `received = accepted + sum(drops by reason)` exact by construction. **Video breaks that**: ADR-0036 §1 carries video on unidirectional QUIC streams, one group of pictures per stream, so SEVERAL FRAMES SHARE ONE STREAM and a transport-boundary count no longer counts frames at all. The counting point moves to the parse boundary and the identity is re-established there. **Why this is filed rather than left in a code comment**: the comment lives in `packages/sdk-core/src/media/pipeline/ingress.ts`, which the video author has no reason to open before deciding where to count; the durable homes are this entry and the `docs/observability/metrics/client.md` §Media-path metrics identity block, which both state it. **Carries a second, smaller correction with it.** `docs/user-stories/2026-08-27-hear-yourself-through-handler.md:53` was corrected in place at task 19 with an additive clause recording that the emitted term is `accepted`, not `played`, and that the identity holds at the crypto/parse boundary and not at the playback boundary. **Line 268 of the same file repeats the `played` phrasing in a forward-looking Story-3 sentence and was deliberately NOT swept** — it is the same sentence for the same future reader, so its correction belongs with whoever moves the counting point rather than as a second, separate edit now.
- [ ] **quinn's datagram RECEIVE buffer is roughly HALF MH's own ingress ring, so quinn sheds first and invisibly — which makes `mh_media_frames_dropped_total{reason="ingress_queue_overflow"}` look STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE in production, and leaves ADR-0036 §1's bind-first principle enforced on egress and violated on ingress (owner: `media-handler` for the ordering, `operations` as the consumer whose alert cannot fire; found 2026-09-08 by @operations at Gate 1 of `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-08-mh-datagram-receive-path-gap/`, arithmetic re-derived independently by the implementer and the unreachability claim seconded by @code-reviewer; trigger: the next touch of `DATAGRAM_RECEIVE_BUFFER_BYTES` or `INGRESS_QUEUE_FRAMES`)**: `DATAGRAM_RECEIVE_BUFFER_BYTES` is 2048 B (`crates/mh-service/src/config.rs`) against a `NOMINAL_AUDIO_FRAME_BYTES` of 236 B — **≈8.7 frames, ≈174 ms** of quinn-side absorption. `INGRESS_QUEUE_FRAMES` is **16**, and its own doc comment claims "~320 ms of ingest backlog, far beyond any healthy scheduling gap". **Under scheduling pressure quinn therefore evicts before MH's ring ever reaches its bound.**

  **Three consequences, and the first is the one that makes this worth doing.** (1) `ingress_queue_overflow` is a counter that exists and cannot fire — the same objection `crates/mh-service/src/media/ingress.rs`'s own module doc makes for loop C ("the counter would exist and be untestable, which ADR-0036's coverage rule treats as worse than absent"), and the same lesson as the `StreamRateLimited` token. (2) The documented "~320 ms" absorption is fiction; real absorption is ~174 ms, set by a constant chosen for an unrelated reason — clearing the max-Opus-frame floor. Nobody picked 174 ms. (3) `config.rs`'s `ConfigError::EgressQueueDoesNotBindFirst` enforces exactly this ordering on the **egress** side (`MH_DATAGRAM_BUFFER_AUDIO_FRAMES` must strictly exceed `EGRESS_QUEUE_FRAMES`, so MH's own queue trips first and back-pressure is countable in MH's code rather than silently discarded inside quinn) and the ingress side has **no counterpart**. That variant is the model for the missing check.

  **Two independent derivations agree, which is the strongest evidence in that devloop.** @operations computed 8.7 frames from the constants; the implementer measured ~7 survivors on the live Kind cluster (60 datagrams sent on one connection, 47 accounted). The gap closes once datagram encapsulation overhead is included. Carry both — one route alone invites the next reader to dismiss it as arithmetic.

  **Why it was FILED rather than fixed in the devloop that found it.** The remedy moves `DATAGRAM_RECEIVE_BUFFER_BYTES`, and quinn derives the advertised `max_datagram_frame_size` from that same field — so it is a **wire-visible negotiated-limit change**, not an internal tuning knob, and it deserves its own planning with an old-client/new-MH story. **Note what does and does not change this**: `mh_media_frames_dropped_total{reason="transport_receive_dropped"}`, landed at story task 26, makes the shed VISIBLE for the first time. It does not fix the inversion. This stays a config-and-validation question.

- [ ] **MH has NO DETECTIVE signal for silent ingress media loss — only a forensic one — and closing that needs exactly ONE new series, because the other half already exists (owner: `observability` with `media-handler`; filed 2026-09-08 at Gate 1 of `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-08-mh-datagram-receive-path-gap/`, shape found by @observability, operational stake stated by @operations; trigger: the next media-observability task, or the first incident where audio is silently lost mid-meeting)**: `mh_media_frames_dropped_total{reason="transport_receive_dropped"}` is computed by differencing quinn's received-datagram count against what the ingress loop read, and that difference is only final **at connection teardown**. Meetings run for an hour, so during a live incident nothing increments: the counter describes an incident that has already ended.

  **The closure is much smaller than it looks.** The *accounted* side is already live and queryable at any instant — `forwarded{direction="ingress"} + dropped{direction="ingress"}` is what the ingress loop read, and `forward.rs` keeps that sum whole deliberately (its `NoSubscriber` branch increments `forwarded{ingress}` before its egress-direction drop for exactly this reason). **The only missing term is the received total**: `mh_media_datagrams_received_total`, a periodic sum of `quinn::Connection::stats().frame_rx.datagram` over live connections. The live silent-loss rate is then a PromQL subtraction of two series, one of which is already published.

  **Why it is not free, and therefore correctly deferred.** It is a new metric NAME — its own catalog entry, its own dashboard panel (`validate-application-metrics` matches at name granularity, unlike a new `reason` token), and a `metric-coverage` reference. And it needs a sampling cadence, which is a real design decision: making the count readable mid-session requires either a shared atomic plus a per-connection sampler task, or a tick inside the receive loop's `select!` — both are per-connection structure rather than a marginal increment.

  **Why it matters, and do NOT trim this clause as editorial — it is what makes the entry actionable.** Without it MH cannot detect silent ingress loss while it is happening at all. The nearest substitute is watching `forwarded{direction="ingress"}` fail to track the expected publisher frame rate, and **nothing records that expected rate**, so a responder would have to already know it. `docs/runbooks/mh-incident-response.md`'s scenario for `transport_receive_dropped` leads with the inverted habit this creates: **a flat series during an active no-audio incident is NOT evidence that ingress is healthy.**

- [ ] **Datagrams a peer sends BEFORE authenticating are counted by nothing, on all seven pre-auth and failed-auth exit paths — and whether they belong on a media/session-scoped counter at all is an open design question, not an oversight (owner: `media-handler` with `security`; filed 2026-09-08 by @security as SEC-2 at Gate 1 of `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-08-mh-datagram-receive-path-gap/`; trigger: the next pre-auth abuse question, or the next touch of `handle_connection`'s early-return paths)**: story task 26's two ingress tokens are both sampled **after** `jwt_validator.validate_meeting_token` in `crates/mh-service/src/webtransport/connection.rs`. Every path that returns before it therefore records nothing:

  1. `accept_bi` failure; 2. `read_framed_message` error; 3. `MhClientMessage` decode failure; 4. an envelope carrying no oneof variant; 5. **JWT validation failure — the actual abuse case**; 6. `RegistrationOutcome::Timeout`; 7. `RegistrationOutcome::Cancelled`.

  **So the peer that opens a WebTransport session, floods datagrams and never authenticates is exactly as invisible after task 26 as before it.** That claim was made in the wrong direction during that devloop's planning ("makes pre-auth datagram consumption visible") and was **withdrawn**; it must not reappear in the catalog, a dashboard or a runbook, because it would be relied on. The paths are enumerated individually rather than as a category so the work can be sized.

  **The design question is genuinely open and this entry does not answer it.** A counter that fires before there is a session to attribute it to has a semantics problem as well as a placement one: it cannot carry `key_custody` meaningfully, it has no session to bound its cardinality against, and an unauthenticated peer would control its rate. The adjacent constraint is `crates/mh-service/src/webtransport/media_transport.rs`'s ordering obligation — nothing in that module may run before the JWT gate — so any remedy that reads datagrams pre-auth is barred outright, and the tractable shapes are accept-loop-scoped rather than media-scoped. **Filed next to the buffer-inversion entry above deliberately: they are two halves of one mechanism (datagrams MH receives and never reads) and should be found together.**

- [ ] **No named check covers "a value derived from per-frame media crossing a privacy boundary into a log", and the only control on that path today is one newtype (owner: `security` with `observability` for the check's wording, `media-handler` as the affected path; identified 2026-09-08 by @semantic-guard at Gate 1 of `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-08-mh-datagram-receive-path-gap/` in answer to a direct question; trigger: the next `scripts/guards/semantic/checks.md` revision)**: at one 20 ms Opus frame per datagram, a per-connection count of received media frames **is talk duration for that participant**. `crates/mh-service/src/webtransport/connection.rs` logs `connection_id` beside `participant_id`, so such a value in a log field is joinable to a named party.

  **Nothing in the tree catches this class.** `scripts/guards/semantic/checks.md`'s credential-leak check explicitly scopes stable per-participant identifiers as *"linkability, not leakage"* and **out of scope**, so the credential lens deliberately excludes it; and the in-crate macro-deny walker in `crates/mh-service/tests/media_metrics_integration.rs` scans for macros **under** `crates/mh-service/src/media/`, which structurally cannot see a sibling logging a value that came **out** of that directory — the exact "second route" that directory's module docs name.

  **The current control is a type, and that is fine until someone deletes it.** Story task 26's `media::ingress::FramesRead` has no `Display`, no `Debug`, no derive of either, a private field, and **no accessor returning the count** — its only method consumes the value and returns a difference — so a `debug!` on it is a compile error. That is a strong control for one value on one path. It is not a check, it does not generalise, and it depends on the next author reading its rustdoc. **Same tracking shape as the zero-trust-overclaim entry**: recorded as a named-check candidate so the type-system control does not silently become the institutional memory.

- [ ] **`NotifyParticipantConnected` became a BLOCKING PRECONDITION for a media session, and three consequences of that were deferred as ONE decision, not three (owner: **client + operations** for the close code, **observability + media-handler** for the binding-step latency instrument, **operations** for the doc-deletion trigger; filed 2026-09-08 by @operations at Gate 3 of `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-05-sender-id-binding-contract/`, per that record's §7 DoD item 22; trigger: the client media-reconnect work, whichever devloop takes it)**: eight live pointers in shipped runbooks, alert annotations and rustdoc cite this entry by name. It is the target of every "see `docs/TODO.md`" in `docs/runbooks/mh-deployment.md` §"MH's media path now depends on MC's gRPC availability", `docs/runbooks/mh-incident-response.md` §Scenario 15 (Step 2 caution 2, the `user_ambiguous` row, §Known blind spots, §"Do not fix this by shortening the retry budget"), `crates/mh-service/src/config.rs::MC_UNAVAILABLE_CLOSE_JITTER_MAX_MS` and `crates/mh-service/src/webtransport/connection.rs::close_declined_connection`.

  **The three faces are recorded as ONE entry deliberately, and splitting them is the failure mode.** Left as independent-looking items, a future reader tunes the timeout in isolation, and *that is the outage*: shortening the binding deadline before the client can read a retryable close and back off converts a contained MC outage into a synchronized reconnect herd against the service that is already the bottleneck.

  1. **A retryable-vs-terminal close code the client's backoff can read.** MH closes a declined connection by dropping it; it calls `wtransport::Connection::close()` nowhere, so **no reason crosses to the client at all** (@security S8 — this is stronger than a bounded static, not weaker). The client therefore cannot distinguish "MC is down, back off" from "your session is terminally refused", and retries on its own cadence. **If a close code is ever added it stays a bounded CODE, never a string, and never carries an identifier** — a reject arm is the natural place to helpfully include the offending value, and that value is the identity this whole contract exists to protect. Wire-visible change on a surface neither media-handler nor meeting-controller owns; @security agreed at Gate 1 that this is a legitimate cross-owner boundary.

  2. **The ~48s binding deadline, which must NOT be shortened first.** `MC_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` 5s + `MC_RPC_TIMEOUT` 10s per attempt x `MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS` 3, plus 1s/2s backoff (`crates/mh-service/src/grpc/mc_client.rs`). @operations first ruled this should be bounded to ~10s and then **reversed** on the visibility-not-availability-trade correction: with no client-side backoff, the 48s is functioning as an **accidental rate limiter on the reconnect herd**, so cutting it to 10s does not reduce load on a down MC — it multiplies the retry rate roughly 5x. A fast fail is only correct once the client backs off, i.e. only after (1). **The bounded jitter that DID ship (`MC_UNAVAILABLE_CLOSE_JITTER_MAX_MS`, MC-unreachable arm only) is not grounds to close this** — @security's mirror clause: jitter acts on the wave's *phase*, the close code on the *existence of a termination condition*. Different variables; the first does not substitute for the second.

  3. **A latency instrument on the binding step itself — the residual OPS-3b leaves open.** `record_webtransport_handshake_duration` runs **before** the blocking wait, so up to 48s of media-connect stall sits outside `mh_webtransport_handshake_duration_seconds` and `MHWebTransportHandshakeSlow` cannot fire on it: **a 48s stall reads as a healthy sub-second handshake.** The histogram is deliberately NOT moved (@paired-media-handler's ruling) — moving it would make a metric catalogued as "session accept through JWT validation" silently absorb an MC dependency wait, so an MC slowdown would page pointing at MH's accept path, reintroducing in a second place exactly the misdirection `MHHighWebTransportRejections`'s new description was written to fix. **The uncovered case is a binding that SUCCEEDS SLOWLY**: MC degraded but answering, so `started` climbs normally, the decline ratio is flat, the handshake looks healthy, and media connect is 40x slower **with every signal green**. `MHMediaSessionDeclineRate` does not cover it, because nothing declines. A new instrument on the binding step is the only thing that would.

- [ ] **`docs/runbooks/mh-incident-response.md` §Scenario 15 Step 2 carries an absence-as-signal row that MUST BE DELETED once no pre-contract mc-service image can be deployed, and nothing else will prompt the deletion (owner: **operations**; filed 2026-09-08 by @operations at Gate 3 of `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-05-sender-id-binding-contract/`; trigger: the first deploy cycle after which no mc-service image predating `NotifyParticipantConnectedResponse.sender_id` can be rolled out anywhere)**: the row reads *"Series absent or flat ⇒ version skew — the mc-service image predates the `sender_id` field"*, and it is legitimate **today** for a reason the runbook states: a pre-contract MC does not merely fail to set the field, it **does not export `mc_media_sender_binding_responses_total` at all**, which is the only discriminator the wire format does not carry (the field is a bare `uint32`, so absent and zero are the same bytes).

  **Once that image cannot be deployed, absence means something else entirely** — a scrape failure, a relabeling drop, a renamed metric — and the row actively misdirects, sending a responder to rebuild an image that was fine. The runbook already carries the interim caution (confirm MC exports *any* series before reading absence as skew); this entry is the deletion trigger, because **the whole point of the row is that it has no other expiry mechanism.** Recorded separately from the entry above rather than folded into it: different owner, different trigger, and it is a documentation deletion rather than a contract change.

- [ ] **`user_ambiguous` has no operator remedy — the durable fix is a contract change so one authenticated `sub` resolves to a single sender (owner: **meeting-controller + protocol**, with auth-controller + security co-sign under ADR-0024 §6.4; drafted by @implementer and @paired-protocol, filed 2026-09-08 by @operations at Gate 3 of `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-05-sender-id-binding-contract/` as the target of a live runbook pointer; trigger: the next devloop touching the join/allocation identity path or `NotifyParticipantConnected`)**: MC mints a fresh `participant_id` per join and does not bar the same `sub` joining twice (two devices, or a reconnect that produced a second roster entry), so `MeetingActorHandle::get_sender_id_for_user` (`crates/mc-service/src/actors/meeting.rs`) returns `SenderLookup::Ambiguous` and MC answers `0` — fail-closed, correct, and unactionable at 3am **because reconnecting *causes* the condition.** Picking either candidate would bind MH's connection to an ordinal that may belong to the user's *other* participant, so MH would stamp the wrong `sender_id` onto those frames: right half the time and undetectable when wrong.

  **The runbook and dashboard now say "no operator remedy" honestly, but that is a description of a gap, not a fix.** `docs/runbooks/mh-incident-response.md` §Scenario 15 Step 2 is what points here, and it is the reason this entry must exist rather than being folded into a broader identity item: an operator who reaches that row has already been told there is nothing to do, and this is the only place recording that someone is expected to change it.

  **Candidate shapes, neither free:** (a) resolve the ambiguity at the source — a per-connection identity in the meeting token so `NotifyParticipantConnected` names a specific participant rather than a bare `sub` (touches AC mint ordering, `MeetingTokenClaims`, and the proto request shape); or (b) MC carries a deterministic sender per `(sub, connection)` and MH's notification echoes enough to disambiguate. Both are proto/identity-plane changes under ADR-0024 §6.4, so **owner-implemented with protocol + auth-controller + security co-sign, not an inline edit.**

  **Explicitly NOT the surfacing devloop's to fix.** Task 24 owed only the fail-closed `Ambiguous` → `0` arm, which landed and is tested (`one_user_with_two_participants_is_ambiguous_and_fails_closed`, `crates/mc-service/tests/media_coordination_integration.rs`). **Do not close this entry by citing that test** — it proves the refusal is correct, which is the opposite of proving the condition has been eliminated.

Constraints the `media-protocol` codec **cannot** enforce, recorded here so they do not depend on a
task prompt surviving a re-scope. Each is also stated in the crate's rustdoc so it travels with the
wire format; this file is the copy that survives a prompt rewrite. Landed 2026-08-31 with the frame

- [ ] **The `wrap_key_id_mismatch` reject token overclaims a cause the receiver cannot substantiate (owner: protocol; raised by @observability at story task 15 planning, `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-05-sdk-frame-v2-sframe-stack/`; CLOSURE TRIGGER: must precede story task 19)**: the token in `proto/test-vectors/frame-v2.vectors.json` → `reject_reasons` (`layer: crypto`, `drops_frame: false`, `spec_anchor` → the story file) names "the wrapped key is bound to a different key id" as the cause, but **the receiver cannot detect that condition at all**. The wrap's bound key id is nowhere on the wire — the 50-byte block is `kek_generation ‖ 32 wrapped ‖ 16 tag` and the binding exists only as the seal-time AAD — so `wrap_for_different_key_id` (wrap AAD `…0709`, frame kid `…0708`) and `unwrap_reject_wrong_kek` (correctly bound, wrong KEK) produce the **same GCM tag mismatch, one bit, indistinguishable**. The AEAD *is* the only check at the unwrap site and it reports one bit; what actually forks the two outcomes is receiver state (a usable transmit key for the frame's kid already cached → non-fatal, ignore the wrap, play; none → `unwrap_failed`, drop). **The hazard is the misleading NAME, not a wrong spelling (the basis of @security's accepted deferral)**: the token names a condition the receiver cannot detect, and the natural way to make it detectable — widening the KEK-unwrap AAD to carry the wrap's declared key id — **destroys the very binding the row exists to enforce**. The binding IS that the unwrap AAD is the frame's OWN key id, so a widened AAD lets any key id open and the mis-bound wrap would be accepted. So the name invites a "fix" in exactly the wrong direction: whoever tries to make the code substantiate the token either fakes the check or breaks the control. Close by renaming toward the observable, never by making the current name true. **The realistic production firing condition is a KEK-generation skew on a key-bearing frame from a sender whose transmit key the receiver already holds — a different remedy at 3am from "someone is mis-binding wraps."** Deferred from task 15 because renaming is a cross-language contract change spanning the `proto/**` GSA, the generator `crates/media-vector-gen/src/inventory.rs`, the g16 `spec_anchor` (the token must appear verbatim in the story file — `validate-frame-vectors.sh:456` — so the user-story text moves with it), any consumer's error→reject_reason mapping, and `docs/observability/label-taxonomy.md`; and because there is a genuine **design question inside it** — rename toward the observable (shape of "unwrap failed but key already held"), OR fold it into `unwrap_failed` as a receiver-state sub-case, OR add a `receiver_state` discriminant — which warrants its own planning rather than a spelling fix. **The CLOSURE TRIGGER is task 19, not a date**: task 19 lands `dt_client_media_frames_*` and puts this `reason` vocabulary in front of oncall; until then the token is only a vector-row outcome and no operator sees it, but the moment the client media counters ship the overclaim is live in an operator-facing vocabulary. `docs/observability/label-taxonomy.md` already records the current name in the receiver-state-dependent family with a KEK-generation-skew triage pointer written to be replaced when this lands (@observability, task 15). Close by choosing among the three shapes with @observability + @security, then landing the rename (or refold) across all sites above together.  **AMENDED 2026-09-08 (story task 19) — THE CLOSURE TRIGGER HAS FIRED. Still open; owner still protocol.** Task 19 landed `dt_client_media_key_wrap_outcomes_total{outcome}`, on which `wrap_key_id_mismatch` is now an OPERATOR-FACING label value for the first time — it was previously only a vector-row outcome nobody saw. It stays OFF `dt_client_media_frames_dropped_total` (`drops_frame: false`; counting a played frame as a drop would break `received = accepted + sum(drops by reason)`). **RULED (a): NO RENAME IN THIS DEVLOOP** (@observability, after their first ruling's premise was disproved; endorsed by @security and @team-lead). The reversal matters and is recorded because the argument, not the verdict, is what should govern the spin-out: renaming `expected.outcome` while `reject_reason` on the SAME ROW keeps the old spelling produces a vectors row carrying TWO NAMES FOR ONE CONDITION **inside the SSoT** — strictly worse than either endpoint — and renaming both is not a bigger version of that, it IS the spin-out. The principle 'rename at the source, not just the label' survives and had been applied to the wrong node: the source is the vectors file, not the TypeScript union. **PROPOSED TARGET SPELLING for the rename: `unwrap_failed_key_held`**, chosen so the spin-out inherits a name rather than coining a third, and so `unwrap_failed` (drop) and `unwrap_failed_key_held` (kept) read as the two halves of one AEAD failure that `label-taxonomy.md` says they are. **SCOPE ADDITION — a site the entry did not previously name.** This entry's scope list says 'consumer error→`reject_reason` mappings'; that does NOT cover `proto/test-vectors/frame-v2.vectors.json` → `vectors[].expected.outcome`, which is a SECOND, INDEPENDENT pin of the same value on the `wrap_for_different_key_id` row (`:608` as `reject_reason`, `:613` as `expected.outcome`), generated from `crates/media-vector-gen/src/inventory.rs` whose comment states its purpose: declared in the SSoT 'so a codec in a third language cannot get this wrong by omission'. **The rename must move BOTH fields.** Until task 19, NEITHER was read by the TypeScript harness — `:407` hardcoded the outcome literal and every `row.reject_reason` read is guarded on a `kind` this row does not have — so a partial rename would have passed green. Task 19 fixed both: `vectors.conformance.test.ts` now reads `row.expected?.outcome` and asserts `row.reject_reason === row.expected?.outcome` as a FILE-INTERNAL CONSISTENCY check. **Spin-out target: to be scheduled by @team-lead; owner protocol.** **OPERATOR-FACING MITIGATION SHIPPED MEANWHILE**: `docs/observability/metrics/client.md`'s entry for this value LEADS with the observable firing condition (the unwrap failed — a one-bit GCM tag mismatch — AND a usable transmit key was already held) and states the realistic production cause as a KEK-generation skew, so a runbook triages on the condition regardless of the token's name.

- [ ] **MC's `policy_generation` resets to 1 for a surviving meeting after an MC restart (owner: meeting-controller; filed 2026-09-02 at story task 13, `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-02-mc-media-routing-control-plane/`; CLOSURE TRIGGER: must be closed BEFORE the re-assert cadence lands)**: `PolicyGenerations` (`crates/mc-service/src/media_routing/generation.rs`) is an in-process registry. After an MC restart the map is empty, so the meeting's next first-push starts again at 1 — which MH, correctly, ignores as lower than the generation it has already applied. **It is LOUD, not silent**: the echo diverges, MC logs `error!`, `mc_media_policy_pushes_total{outcome="generation_mismatch"}` increments and `mc_media_generation_divergence` goes non-zero (via `abs_diff`, so `applied > sent` reports a real magnitude rather than a healthy-looking 0). **Barely reachable today** — MC pushes once per meeting, at first join, so the hole needs a surviving meeting *and* an MC restart *and* a subsequent push, and there is no subsequent push. **That is exactly why the trigger is the cadence, not a date**: cadence is what re-pushes a surviving meeting, and it turns a barely-reachable hole into one that fires on every MC rolling deploy, for every live meeting. **Fix when acted on**: a durable or handler-seeded generation floor — either persist the last-pushed generation per (meeting, handler), or seed the registry from the `applied_generation` the handler echoes on the first push after a restart. The second is cheaper and needs no new storage, but makes MC trust a value MH asserts; that trade is the decision this entry defers.

- [ ] **`handler_id` is a per-INCARNATION token, so MC's ADR-0036 §8 misroute check is present as an observable but DISARMED as a control (owner: media-handler for the id, global-controller for the refresh path; spin-out slug `2026-09-02-mh-stable-handler-id`; filed 2026-09-02 at story task 13)**: `crates/mh-service/src/config.rs` derives `handler_id` from `HOSTNAME` plus the first 8 chars of a **fresh `Uuid::new_v4()` sampled at process start** whenever `MH_HANDLER_ID` is unset — and it is unset in all three MH manifests, deliberately. MC compares the echoed id against the `mh_id` frozen in its Redis assignment snapshot, which has no TTL (`delete_meeting` is the only thing that clears `meeting:{id}:mh`), so **every ordinary MH pod restart makes the mismatch certain rather than merely possible**. **What MC deliberately does instead of the contract's literal MUST**: `internal.proto` says MC MUST compare and fail loud, but that MUST was written against a premise this tree does not satisfy. Making it fatal would reintroduce ADR-0036 §8's blackhole-through-a-rolling-deploy on every MH restart — clients kicked at the registration timeout for a handler that is working correctly. So for the interim `handler_id_mismatch` is **non-fatal AND demoted to lowest precedence** (`crates/mc-service/src/media_routing/confirm.rs::evaluate`); those are **one decision with one cause and they revert together**. Recorded here so the next reader does not "fix" MC into compliance with a MUST whose premise is false. **The honest cost**: an *impersonating* handler is now indistinguishable from a *restarted* one — neither aborts the push, and neither pages (the alert expression excludes `handler_id_mismatch`). **Definition of done spans TWO halves, named so the easy one is not closed alone**: (1) a stable `MH_HANDLER_ID` — `mh-service` config default plus the three infra manifests plus GC's registry keying; and (2) **GC's assignment-refresh path** — `gc-service/src/services/mc_assignment.rs::assign_meeting_with_mh` re-selects MHs on an existing healthy assignment but **returns early without calling MC's `AssignMeetingWithMh`**, so MC's snapshot goes stale against a *genuinely reassigned* handler. A stable id alone therefore yields a check that looks trustworthy and is not. When both land, restore handler-first ordering and fatality together, and drop the `handler_id_mismatch` exclusion from all three sites that hold it (the alert rule, `docs/observability/metrics/mc-service.md`, `docs/runbooks/mc-deployment.md`).

- [ ] **The declared audio slot id must equal the MH egress stream id, and MC enforces it by REJECTING otherwise (owner: meeting-controller; filed 2026-09-03 at story task 14, `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-03-mc-client-media-signaling/`; CLOSURE TRIGGER: the capability-triggered policy re-push)**: MH stamps each frame's relay-region `stream_id` from the egress slot id in the forwarding policy MC pushed at **first-participant join** — `MAIN_AUDIO_SLOT_ID`, fixed before any client could declare a receive capability. A subscriber validates an arriving `stream_id` against its own declared slots (which is precisely why `ReceiveSlot.slot_id` shares the relay-region value space), so **the loopback works if and only if the client declares that same id**. Task 13 pushes once at join and task 14 adds no re-push, so MC cannot renumber MH's egress mid-connection. **What MC does in the interim**: rejects a declaration that asks for audio in a slot it has no plan for (`mc_media_receive_capability_declarations_total{outcome="slot_id_not_planned"}`), rather than accepting it and reporting `FEWER_SOURCES_THAN_SLOTS` — which would tell the client "there is nobody to show you" while MH actively forwards a source the client will drop, i.e. a healthy-looking session with silent audio. **Zero-audio declarations are exempt**: a subscriber declaring `{}` or video-only is legitimately asking to send without receiving, and MC makes no false claim by accepting it. **Residual cost of that exemption, folded in here rather than filed separately because the same re-push removes it** (noted by @dry-reviewer at Gate 1): MH's frozen policy still carries an egress for that subscriber, so MC keeps forwarding media to a client that declared no slot to receive it into. That is wasted egress, not a false wire claim — the client asked for nothing and is told nothing — which is why it is exempt rather than rejected; but it is real bandwidth, and it scales with send-only participants. **`SLOT_STATE_SOURCE_UNREACHABLE` was considered and rejected as the conveyance**: that state is defined in ADR-0036 §9 visibility-graph terms, and bending a published wire enum to cover an MC-internal provisional constant is semantic drift on a contract other services and stories read. **Retired, not weakened, by either**: (1) a capability-triggered re-push of the forwarding policy — `internal.proto`'s `egress_stream_id` comment already anticipates this ("`slot_id` is client-chosen and is renumbered whenever the subscriber re-declares its receive capability"); or (2) making declared slots an input to `compute_assignment`, which `assignment.rs::MAIN_AUDIO_SLOT_ID`'s rustdoc pre-commits to and which was NOT done in story 1 because at join the participant has declared nothing, so the join-time push would carry an empty policy and the loopback would never forward. **Do NOT relax the equality match into a kind-only match to make it "more flexible"** — that reintroduces the silent-dark-media path the rejection exists to prevent. The per-connection cache of the planned slot id (`webtransport/connection.rs::MediaSignalingContext`) is retired at the same time.

- [ ] **A receive-capability declaration is the PRECONDITION FOR PUBLISHING, not an independent step (owner: client for the SDK consequence, meeting-controller for the MC half; filed 2026-09-03 at story task 14)**: MC emits the send directive when the client declares its receive capability, **not** at join. A client that joins and never declares is never told to send — the connection stays healthy in every other respect, which is exactly what makes the omission hard to notice from the client side. The coupling is deliberate: composing the directive and the slot assignments from **one** meeting-state snapshot is what keeps the directive's target set and the assignments' sources from disagreeing, and it costs one meeting-actor round trip instead of two. Client-side tasks (notably task 19) must send a `ReceiveCapability` before expecting a `SendDirective`, including in the send-only case — a `{}` declaration is valid and still yields a directive.  **AMENDED 2026-09-08 (story task 19) — CLIENT HALF HONOURED; entry stays open for the MC half.** `MeetingSession.startMedia()` sends `ReceiveCapability` and only then waits for a `SendDirective`; `SignalingClient.sendReceiveCapability` accepts an EMPTY slot list, so the send-only case is expressible. The coupling is documented at both call sites rather than only here, because the symptom this entry describes — a healthy connection that is never told to send — is unreadable from the client side without it.

- [ ] **`SLOT_STATE_ZERO_REQUESTED` may be unemittable in principle — an open protocol question, NOT a settled "reachable once video lands" (owner: protocol; filed 2026-09-03 at story task 14)**: the state means *"the subscriber requested zero of this kind"*, but it rides a `StreamAssignment` whose `slot_id` the proto defines as echoing "the `ReceiveSlot.slot_id` the subscriber chose" — and a subscriber who declared a slot **of that kind** did not request zero of it, while a subscriber who declared none chose no id to echo. MC therefore never emits it in story 1: a zero-slot declaration yields an empty `StreamAssignments` list, and fabricating `slot_id = 0` to carry the state would break the echo property on a published contract to satisfy a test. It remains in `mc_media_slot_states_total`'s exhaustive label domain (a wire-vocabulary mirror covers states it does not yet emit). **Recorded as a question so story 2 does not inherit "reachable with video" as established fact**: either the state needs a carrier that is not a declared-slot echo, or it is dead and should be reserved.

- [ ] **MC's directed audio bitrate and MH's datagram-buffer sizing are one relationship in two services with no guard (owner: media-handler and client; filed 2026-09-03 at story task 14; TRIGGER: task 19 fixing the SDK's VBR floor)**: `mh-service` sizes `NOMINAL_AUDIO_FRAME_BYTES` — and therefore the operator-facing "N frames = M ms" datagram-buffer budget it reports — at `SUPPORTED_AUDIO_BITRATE_FLOOR_BPS = 32000`, the **smallest** audio frame it expects, behind a `const _: () = assert!` whose message records that sizing at the ceiling was proposed and reversed. MC directs a **maximum** of `MC_AUDIO_MAX_BITRATE_BPS = 48000`, the top of that band, so MH's sizing stays conservative today. **The residual coupling**: MH's constant is pinned to the *SDK's actual VBR floor*, not to MC's ceiling, so if task 19's Opus encoder lands a floor below 32 kbps, real frames fall under MH's nominal size and the reported latency budget loosens silently — nothing fails and nothing is counted, in the service whose ADR-0036 §1 goal is to prefer loss to unbounded latency. Similarly `MC_AUDIO_FRAME_RATE_HZ = 50` **is** `mh-service`'s `AUDIO_FRAME_DURATION_MS = 20` in the reciprocal unit; moving to §3's 40 ms signature-overhead mitigation is a coordinated change, not a unilateral one. **Not fixed by a shared constant here**: `crates/media-protocol/**` is a Guarded Shared Area and neither owner was on the task-14 devloop. MC validates its two values against the band at config load and the ConfigMap comments cross-reference MH's constants by name with an explicit do-not-unify note; that is a documented inequality, not a checked one. **When acted on**: a shared ConfigMap both services read and validate locally, following this story's Assumption 7 shape.  **AMENDED 2026-09-08 (story task 19) — THE TRIGGER FIRED, AND IT IS NOW THREE ENCODINGS IN THREE SERVICES, NOT TWO. Owner list gains `client`.** `packages/sdk-core/src/config/clientConfig.ts::media.audio.frameDurationMs = 20` is the third encoding of the frame-duration relationship, alongside `crates/mc-service`'s `MC_AUDIO_FRAME_RATE_HZ = 50` (reciprocal unit) and `crates/mh-service`'s `AUDIO_FRAME_DURATION_MS = 20`. It carries an `ANCHOR (DRY):` comment naming both siblings by file and identifier. **No shared home is reachable and that was checked rather than assumed**: a browser SDK cannot import a Rust `const` and cannot read the ConfigMap this entry proposes as its own remedy, so that remedy does not cover the client at all; and `proto/dark_tower/signaling/v1/signaling.proto` states explicitly that audio ignores `EncodingParameters.frame_rate`, so there is no wire carrier either. A third encoding is the honest option. **This entry's CLOSURE TRIGGER ('task 19 fixing the SDK's VBR floor') is no longer a future event — it fired, and the answer was that the SDK has no configurable VBR floor to fix.** See the amendment on the `NOMINAL_AUDIO_BITRATE_BPS` entry for the measured consequence (~970 ms against a documented 640 ms, one-directional, MH's compile-time pin accidentally correct). **The bitrate half is now single-sourced on the wire**, which this entry did not anticipate: `EncodingParameters.max_bitrate_bps` on the send directive is the SSoT and configures the encoder whenever MC supplies it; the SDK constant is a `DEFAULT_` fallback for its absence only. A client-side acceptance band was proposed and REJECTED (@dry-reviewer): `MC_AUDIO_MAX_BITRATE_BPS` is an operator-settable env var that MC validates at config LOAD and refuses to start without satisfying, so a mirrored client validator would hard-fail every fielded SDK the first time an operator legitimately raised the ceiling — the mirrored-validator pattern already barred once in this tree.

(b) `mc-deployment.md`'s existing `mc_media_policy_pushes_total{outcome!~"match|handler_id_mismatch"}` gate looks identical but is a **temporary** carve-out with a revert trigger; these two are permanent and correct. **Do not let a future cleanup fold the three together.**
  **Exclude the MC-internal-defect tokens** (`unknown_stream_number`, `transport_mode_unspecified`) from any page: they are fail-closed diagnostics to file against `meeting-controller`, not operator-actionable. - [ ] **Layer 5's Rust lint omits `--all-features`, so feature-gated crates are NEVER linted by the pipeline — the pre-commit hook is strictly STRONGER than the gate it mirrors (owner: infrastructure for the Layer-5 wrapper machinery; affected consumer: test; trigger: Gate-3 follow-up, needs its own budget; surfaced 2026-09-03 at Gate 2 of `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-02-mc-media-routing-control-plane/`)**: `scripts/lang/rust/lint.sh:7` runs `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `.githooks/pre-commit:24` runs `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`. `crates/env-tests` declares **no default features** (`Cargo.toml:9-15` — `smoke`, `flows`, `observability`, `resilience`, all opt-in), so every test target in that crate is invisible to Layer 5 and has, as far as this gap goes, never been linted. **Demonstrated, not hypothesised**: task 13's `26_mh_quic.rs` edit shipped an `empty_line_after_doc_comments` error through a green Layer 5 and a green `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` run by the implementer, and was caught only by the local pre-commit hook. **Why that ordering is the defect**: the authority gate is weaker than a developer's local hook, so a lint in feature-gated code either blocks at the very last step after passing every gate that was supposed to catch it, or — in CI, where no git hook runs — reaches the branch unlinted. A gate that is weaker than the thing it authorises is the same shape as this devloop's Lesson 4: a control that exists but does not evaluate what everyone assumes it evaluates. **Not fixed here, deliberately**: adding `--all-features` to `lint.sh` will surface whatever lint backlog exists across every feature-gated target in the workspace, which is task-sized and needs its own budget rather than being absorbed into an unrelated diff. **When acted on**: align the two commands, and consider whether the hook or the pipeline should be the single source — two encodings of "the lint command" is itself the drift. Also check the sibling wrappers (`fmt.sh`, `test.sh`) for the same omission before assuming it is clippy-only.

- [ ] **MC's confirm classifier has no arm for MH's `RejectedInvalid`, and two of MH's reject reasons are resource ceilings MC cannot satisfy by construction (owner: protocol for the contract half + meeting-controller; trigger: real multi-handler placement or larger meetings — the scaling story; raised by @media-handler at Gate 3 of `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-02-mc-media-routing-control-plane/`, explicitly NOT a defect against task 13)**: `PolicyPushOutcome` has five arms mirroring `internal.proto`'s vocabulary, none of which is "MH refused the policy as structurally invalid". That is correct today — MC satisfies every *structural* `MeetingPolicy::from_request` rejection by construction (pinned by `mh_client.rs::built_request_satisfies_every_mh_rejection_by_construction`). But two `from_request` arms, `TooManyEgressStreams` and `TooManyCandidateSources`, are **MH-side resource ceilings** read from `PolicyLimits`, which MC does not know and cannot satisfy by construction. Unreachable at loopback and N=2. **The failure mode when it becomes reachable**: MH rejects with `RejectedInvalid` and installs nothing, so `applied_generation` stays at the prior generation, so MC's classifier reads `no_applied_generation` or `generation_mismatch` — both `Retryable` — and MC burns its whole retry budget re-sending a policy that can never be accepted, before failing loud as "retries exhausted". **Slow-but-loud, not silent**, which is why this is a scaling-story concern and not a task-13 defect. **Fix when acted on**: the proto must surface the apply-reject *reason* to MC so the classifier can distinguish "MH will never accept this" from "MH failed to apply this time" — a protocol-owned contract change, hence the first owner. Do not work around it MC-side by mirroring `PolicyLimits`: that is the mirrored-validator @dry-reviewer barred at Gate 1, and it would drift silently the first time MH retunes a limit.

The three MH-owned *operator-facing* sites (metrics catalog, dashboard panel description, runbook Scenario 13) were retired at task 13 and are already accurate.


- [ ] **`crates/dt-guard/**` has no owner derivable from the path** — the general fix is still open; owner: infrastructure. **Interim LANDED 2026-09-02** (story task 10, `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-02-mc-kek-identity-sender-id/`): CLAUDE.md's Specialists section now carries a `crates/dt-guard/**` note splitting ownership by **what the edit changes** — guard *policy content* (what a vocabulary term, allow- or deny-list entry, threshold, or required-shape rule means) belongs to the specialist owning that policy, e.g. `observability` + `security` for `common/pii_vocabulary.rs`; guard *machinery* (crate/module layout, clap dispatch, matcher implementations, and the shape of the constructs policy is expressed in) is infrastructure. For any list construct, membership is content; evaluation order and construct shape are machinery. An edit that *changes* a machinery construct is both; one that merely *satisfies* an existing construct is content — the test is what the edit changes, not what the author had to read to get it right. **CORRECTION to this entry's original wording, by the seat that wrote it**: it cited "the Lead's ADR-0034 ruling" as establishing infrastructure as owner. ADR-0034 lines 263-294 are a dated Wave/Day construction schedule under `## Implementation Status` with every row `❌ Pending` — a build assignment, not an ownership registry, and reading it as one is a category error (raised by @observability 2026-09-02, confirmed against the file by @infrastructure and by the Lead). The Lead's devloop ruling stands on its own authority; the ADR does not corroborate it. The tables do not support the opposite reading either — line 285's Owner column is `infrastructure` with observability/security in a `(pair: …)` parenthetical, and line 270 shows the table *moves* the Owner column when ownership genuinely differs (`src/common/path_safety.rs` → security) — so read as the schedule they are, they say nothing about standing ownership for anyone. **Still do NOT fix by adding a key to `scripts/guards/simple/cross-boundary-ownership.yaml`** — that file is a GSA mirror, `gsa_sync.rs:196-205` rejects stray keys, and populating all five mirrors would wrongly declare dt-guard a Guarded Shared Area (it meets no ADR-0024 §6.4 criterion). **What remains task-sized**: `cross_boundary_scope.rs` reads owners from `main.md` tables, not from any manifest, so there is still no general non-GSA path→specialist map — the CLAUDE.md note is prose a human must read, not something a guard enforces, and it covers one crate rather than the class. Needs a micro-debate on whether a second, non-GSA ownership manifest should exist. *(Original wording by @infrastructure, filed by protocol; corrected and interim-closed by @infrastructure at story task 10, after the recurrence this entry predicted arrived as OPS-11. The one-directional derivation still exists — `docs/specialist-knowledge/infrastructure/INDEX.md:30` lists `crates/dt-guard/` under Code Locations — but it is discoverable from infrastructure, not from the path.)*


- [ ] **MC has NO join rate limit and NO `jti` replay check, which is what makes the `sender_id` exhaustion threat above reachable (owner: meeting-controller + security; trigger: before MC is exposed to untrusted meeting tokens outside a devloop cluster, or the first `MCSenderIdSpaceExhausted` firing that triage attributes to a driven cause rather than a reconnect loop; filed at story task 10, deferral tested against the burden by @security)**: neither control exists today — `rate_limit` appears nowhere in `crates/mc-service/src`, and `jti` appears in `auth/mod.rs` only in test fixtures. A single valid meeting token therefore permits unbounded joins until it expires, and because `sender_id`s are never recycled (see the entry titled *"KEK rotation, the KEK-epoch `sender_id` reset..."*, consequence (a)) that converts one authenticated participant into a permanent, unrecoverable denial of one meeting's media path. **Explicitly NOT covered by anything shipped** — task 10 landed *detection* (`MCSenderIdSpaceExhausted`, `> 0` on a 15m increase, plus the Scenario 8 root cause 11 triage guidance naming the deliberate cause first). Do not read the alert as mitigation: it fires *after* the meeting is already permanently broken. **Why it was deferred rather than taken at task 10, tested against fix-now vs fix-later** (@security, ratified by @team-lead): a configured join bound needs a config knob nobody has chosen, and under OPS-4 that drags in a ConfigMap key, startup validation and a `mc-deployment.md` §Configuration Reference row — the exact shape @team-lead refused for `supported_codecs` at the same gate; and `jti` replay needs cross-instance shared state with a TTL keyed on token expiry, i.e. Redis plus ADR-0003/0007 semantics. Different surfaces, different threats, both open.

- [ ] **KEK rotation, the KEK-epoch `sender_id` reset, and reconnect KEK re-issue are all deferred (owner: meeting-controller; filed at story task 10)**: task 10 shipped the meeting KEK, its `u16` generation counter, and the monotonic non-recycling `sender_id` allocator with a fail-closed exhaustion reject — but **no rotation of any kind**. Three consequences, recorded so none is mistaken for an oversight. **(a) The `sender_id` namespace has no reclaim path, and exhaustion is REACHABLE ON PURPOSE — this is a threat, not a capacity limitation.** Exhaustion is terminal for a meeting: `mc-incident-response.md` Scenario 8 root cause 11 says the only remediation is to end and restart it, because the KEK-epoch reset that would reclaim the namespace ships with rotation. **The adversarial reading, recorded because the entry previously read as a scaling note** (raised by @security at Gate 3 of story task 10): every join consumes one never-recycled id; MC has **no join rate limit and no `jti` replay check** (see the entry titled *"MC has NO join rate limit and NO `jti` replay check"*); and the browser reconnect path is unwired, so every reconnect is a fresh join. One valid meeting token therefore permits unbounded joins until it expires. Cost to an authenticated participant is **one meeting token**; effect is **permanent denial of the media path for every participant in that meeting**; and the only remedy is destroying the meeting. Detection landed with task 10 (`MCSenderIdSpaceExhausted`); the *prevention* did not. **(b) ADR-0036 §4's leave-triggered debounced rotation is absent**, so a departed participant retains a KEK that unwraps every subsequent transmit key for the meeting's remaining life — §4 bounds a leaver by the rotation window `W` and by nothing else, and today `W` is unbounded. **(c) Reconnect KEK re-issue is satisfied only vacuously.** §4's rotation table requires MC to re-issue the current KEK on reconnect; `ReconnectResult` carries no KEK field and there is no wire message for one. That is *correct today only because the KEK never rotates* — the client already holds the only KEK there is. **When rotation lands, `ReconnectResult` must carry the KEK and generation, or a reconnecting participant will hold a stale KEK and silently fail to unwrap.** Do not read (c) as already handled.

Without the check a relay gains 16 free bits per frame and can place a frame in a slot the subscriber never assigned. Applies to **both** audio (datagram) and video (stream) receive, since the relay region is present in every frame regardless of transport. Target: SDK receive path, story tasks 15/19. The caller must bound **both** buffered bytes per stream (`media_protocol::frame::MAX_FRAME_BYTES`) and time-to-completion, and **count the give-up**. The codec sees one buffer and has no notion of time or stream count, so it cannot enforce this. Two callers, not one: MH's video forward path (task 16, @media-handler has accepted ownership) **and the SDK's video-stream receive reader** (@client's catch — video is carried on unidirectional QUIC streams per §1, so the SDK is itself a `decode_stream_frame` caller and owes the identical bound). Original text: **A task-8 vector that contradicts a recorded ruling is a defect to escalate, not a precedence question** (raised by @security after @client had adopted the opposite rule during Gate-2 coordination). The cross-language vectors are the SSoT for Rust↔TypeScript agreement and rightly beat *prose* — but they are **generated from the Rust encoder and then frozen**, so a vector that disagrees with a recorded ruling means the Rust codec implemented that ruling wrongly and the freeze captured the error. Conforming the TypeScript codec to such a vector makes both implementations **consistently wrong with the drift guard green**, which is strictly worse than a divergence, because a divergence is loud and this is silent. The rule: vectors beat prose; a vector contradicting a ruling is escalated to protocol + security and is **not built against** in the meantime. This bites hardest on the **extension-grammar** rows: unlike the AAD-span rows, which are anchored externally against the SFrame specification, the TLV registry is ours alone — nothing outside this repository says what type `0x01` means or that its accepted value set is `0..=100` — so those vectors can prove internal consistency only, never correctness. Target: story tasks 8 and 15. Delete when task 8 lands the drift guard together with this escalation rule.

  **CONSEQUENCE (a) DISCHARGED 2026-09-05 (story task 16) — STRUCTURALLY, NOT WITH A LABEL. Consequence (b) remains open, so this entry stays open.** The requirement was that a `truncated` from `rewrite_relay_region` must not be collapsed with a datagram-decode `truncated` and mis-attributed to the sender. Task 16 removes the ambiguity at the source rather than adding a dimension to describe it: **MH calls `decode_datagram` on ingress AND `rewrite_relay_region` for the rewrite**, so every codec token MH emits comes from `decode_datagram` and is by construction a *sender-side* condition, while a rewrite failure on an **already-decoded** frame is not a sender fault at all — it is an MH bug, and it carries its own MH-local token `relay_rewrite_failed`, which should read zero forever. **No `entry_point` label was added**, so §11's dimension bar is not tested against and the counter's cardinality does not grow. The two parses are not two parsers: both entry points invoke the same `parse_layout`, so `codec.rs`'s "two parsers diverge on exactly the malformed ones an attacker constructs" invariant is intact — and the second parse is the *price* of the derived-offset guarantee, since the single-parse alternative is decode-then-pass-the-offset, which is the cached-offset hazard with a shorter cache lifetime.

  **WHY THIS WAS RE-FILED RATHER THAN DONE AT TASK #12, and why the re-file is the dangerous moment for this entry.** Verified at task #12 that this entry is **not stale**: all four keys have **zero** hits across `infra/`, so task 11 landed only the code half — exactly the "two of three" this entry already credits it with, leaving "no manifest", which is this entry. It was re-filed anyway because it is a four-file edit entirely inside `infra/services/mh-service/`, owned by @infrastructure, who was not on task #12's review panel; under ADR-0024 §6.3 that needs the owner confirming at Gate 1 **and** Gate 3, which could not be obtained, and landing owner-less manifest edits is a worse outcome than a re-file. **The detection gap travels with the re-file and is the whole reason this entry exists**: `dt-guard env-config` rule 1 tracks only `MissingEnvVar` reads, so a defaulted key is invisible to it, and rule 3's orphan check fires only on keys that *are* in a ConfigMap — **both halves are silent by construction**, so nothing mechanical will ever surface this. It needs a human to schedule it; no test will fail, no guard will red, no alert will fire. **The allocation is owed before story close.** **Framing that must survive into the ConfigMap comments**: all four are **resource-exhaustion guards, never capacity figures**. None is advertised to GC, none participates in placement. `MH_MAX_TOTAL_EGRESS_EDGES` in particular must carry the `MH_MAX_CONNECTIONS` framing. **CORRECTED at Gate 3 of `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-02-mh-register-meeting-policy-apply/` by the seat that supplied the original wording (@operations), with @security and @observability concurring.** This paragraph previously said the default is sized far above expected peak *on purpose*, so that hitting it means a bug, a leak or a hostile MC rather than growth, and that a bound reachable by legitimate growth would produce a rotating victim under §8's jittered cadence. **Every clause of that is false**, and it must not propagate into a ConfigMap comment: it IS reachable by ordinary growth, the victim does not rotate, and the condition does not clear on the next tick. The correct framing — unreclaimable floor, remedy is reclamation and not a larger ceiling — is in the dedicated reclamation entry below and in `crates/mh-service/src/config.rs::DEFAULT_MAX_TOTAL_EGRESS_EDGES`; **cite those, do not restate them here.**

- [ ] **MH bounds forwarding policy per-meeting and in aggregate, but does NOT bound the number of registered meetings (owner: media-handler + operations, as a capacity-model decision; filed 2026-09-02 at Gate 1 of `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-02-mh-register-meeting-policy-apply/` by @operations at @security's request; trigger: the R-22 egress-budget work at story 2)**: `crates/mh-service/src/session/mod.rs` inserts into `registered_meetings` with no count cap. Story task 11 added a per-meeting egress bound and an aggregate egress-edge bound, and **neither closes this**, because `internal.proto::RegisterMeetingRequest.egress_streams` makes an **empty** egress set legal and meaningful ("this handler forwards nothing for this meeting"): a caller can register arbitrarily many near-free meetings and the aggregate-edge bound never fires.
  **Deliberately not fixed at task 11, and the reason matters more than the gap.** The caller is an authenticated MC holding `service.write.mh`, so this is a capacity-model question rather than an access-control one. More decisively, choosing MH's meeting ceiling is the *same decision* that settles R-22's deferred egress-budget chain — bolting a number on here would pre-empt that with a value nobody chose, which is precisely why arming the already-drifted `MH_MAX_STREAMS` was rejected in the same review. **Filed so it is on the record as a known gap rather than as something four reviewers each assumed someone else had checked.**

- [ ] **MH never reclaims an ended meeting's routing entry, so `MH_MAX_TOTAL_EGRESS_EDGES` is consumed by a permanently-unreclaimable floor — an availability defect, not deferred hygiene (owner: protocol + meeting-controller + media-handler, because the fix needs a teardown signal on `MediaHandlerService`, which is a `proto/**` Guarded Shared Area edit; trigger: story 2's R-22 egress-budget work, the same trigger as the meeting-count entry above; raised as OPS-1 by @operations and S-1 by @security independently at Gate 3 of `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-02-mh-register-meeting-policy-apply/`)**: `RoutingSnapshot::with_policy` is the only mutator of the meeting map and it only inserts; `SessionState.registered_meetings` is likewise insert-only; and `MediaHandlerService` has exactly one RPC, so MH is given no meeting-ended signal it could act on (`NotifyMeetingEnded` is MC→GC, `proto/dark_tower/internal/v1/internal.proto`).
  **What ratchets is a FLOOR, not the total** — the correction matters, because the remedy follows from it. `projected_total_edges` subtracts the meeting's own installed edges before adding its new ones, so a **live** meeting shrinking 5 edges to 4 computes `B - 5 + 4`, installs, and drops the handler total. Headroom does come back — only from meetings still alive to shrink. What nothing releases is the edges held by meetings that have **ended**. That floor rises at the pod's meeting-completion rate while the reclaimable headroom above it shrinks asymptotically.
  **The failure is gradual, asymmetric and self-concealing.** `apply_failed` from this cause is **intermittent before it is permanent**: it clears when some unrelated meeting happens to shrink and returns when none does, uncorrelated with anything the affected meeting did, worsening over uptime — which is the shape that gets misfiled as a transient and closed. What fails is every registration that would add a **net** edge, which is broader than "new meetings": an existing, healthy meeting **cannot admit a new participant**, because that needs an extra egress edge, therefore a higher generation with more edges, therefore the cap arm. Already-installed meetings re-assert at an unchanged generation, take the `==` arm *before* the cap is evaluated, and keep reporting `outcome="applied"` at the full cadence. `RegisterMeeting` still answers `accepted: true` and GC keeps placing meetings on the pod, because these bounds are resource guards and are deliberately not advertised as capacity. So the user-visible symptom is *"some participants can't hear anything in a meeting that's otherwise working, and it's the ones who joined most recently"* — and those users blame their own network and drop, so the affected population removes itself from the signal. That is ADR-0036 §8's black-hole-reporting-healthy failure arriving through a resource bound rather than through a generation echo.
  **This inverts the veto recorded in the same review.** `MH_MAX_STREAMS` was vetoed at Gate 1 partly because a cap on the total across all meetings makes one meeting's re-assert fail on unrelated meetings' load, with a rotating victim under §8's jittered cadence. A fresh knob was then approved with a condition (sized far above peak, so reaching it means a bug or a hostile MC and never growth) that assumed a quantity which comes back down. It does not, for ended meetings. Rotating is the mild form — each victim recovers on the next tick; this is the severe one.
  **The remedy is a reclamation path, NOT a larger ceiling.** Raising `MH_MAX_TOTAL_EGRESS_EDGES` buys time proportional to the **meeting-completion rate**, not to the ceiling, because the ceiling is consumed by finished meetings at whatever rate meetings finish — independent of concurrent load. Doubling the number doubles time-to-onset and changes nothing else. Interim operational remedy is a pod restart, which **is** recoverable: healthy meetings re-assert on the next §8 tick and reinstall at their current generation (`docs/runbooks/mh-incident-response.md` Scenario 13).
  **Distinct from the meeting-count entry above, which is its inverse** — that one records that arbitrarily many *empty* meetings never trip the aggregate bound; this one records that non-empty meetings trip it after they are gone. Both would still be true if the other were fixed. **Paired with the missing early-warning signal** filed as the saturation-gauge entry under §Observability Debt: this entry is the missing reclamation, that one is the missing gauge, and they are two halves of one cliff.

The ratchet is not**: as of story task 11, `handle_config_apply` installs `policy.generation` and thereafter refuses everything strictly below it, **with no downward path within the process**. So a single `RegisterMeeting` from any fleet peer holding a valid `service.write.mh` token, carrying `policy_generation: u64::MAX` for a meeting it does not own, lands every subsequent legitimate re-assert from the owning MC on `rejected_stale` — permanently, while `accepted: true` and `mh_grpc_requests_total{status="success"}` both stay green.   **Detection landed at task 11; enforcement did not, deliberately.** `handle_register_meeting` now WARNs with `previous_mc_id` / `new_mc_id` when the owning `mc_id` changes, instead of the previous unconditional INFO that made an ownership change and an ordinary re-assert the same log line.   **The property task 13 inherits, and the reason this is filed rather than remembered**: generation monotonicity has **no recovery path within a process**. Once a bogus high generation is installed, nothing short of a pod restart lets the owning MC re-take the meeting — and task 13 is the change that makes generations load-bearing, so it is the point at which the exposure becomes real rather than theoretical. **Options when acted on**: bind the meeting to its registering `mc_id` and reject a different one (simplest, breaks MC failover); accept a different `mc_id` but reset the installed generation on ownership change (preserves failover, weakens the ratchet); or carry meeting ownership in the meeting token itself so MH can verify it rather than trust it (strongest, largest change, and the only one that closes the authorization gap rather than working around it).

But with the re-assert cadence deferred out of task 13, MC pushes **once** per meeting, so a meeting wedged *after* its one push produces no further push to diverge on and stays silent until the cadence story lands. Detection is therefore real but first-push-only; it is not preventive, and it is not continuous.

Each is a rule the proto **cannot** enforce and whose violation is **green under every test the story that introduces it can construct** — @test's "equivalent mutants under the reachable input space". The mitigation ladder, strongest first, is: (1) structural impossibility beats a test; (2) where structure cannot carry it, pin the killing test *with its distinguishing input named*, because "add a test" without the input is not a pin. There is no function accepting a `SenderId` alone, so the wrong index is a *missing function* rather than a remembered rule. `SenderId` is a fresh `NonZeroU16` newtype (never `UserId`, and never `common::types::StreamId` — a second trap @dry-reviewer caught: `u32`, subscriber-chosen, pre-ADR-0036 semantics), with its width derived from `media_protocol::frame::KEY_ID_SENDER_ID_BITS` by `const` assertion so no `65535` literal exists in MH. - [ ] **MH's egress-drop counter is structurally blind to quinn's own silent drop-oldest one layer below it; the far-end hop-sequence gap counter is the compensating control, and that relationship must be stated at BOTH metric definitions (raised by @dry-reviewer and @paired-media-handler, verified and ruled by @observability at Gate 1 of `docs/devloop-outputs/2026-09-01-mh-transport-seam/`; owner: observability for the catalog wording, media-handler for story task 16's counter, operations for story task 21's egress-exhaustion runbook)**. Three facts, none visible from wtransport's own API: **(i)** `quinn_proto::SendDatagramError` (`quinn-proto-0.11.17/src/connection/datagrams.rs`) carries a fourth variant, `Blocked(Bytes)` — precisely the payload-returning back-pressure shape MH wants — but `quinn::Connection::send_datagram` (`quinn-0.11.11/src/connection.rs`) calls `datagrams().send(data, true)` with `drop` hardcoded `true` and handles the blocked arm as `unreachable!()`, so on the API wtransport actually calls (`wtransport-0.7.2/src/driver/mod.rs`) transport back-pressure is unreachable **by construction**, not merely unsignalled. The egress loop must therefore derive back-pressure from its own queue depth and never from a transport error return — there is no transport error to key on. **(ii)** quinn's eviction path pops the oldest datagram and emits only a `trace!`, incrementing no `ConnectionStats` field; and because an evicted datagram was never transmitted, it never enters quinn's *lost-packet* statistics either. Its only native signal is a log line gated on trace level — which ADR-0036 §11 rules out in terms ("A log level is not an acceptable gate"). **(iii)** Consequently, under congestion severe enough to saturate quinn's buffer but not MH's, **MH's egress-overflow counter reads flat at exactly the moment loss is worst**: "no loss" and "loss we cannot see" are indistinguishable on that signal. ADR-0036 §1 already decided the remedy — size `datagram_send_buffer_size` so "the application-level egress queue bound must trip **before** the transport ceiling", expressed in frames of audio — and story task 12 makes it a startup validation.
